question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
enjoy
explain_ko: enjoy는 '즐기다'라는 뜻이다. forget(잊다)·borrow(빌리다)·repair(고치다)와 혼동하지 않는다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Can I _____ your pencil for a minute?
explain_ko: 상대의 물건을 잠깐 쓰겠다고 할 때는 borrow(빌리다)를 쓴다. lend는 반대로 내가 빌려주는 것이라 문맥에 맞지 않는다.

question:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
friendly and caring toward other people
explain_ko: 다른 사람에게 친절하고 배려한다는 뜻은 kind(친절한)이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
Mina felt very [happy] when she passed the test.
explain_ko: happy(기쁜)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 glad(기쁜)이다. upset·tired·bored는 다른 감정이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
forget
explain_ko: forget은 '잊다'라는 뜻이며 remember(기억하다)와 반대되는 말이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Please be _____ when you cross the busy street.
explain_ko: 위험한 상황에서 조심하라는 뜻이므로 careful(조심하는)이 알맞다.

question:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
able to cause harm or injury
explain_ko: 해를 끼칠 수 있다는 뜻은 dangerous(위험한)이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The new bakery became very [popular] among students.
explain_ko: popular(인기 있는)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 well-liked(사랑받는)이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
collect
explain_ko: collect는 '모으다'라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Every Saturday, the soccer team members _____ at the park to practice.
explain_ko: 한 장소에 모인다는 뜻이므로 gather(모이다)가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
known to you very well because you have seen or heard it before
explain_ko: 잘 알고 있는이라는 뜻은 familiar(익숙한)이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The coach will [introduce] the new player to the team.
explain_ko: introduce(소개하다)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 present(소개하다, 보여주다)이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
discover
explain_ko: discover는 '발견하다'라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
The little monkey was _____ about the strange box and opened it.
explain_ko: 신기한 것에 호기심을 보였다는 문맥이므로 curious(호기심 많은)가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
to form a picture of something in your mind
explain_ko: 마음속으로 그려본다는 뜻은 imagine(상상하다)이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
We saw [several] birds flying over the lake.
explain_ko: several(몇몇의)과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 some(몇몇의)이다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
My brother _____ soccer after school every day.
explain_ko: 주어가 3인칭 단수(My brother)이고 습관이므로 plays. play는 주어와 수가 안 맞고, is play는 be동사와 일반동사를 함께 쓴 오류.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: They are in the library now.
explain_ko: 3인칭 단수 주어 She의 부정은 doesn't like가 되어야 함. 나머지는 be동사·일반동사 현재형을 바르게 씀.

question:
다음 문장을 부정문으로 바꿀 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Mr. Brown teaches science.
→ Mr. Brown _____ science.
explain_ko: 3인칭 단수 일반동사 부정은 doesn't + 동사원형. doesn't teaches는 원형이 아니고, isn't teach는 be동사로 부정한 오류.

question:
다음 우리말과 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
너의 여동생은 키가 크니?
explain_ko: 형용사(tall)가 보어인 be동사 문장의 의문문은 Is + 주어 + 보어? Does는 일반동사가 없어 틀리고, 나머지는 어순 오류.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
Look! The children _____ in the pool.
explain_ko: Look!으로 지금 일어나는 일이므로 현재진행형, 복수 주어라 are swimming. swim은 m을 겹쳐 swimming으로 써야 하고, is는 수 불일치.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Is he running in the park?
explain_ko: know처럼 상태·인지를 나타내는 동사는 진행형으로 쓰지 않으므로 I know her name.이 맞음. 나머지는 진행형 긍정·부정·의문문을 바르게 씀.

question:
다음 문장을 현재진행형으로 바꿀 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Mina writes a letter.
→ Mina _____ a letter now.
explain_ko: 주어가 단수이므로 is + writing(e를 빼고 -ing). writeing은 철자 오류, are는 수 불일치, writing만 쓰면 be동사가 빠짐.

question:
다음 우리말과 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
너는 지금 무엇을 먹고 있니?
explain_ko: 의문사 진행형 의문문은 의문사 + be동사 + 주어 + -ing. What you are는 주어·동사를 바꾸지 않았고, do는 진행형과 함께 쓸 수 없음.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
We _____ a museum in Gyeongju last summer.
explain_ko: last summer는 과거를 나타내므로 visited. visitted는 t를 겹치지 않는 동사의 철자 오류, visit·are visiting은 시제가 맞지 않음.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: She buyed a new pencil case yesterday.
They didn't go out last night.
I met Jake at the bus stop.
explain_ko: buy의 과거형은 불규칙 변화 bought. 나머지는 be동사 과거(was), 과거 부정(didn't go), 불규칙 과거(met)를 바르게 씀.

question:
다음 문장을 의문문으로 바꿀 때 빈칸에 차례로 알맞은 것은?
Your cat slept on the bed.
→ _____ your cat _____ on the bed?
explain_ko: 일반동사 과거 의문문은 Did + 주어 + 동사원형. Did 뒤에 slept를 쓰면 과거가 겹치고, Does는 현재, Was는 be동사라 틀림.

question:
다음 우리말과 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
그들은 어제 학교에 있지 않았다.
choices: They were at not school yesterday.
They did not at school yesterday.
They not were at school yesterday.
They were not at school yesterday.
explain_ko: be동사 과거 부정은 were 뒤에 not. did not은 뒤에 일반동사가 없어 틀리고, 나머지는 not의 위치가 잘못됨.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
Kevin is going to _____ his grandparents this weekend.
explain_ko: be going to 뒤에는 동사원형이 옴. visits·visited·visiting은 모두 원형이 아님.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Will you help me with this box?
We won't be late for the concert.
I am going to join the art club.
explain_ko: will 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 It will rain tomorrow. 나머지는 be going to, will 의문문, won't be를 바르게 씀.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
I will clean my room tomorrow.
= I _____ clean my room tomorrow.
explain_ko: will은 be going to + 동사원형으로 바꿀 수 있음. am going은 to가 빠졌고, going to는 be동사가 빠졌으며, will going to는 두 표현을 섞은 오류.

question:
다음 우리말과 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
그녀는 다음 달에 춤 수업을 들을 거니?
choices: Does she going to take a dance class next month?
Is going she to take a dance class next month?
Is she going to take a dance class next month?
Is she going take to a dance class next month?
explain_ko: be going to 의문문은 Be동사 + 주어 + going to + 동사원형. Does는 be going to와 함께 쓸 수 없고, 나머지는 going·to의 위치가 틀림.

passage:
Summer Art Camp for Kids
Do you like drawing and painting? Join our Summer Art Camp! The camp is for students from ten to thirteen years old. It runs from July 22 to July 26. Classes start at 10 a.m. and end at 1 p.m. You can learn painting, clay art, and paper crafts. The fee is 50 dollars for five days. Please bring an apron and a water bottle. We give you all the other art supplies. To sign up, visit the front desk of the community center.
question: 다음 안내문을 읽고 알 수 없는 것은?
explain_ko: 나이(10~13세), 시간(10시~1시), 참가비(50달러)는 나오지만 강사 이름은 나오지 않는다.

passage:
Sunny Bakery Grand Opening
Sunny Bakery opens on Main Street this Saturday! We bake fresh bread every morning. On opening day, all cakes are 20 percent off. The first fifty visitors get a free cookie. Do you have a reusable shopping bag? Bring it, and you get a free muffin, too. We open at 8 a.m. and close at 9 p.m. We are closed on Mondays. Come and enjoy our sweet bread with your family!
question: 광고에 따르면, 무료 머핀을 받으려면 어떻게 해야 하는가?
choices: 다시 쓸 수 있는 장바구니를 가져간다
explain_ko: reusable shopping bag 을 가져오면 머핀을 준다. 처음 50명에게 주는 것은 쿠키이고, 케이크는 할인 대상이다.

passage:
Green Park Swimming Pool
Green Park Pool is open from June to August. It opens at 9 a.m. and closes at 6 p.m. Children under seven must swim with an adult. A ticket is 3 dollars for students and 5 dollars for adults. Please wear a swimming cap in the pool. Do not run near the pool. Do not bring food into the pool area. You can buy snacks at the café next to the pool.
question: 안내문에 따르면, 학생 두 명과 어른 한 명의 입장료는 모두 얼마인가?
explain_ko: 학생 3달러×2 + 어른 5달러 = 11달러. 학생·어른 요금을 바꿔 계산하면 13달러가 된다.

passage:
Join the Robot Club!
Are you interested in robots? The Robot Club is looking for new members. We meet every Wednesday after school in Room 205. In the club, we build small robots and learn simple coding. You don't need any experience. Our teacher, Mr. Brown, helps new members. At the end of the year, we take part in a robot contest. Do you want to join? Write your name on the list outside Room 205 by Friday.
question: Robot Club 에 가입하고 싶은 학생이 해야 할 일은?
explain_ko: 마지막 문장에서 금요일까지 205호 밖 명단에 이름을 쓰라고 한다. 경험이 필요 없으므로 로봇을 가져갈 필요도 없다.

passage: Last Sunday, Emma went to the park with her little brother, Leo. They wanted to fly a kite. The wind was strong, so the kite went very high. Suddenly, the string broke. The kite flew away and landed in a tall tree. Leo started to cry. Then an old man came with a long stick. He got the kite down for them. Emma and Leo said, "Thank you!" and smiled.
question: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 바람이 약해서 연이 높이 날지 못했다
한 노인이 긴 막대로 연을 내려 주었다
Emma 는 언니와 함께 공원에 갔다
explain_ko: an old man came with a long stick. He got the kite down 과 일치. 함께 간 사람은 남동생이고, 바람이 강했으며, 연은 나무에 걸렸다.

passage: Jiho visits his grandmother every Saturday. She lives in a small house near the sea. This Saturday, they made kimchi pancakes together. Jiho cut the green onions, and Grandma mixed the flour and water. The first pancake was too thick, so it didn't cook well. The second one was perfect. They ate the pancakes with rice. Jiho said, "Grandma, your pancakes are the best!"
question: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 첫 번째 전은 아주 잘 익었다
explain_ko: 첫 번째 전은 너무 두꺼워서 잘 익지 않았다(didn't cook well). 나머지는 글과 일치한다.

passage: Today is Sora's first day at a new school. She feels a little shy. In the classroom, she sits next to a girl named Kate. Kate says hello and shows Sora her pencil case. It has a cat on it. Sora has the same pencil case! The two girls laugh together. At lunch, they eat together and talk about their favorite animals. Sora is not shy anymore.
question: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Kate 는 오늘 새 학교에 처음 왔다
Sora 와 Kate 는 똑같은 필통을 가지고 있다
Kate 의 필통에는 개 그림이 있다
explain_ko: Sora has the same pencil case! 와 일치. 전학 온 사람은 Sora 이고, 둘은 점심을 같이 먹으며, 필통에는 고양이가 있다.

passage: Ben loves soccer, but he is not a fast runner. On Friday, his team had a big game. Ben's job was to stop the ball in front of the goal. The other team kicked the ball at the goal many times. Ben stopped it every time. In the last minute, his friend Max scored a goal. Ben's team won the game one to zero. After the game, the coach said, "Great job, Ben!"
question: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Ben 이 경기 마지막에 골을 넣었다
explain_ko: 마지막에 골을 넣은 사람은 친구 Max 이다. Ben 은 골문 앞에서 공을 막는 역할이었다.

passage: Camels live in hot and dry deserts. They can walk for many days without water. How can they do that? A camel has a hump on its back. The hump stores fat, not water. The camel uses this fat for energy. Camels also have long eyelashes. The eyelashes keep sand out of their eyes. Their wide feet help them walk on soft sand.
question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: how camels live well in the desert
why camels drink a lot of water
what camels eat in the desert
explain_ko: 혹·긴 속눈썹·넓은 발 등 낙타가 사막에서 잘 사는 방법을 설명하는 글이다. 혹에는 물이 아니라 지방이 있다고 했으므로 물을 많이 마신다는 선택지는 틀리다.

passage: Sleep is very important for students. When you sleep, your body grows and rests. Your brain also saves the things you learned that day. Students need about nine hours of sleep every night. Without enough sleep, you can feel tired and angry. It is also hard to focus in class. So put your phone away and go to bed early tonight. Your body and brain will thank you.
question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: why students feel angry at school
how to use your phone at night
why sleep is important for students
the best time to study at home
explain_ko: 첫 문장부터 잠이 학생에게 왜 중요한지(성장·기억·집중)를 설명한다. 휴대 전화·화는 일부 내용일 뿐이다.

passage: Plastic bottles are everywhere. People use them once and throw them away. But plastic does not go away easily. It stays in the ground for hundreds of years. Some plastic goes into the sea and hurts fish and birds. We can help. First, carry your own water bottle. Second, put plastic in the recycling bin. Small actions can make the earth cleaner.
question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: problems with plastic and ways to help
fish and birds in the sea
explain_ko: 플라스틱이 오래 남아 동물을 해치는 문제와, 개인 물병·분리수거라는 해결 방법을 함께 말한다. 바다 동물은 예시일 뿐이다.

passage: Bicycles today are light and fast. But the first bicycles were very different. About two hundred years ago, a bicycle had no pedals. People sat on it and pushed the ground with their feet. Later, people put pedals on the front wheel. The front wheel was very big, so riding was dangerous. Finally, bicycles got two wheels of the same size. That is the bicycle we ride today.
question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the best places to ride a bicycle
how to ride a bicycle safely
explain_ko: 페달 없는 자전거 → 앞바퀴에 페달 → 같은 크기 두 바퀴로 이어지는 자전거의 변화를 설명한다.

passage:
Dear Ms. Wilson,
My name is Hana Lee. I am a student at Riverside Middle School. I often use the school library after class. I really like the science books there. But the library doesn't have any books about space. Many of my friends are interested in space, too. Could you please buy some books about planets and stars? We will read them carefully. Thank you for reading my letter.
Best wishes,
Hana Lee
question: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 우주에 관한 책을 사 달라고 요청하려고
빌린 책을 늦게 돌려준 것을 사과하려고
explain_ko: Could you please buy some books about planets and stars? 에 목적이 드러난다.

passage:
Hi Aunt Julie,
Thank you so much for the birthday present. I got it yesterday. The blue backpack is really nice! It has many pockets, so I can put my books and pencils in it. I took it to school today. My friends said it looks cool. I will use it every day. I hope you can visit us this summer.
Love,
Ethan
question: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 첫 문장부터 생일 선물(파란 가방)에 대한 감사를 전한다. 여름 방문 이야기는 끝인사일 뿐이다.

passage:
Dear students,
I have some news about our field trip to the zoo. The trip was on Friday, May 10. But the weather report says it will rain a lot that day. So we are moving the trip to Tuesday, May 14. The bus leaves school at 9 a.m. like before. Please tell your parents about the new date. See you all on Tuesday!
Mr. Parker
question: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 현장 체험 학습 날짜가 바뀐 것을 알리려고
버스 출발 시간이 바뀐 것을 알리려고
비 오는 날 준비물을 알려 주려고
explain_ko: 비 때문에 금요일에서 화요일로 날짜를 옮긴다는 안내다. 버스 시간은 전과 같다(like before).

passage:
Dear Mr. Harris,
Hello! I am Noah, and I live next door in the yellow house. Yesterday afternoon, I played baseball with my brother in our yard. I hit the ball very hard, and it flew over the fence. I think it is in your garden now. I am very sorry about that. Can I come and get my ball back this weekend? I will be careful next time.
Thank you,
Noah
question: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 정원에 넘어간 공을 찾으러 가도 되는지 부탁하려고
explain_ko: Can I come and get my ball back this weekend? 가 핵심이다. 울타리 수리나 야구 제안은 나오지 않는다.

passage:
M: Hi, Mina. Is that a new bag?
W: Yes, Tom. My aunt gave it to me for my birthday.
M: It's nice. Is it a backpack?
W: No, it's a shoulder bag. It has a big star on the front.
M: A star? Cool. What color is it?
W: The bag is yellow, and the star is white.
M: It looks great with your shoes.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 새 가방으로 가장 알맞은 그림을 고르시오.
choices: 노란 별이 그려진 흰색 어깨 가방
흰 별이 그려진 노란색 어깨 가방
흰 하트가 그려진 노란색 어깨 가방
explain_ko: 배낭이 아니라 어깨 가방(shoulder bag)이고, 가방은 노란색·별은 흰색이다. 색을 바꾼 것과 배낭을 고르면 틀린다.

passage:
M: Mom, where is Coco? I can't find her anywhere.
W: Did you look under your bed?
M: Yes, but she isn't there. She isn't on the sofa, either.
W: Hmm. Oh, look! She's sleeping in the basket next to the window.
M: Oh, there she is. She looks so warm in the sun.
W: Let's not wake her up.
question: 대화를 듣고, 고양이가 있는 곳으로 가장 알맞은 그림을 고르시오.
choices: 창문 앞 바닥에서 햇볕을 쬐는 고양이
창문 옆 바구니 안에서 자는 고양이
explain_ko: She's sleeping in the basket next to the window가 결정적이다. 침대 밑·소파는 없다고 했고, 창문 앞 바닥은 바구니가 아니다.

passage: W: Good morning. Here is the weather for this weekend. Today is Saturday, and it will be sunny and warm all day. But tomorrow, Sunday, will be different. In the morning, it will be cloudy. In the afternoon, it will rain a lot. So don't forget your umbrella tomorrow. Have a nice weekend.
question: 방송을 듣고, 일요일 오후의 날씨로 가장 알맞은 그림을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 일요일 오후에는 비가 많이 온다(it will rain a lot). 맑음은 토요일, 흐림은 일요일 오전이다.

passage:
W: Jake, is your brother in this photo?
M: Yes. He's the boy next to the tree.
W: The boy with the soccer ball?
M: No, that's his friend, Sam. My brother is wearing glasses, and he's holding a guitar.
W: Oh, I see him. He looks very kind.
M: He is. He plays the guitar for me every night.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 형으로 가장 알맞은 그림을 고르시오.
choices: 나무 옆에서 안경을 쓰고 기타를 든 남자아이
나무 옆에서 모자를 쓰고 기타를 든 남자아이
나무 옆에서 안경을 쓰고 축구공을 든 남자아이
explain_ko: 형은 안경을 쓰고 기타를 들고 있다. 축구공을 든 아이는 형의 친구 Sam이고, 모자는 나오지 않는다.

passage:
M: Excuse me. I'm looking for some books about space.
W: Science books are on the second floor.
M: Thank you. Can I borrow three books today?
W: Yes, you can. Just show me your student card.
M: Here it is. How long can I keep the books?
W: For two weeks. Please bring them back on time.
question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 대화하는 장소로 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 책을 빌리고(borrow) 2주 뒤에 돌려주라는 말로 도서관임을 알 수 있다. 서점은 책을 사는 곳이고, science는 책 종류일 뿐이다.

passage:
W: Hello. Please sit down here. How do you want your hair today?
M: I want it short, please. It's too hot these days.
W: Okay. What about the front?
M: Just cut a little. I don't like hair in my eyes.
W: Sure. It will take about twenty minutes.
M: Great. Thank you.
question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람의 관계로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 머리를 어떻게 자를지 묻고(How do you want your hair) 짧게 잘라 달라고 하므로 미용사와 손님이다. 앉으라는 말만 듣고 의사-환자를 고르면 틀린다.

passage:
W: Dad, look! The baby elephant is drinking water.
M: It's so cute. Let's go and see the lions next.
W: Okay. Where are they?
M: The map says they're near the gift shop.
W: Can we give them some food?
M: No, we can't. Look at the sign. It says, do not feed the animals.
question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 대화하는 장소로 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 아기 코끼리와 사자를 보러 다니고 동물에게 먹이를 주지 말라는 표지판이 있으므로 동물원이다. 기념품 가게는 사자 위치를 말할 때 나온 곳일 뿐이다.

passage:
M: Good afternoon. Where are you going?
W: To City Hospital, please.
M: Okay. Please put on your seat belt.
W: Sure. How long will it take?
M: About fifteen minutes. The roads are not busy now.
W: Good. Please stop at the front door of the hospital.
question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람의 관계로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 목적지를 묻고 안전벨트를 매라고 한 뒤 병원 정문에 세워 달라고 하므로 택시 기사와 승객이다. hospital, seat belt 낱말만 듣고 의사나 경찰관을 고르면 틀린다.

passage:
M: Emma, do you want to go to the movies on Saturday?
W: Sure. What time does the movie start?
M: It starts at two o'clock.
W: Then let's meet at one thirty in front of the theater.
M: One thirty? I have a piano lesson until one. How about one forty-five?
W: Okay. See you then.
question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 만나기로 한 시각을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 여자가 1시 30분을 제안했지만 남자가 피아노 수업 때문에 1시 45분으로 바꾸고 여자가 동의했다. 2시는 영화 시작 시각이다.

passage:
W: Hi, Ben. How many members are in your dance club?
M: There are twelve members now.
W: Wow. Can I join, too? I love dancing.
M: Sure. Two students from my class are joining next week, too.
W: Great. So with me, we will have fifteen members.
M: That's right. Welcome to the club!
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 가입하면 댄스 동아리 회원은 모두 몇 명이 되는지 고르시오.
explain_ko: 지금 12명에 다음 주 2명, 그리고 여자까지 더해 15명이다. 12명은 지금 회원 수, 14명은 여자를 빼고 센 수다.

passage:
M: Excuse me. What time does the museum close today?
W: It usually closes at six o'clock. But today is Friday, so it closes at eight.
M: Great. Then I have time to see the dinosaur room.
W: Yes, you do. But the gift shop closes at seven.
M: Okay. Thank you for your help.
question: 대화를 듣고, 오늘 박물관이 문을 닫는 시각을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 평소엔 6시지만 오늘은 금요일이라 8시에 닫는다. 7시는 기념품 가게가 닫는 시각이다.

passage:
W: Excuse me. Which bus goes to Green Park?
M: You can take bus number fifty-two or bus number thirty-five.
W: Which one comes soon?
M: Bus fifty-two comes every twenty minutes. But bus thirty-five comes every five minutes.
W: Then I'll take bus thirty-five. Thank you.
M: You're welcome.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 탈 버스의 번호를 고르시오.
explain_ko: 35번 버스가 5분마다 와서 여자는 35번을 타겠다고 했다. 52번은 20분마다 오는 다른 버스다.

passage:
W: Hi, Minho. What are you doing?
M: I'm making a card for my mom. Tomorrow is her birthday.
W: Wow, it's really pretty. Did you draw these flowers?
M: Yes, I did. I also want to buy a cake for her.
W: That's sweet. Where will you buy it?
M: At the bakery near my house. Can you come with me after school?
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 이어질 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Sure. I can go with you.
explain_ko: 방과 후 빵집에 같이 가 줄 수 있는지 물었으므로 같이 가겠다는 답이 알맞다. 생일은 남자의 엄마 생일이고, 꽃을 그린 사람은 남자다.

passage:
M: Excuse me. Is this seat free?
W: Sorry, my friend is sitting here. She is buying some water now.
M: Oh, okay. I have a heavy bag. Are there any other free seats on this train?
W: Yes. I think there is one by the window over there.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 이어질 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Thanks. I'll go and sit there.
explain_ko: 창가에 빈자리가 있다고 알려 주었으므로 고맙다며 그리로 가겠다는 답이 알맞다. 이 자리는 비어 있지 않다고 했고, 물 이야기는 친구에 관한 말이다.

passage:
M: Sally, you look worried. What's wrong?
W: I can't find my phone. I had it in the classroom.
M: Did you check your bag?
W: Yes, I did. It's not there.
M: What color is it?
W: It's pink, and it has a cat sticker on the back.
M: Oh, I saw a pink phone on the teacher's desk.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 이어질 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Really? I'll go and get it now.
No, it's not in my bag.
explain_ko: 선생님 책상에서 분홍색 휴대 전화를 봤다고 했으므로 지금 가서 찾겠다는 답이 알맞다. 가방에 없다는 말은 앞에서 이미 한 대답이다.

passage:
W: Jason, what do you usually do on weekends?
M: I usually ride my bike at the river park. What about you?
W: I often go hiking with my dad.
M: Sounds fun. Where do you go?
W: We go to Blue Mountain. Do you want to come with us this Sunday?
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 이어질 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: I ride my bike every weekend.
No, I don't have a bike.
Sure. What time should I meet you?
Yes, I went there last Sunday.
explain_ko: 이번 일요일에 등산을 같이 가자고 했으므로 좋다며 만날 시각을 묻는 답이 알맞다. 자전거 이야기는 앞의 주말 활동 답이고, 지난 일요일은 시제가 맞지 않는다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
achieve
explain_ko: achieve는 '이루다, 달성하다'라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Archaeologists found tools used by _____ people thousands of years ago.
explain_ko: 수천 년 전이라는 문맥이므로 ancient(고대의)가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
the way a person or animal acts
explain_ko: 행동하는 방식이라는 뜻은 behavior(행동)이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The young king spoke in a [confident] voice before the soldiers.
explain_ko: confident(자신감 있는)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 sure(확신하는)이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
emotion
explain_ko: emotion은 '감정'이라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Planting more trees can help protect the _____ from pollution.
explain_ko: 오염으로부터 지켜야 하는 대상은 environment(환경)이다.

question:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
the ability to remember things
explain_ko: 기억하는 능력이라는 뜻은 memory(기억력)이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
We bought fresh vegetables from a [local] farm near our town.
explain_ko: local(지역의)과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 nearby(근처의)이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
experience
explain_ko: experience는 '경험'이라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
During the trip, we tried _____ kinds of food from different countries.
explain_ko: 여러 나라의 음식을 다양하게 먹었다는 뜻이므로 various(다양한)가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
a chance to do something you want to do
explain_ko: 하고 싶은 것을 할 수 있는 기회라는 뜻은 opportunity(기회)이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
She put a lot of [effort] into planning the trip.
explain_ko: effort(노력)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 hard work(수고, 노력)이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
improve
explain_ko: improve는 '개선하다, 향상시키다'라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
This new device can _____ your eyes from bright screen light.
explain_ko: 눈을 보호한다는 문맥이므로 protect(보호하다)가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
to make or create something
explain_ko: 무언가를 만들어 낸다는 뜻은 produce(생산하다)이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The engineer finally found a [solution] to the problem.
explain_ko: solution(해결책)과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 answer(해답)이다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
You look very tired. You _____ go to bed early tonight.
explain_ko: 피곤해 보이는 사람에게 일찍 자라고 충고하므로 should(~하는 게 좋겠다). must not·may not은 금지, can't는 불가능이라 흐름에 맞지 않음.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: You must wear a helmet here.
explain_ko: 조동사는 주어가 3인칭 단수여도 -s를 붙이지 않으므로 He can play. 나머지는 조동사 + 동사원형, 의문문, 부정문을 바르게 씀.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Jiho can swim fast.
= Jiho _____ swim fast.
explain_ko: 능력의 can은 be able to로 바꿀 수 있고 주어가 단수라 is. is able은 to가 빠졌고, able to는 be동사가 빠졌으며, are는 수 불일치.

question:
다음 우리말과 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
너는 도서관에서 떠들면 안 된다.
choices: You must make not noise in the library.
You not must make noise in the library.
You must not make noise in the library.
Must not you make noise in the library.
explain_ko: 조동사 부정은 조동사 바로 뒤에 not을 써서 must not + 동사원형. 나머지는 not의 위치가 틀리거나 평서문 어순이 아님.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
Mount Everest is the _____ mountain in the world.
explain_ko: the ~ in the world는 최상급이므로 highest. high는 짧은 단어라 most high가 아니라 -est를 붙이고, higher는 비교급.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Sara is the tallest girl in her class.
My room is as big as yours.
This bag is more heavier than that one.
Math is more difficult than English for me.
explain_ko: heavier가 이미 비교급이므로 more를 함께 쓸 수 없음(heavier than). 나머지는 원급 as~as, 최상급, more + 긴 형용사 비교급을 바르게 씀.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
The blue pen is cheaper than the red pen.
= The red pen is _____ the blue pen.
explain_ko: 파란 펜이 더 싸면 빨간 펜이 더 비쌈 → more expensive than. cheaper than은 뜻이 반대, as cheap as는 같다는 뜻, most는 최상급이라 than과 못 씀.

question:
다음 우리말과 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
치타는 세상에서 가장 빠른 동물이다.
choices: The cheetah the fastest is animal in the world.
The cheetah is the fastest animal in the world.
The cheetah is animal the fastest in the world.
The cheetah is fastest the animal in the world.
explain_ko: 최상급은 the + 최상급 + 명사 순서. 나머지는 the의 위치나 형용사·명사의 순서가 잘못됨.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
My dream is _____ a famous chef.
explain_ko: be동사 뒤 보어 자리에 '~하는 것'을 나타내는 to부정사(to + 동사원형). to becoming은 to 뒤에 원형이 아니고, become·becomes는 동사가 겹침.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Tom hopes to win the race.
explain_ko: want는 목적어로 to부정사를 쓰므로 wants to be. 나머지는 decide·hope의 목적어, 주어 자리 to부정사를 바르게 씀.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
To ride a bike in the rain is dangerous.
= _____ is dangerous to ride a bike in the rain.
explain_ko: 주어 자리의 긴 to부정사는 뒤로 보내고 가주어 It을 씀. That·This·There는 가주어로 쓰지 않음.

question:
다음 우리말과 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
그의 계획은 매일 아침 달리는 것이다.
choices: His plan is run to every morning.
His plan to run is every morning.
To his plan is run every morning.
His plan is to run every morning.
explain_ko: 주어(His plan) + is + 보어(to run) + 때(every morning). 나머지는 to와 run의 위치가 틀리거나 보어 자리가 잘못됨.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
Emma enjoys _____ photos of birds.
explain_ko: enjoy는 목적어로 동명사만 쓰므로 taking. to take는 enjoy 뒤에 쓸 수 없고, take·takes는 동사가 겹침.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Swimming is good for your health.
He finished to write his report.
explain_ko: finish는 동명사를 목적어로 쓰므로 finished writing. 나머지는 주어·보어·목적어 자리 동명사를 바르게 씀.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
To keep a diary is a good habit.
= _____ a diary is a good habit.
explain_ko: 주어 자리 to부정사는 동명사 Keeping으로 바꿀 수 있음. Keep·Keeps·Kept는 동사 형태라 주어가 될 수 없음.

question:
다음 우리말과 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
우리는 공원을 청소하는 것을 끝냈다.
explain_ko: finish + 동명사 + 목적어 순서로 finished cleaning the park. the cleaning park는 '청소하는 공원'이 되어 뜻이 다르고, 나머지는 어순 오류.

passage:
How Do Students at Hillside Middle School Get to School?
Walking 42% / Bus 30% / Car 18% / Bike 10%
Last month, we asked 200 students at our school this question. Walking was the most popular way. Taking the bus came second. Only ten percent of students rode a bike. Many of them said the bike road near our school was too narrow. Students who came by car said their parents drove them on the way to work. Next year, the city will build a wider bike road, so the number of bike riders may grow.
question: 다음 도표와 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 내년에 더 넓은 자전거 도로가 생길 예정이다
explain_ko: 걷는 학생(42%)이 가장 많고 버스(30%)는 두 번째이다.

passage:
Books Borrowed from the School Library
March 320 / April 410 / May 380 / June 250
This chart shows the number of books students borrowed from the library for four months. In March, students borrowed 320 books. The number went up in April and was the highest of the four months. In May, it went down a little to 380. In June, students borrowed only 250 books. The librarian thinks students were busy with their exams in June. She is planning a reading event in July to bring more students to the library.
question: 다음 도표와 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
explain_ko: 4월(410권)이 가장 많다. 가장 적은 달은 6월이고, 5월은 4월보다 줄었으며, 시험은 6월이다.

passage:
School Flea Market
Do you have things you don't use anymore? Bring them to our school flea market!
Date: Saturday, October 12
Time: 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.
Place: School gym
- You can sell toys, books, and clothes. Food is not allowed.
- Buyers can bring their own bags.
- Each seller gets one table for free.
- Please sign up at the student office by October 5.
- Half of the money you earn will go to the children's hospital.
Come and find some great treasures with your friends!
question: 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 번 돈의 절반은 어린이 병원에 간다
explain_ko: Food is not allowed. 라고 했으므로 음식은 팔 수 없다.

passage:
Star Night at the Science Museum
Look up at the night sky with our experts!
When: Every Friday in November, 7 p.m. to 9 p.m.
Who: Families with children eight years old or older
Price: $10 for adults, $6 for children
What to do:
- Look at the moon and planets through a big telescope
- Make your own star map
Notes:
- If it is cloudy, we will show a movie about space instead.
- Only 30 people can join each night, so book online early.
question: 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 일곱 살 어린이도 참가할 수 있다
흐린 날에는 우주에 관한 영화를 보여 준다
하루에 참가할 수 있는 인원에 제한이 없다
explain_ko: If it is cloudy, we will show a movie about space instead. 와 일치. 8세 이상만, 어린이 6달러, 하루 30명 제한이다.

passage: Today was the day of the English speech contest. Minji stood behind the stage and held her paper tightly. Her hands were shaking, and her heart was beating fast. "What if I forget my words?" she thought. Then her name was called. She walked to the center of the stage and started to speak. At first, her voice was small. But soon she saw her friends smiling at her. She finished her speech without a mistake. Everyone clapped loudly. Minji let out a deep breath and smiled.
question: 다음 글에 드러난 Minji 의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 손이 떨리고 가슴이 뛰다가(nervous), 실수 없이 마치고 숨을 내쉬며 웃는다(relieved).

passage: Owen looked out the window and sighed. It was raining hard. His family planned to go on a picnic in the park today. He made sandwiches with his mom last night. "Now we can't go," he said and sat down on the sofa. A few minutes later, his dad called him into the living room. There was a big blanket on the floor with the sandwiches, fruit, and juice on it. "Welcome to our indoor picnic!" said Dad. Owen jumped up and laughed. "This is the best picnic ever!"
question: 다음 글에 드러난 Owen 의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 비 때문에 소풍을 못 가 한숨 쉬다가(disappointed), 거실 소풍에 뛰며 웃는다(delighted).

passage: Lucas practiced the piano every day for six months. Some days his fingers hurt, and he wanted to stop. But he never gave up. Last night, he played a difficult song at the school concert. He didn't make a single mistake. When the song ended, the audience stood up and clapped for a long time. His piano teacher hugged him and said, "You did it, Lucas!" On the way home, Lucas held his little trophy and kept looking at it. "All my hard work was worth it," he thought.
question: 다음 글에 드러난 Lucas 의 심경으로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 오랜 연습 끝에 실수 없이 연주하고 트로피를 계속 바라보며 노력이 보람 있었다고 생각하므로 뿌듯하다(proud).

passage: Grace couldn't wait for Saturday. Her favorite writer was coming to the bookstore downtown to sign books. Grace packed her copy of the writer's new novel and left home early. On the bus, she practiced what to say to the writer. But when she arrived, there was a long line outside the store. A staff member came out and said, "Sorry, everyone. The writer is sick today, so the event is canceled." Grace looked down at her book. She walked slowly back to the bus stop.
question: 다음 글에 드러난 Grace 의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 토요일을 손꼽아 기다리며 할 말을 연습하다가(excited), 행사 취소 소식에 책을 내려다보며 천천히 걷는다(disappointed).

passage: Many people are afraid of bees because they sting. But bees are very important to us. When bees fly from flower to flower, they carry pollen. This helps plants make fruit and seeds. Bees also make honey, but their biggest gift is helping plants grow. Without bees, we would have fewer apples, strawberries, and many other foods. Sadly, the number of bees is getting smaller around the world. Some farmers use chemicals that hurt them, and bees are losing their homes. We need to protect bees for our future.
question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the importance of bees and the need to protect them
the best fruits for our health
explain_ko: 벌이 꽃가루를 옮겨 열매를 맺게 하므로 중요하고, 줄어드는 벌을 지켜야 한다는 내용이다.

passage: Did you know that laughing is good for your body? When you laugh, your heart beats faster and you breathe more deeply. This is a little like doing light exercise. Laughing also helps your body relax, so you feel less stressed. Some scientists say that people who laugh often get sick less. Laughing with friends makes your friendships stronger, too. Even a smile can make you feel a little better. So watch a funny show or share a joke with someone today. Your body will thank you.
question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How to Tell a Funny Joke
Laughter: Good Medicine for Your Body
explain_ko: 웃음이 심장·스트레스·건강·우정에 좋다는 글이므로 '몸에 좋은 약, 웃음'이 알맞다.

passage: Many students get pocket money from their parents. Some spend it all in a few days. Others save some of it every week. Saving money is a good habit to start early. First, write down how much you spend. Then you can see where your money goes. Next, set a goal, like buying a new game or a gift for your mom. Put a little money in a piggy bank each week. Soon you will reach your goal and learn to manage money well.
question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: how students can save their pocket money
explain_ko: 쓴 돈 적기 → 목표 세우기 → 저금통에 넣기 등 용돈을 모으는 방법을 설명한다.

passage: People around the world greet each other in different ways. In Korea, people often bow when they meet someone. In many Western countries, people shake hands. In some parts of France, friends kiss each other on the cheeks. In Thailand, people put their hands together and bow a little. In New Zealand, the Maori people sometimes touch noses. These greetings look different, but they all have the same meaning. They say, "I'm happy to see you." So before you visit another country, learn how people say hello there.
question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: The Oldest Greeting in the World
How to Bow Politely in Korea
explain_ko: 나라마다 인사 방법은 다르지만 뜻은 같다는 내용이다. 한국의 절은 예시 하나일 뿐이다.

passage: Last weekend, Chris cleaned his room. Under his bed, he found an old wooden box. He opened the box and took out a small red toy car. [It] had only three wheels, and the paint was coming off. His grandfather gave him the car on his fifth birthday. Chris remembered racing the car around the kitchen every day. He smiled and put the car on his desk next to his books. "I'll keep this forever," he said to himself. Then he closed the empty box and put it back under the bed.
question: 글의 [It] 이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 바퀴가 세 개뿐이고 페인트가 벗겨진 것은 바로 앞 문장의 장난감 자동차이다.

passage: Emperor penguins live in the coldest place on Earth. In winter, the mother penguin lays one egg and goes to the sea to find food. The father penguin stays and keeps the egg warm on his feet. During the long winter, the fathers stand close together in a big group. [They] take turns moving to the center of the group, where it is warmer. The fathers don't eat anything for more than two months. When the mothers come back, they bring food for the babies.
question: 글의 [They] 가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 바로 앞 문장에서 무리 지어 서 있는 아빠 펭귄들이 번갈아 가운데로 들어간다. 엄마 펭귄은 바다에 가 있다.

passage: Amy and her older sister, Jane, went to the market to buy food for dinner. Amy had the shopping list, so (a) she read it out loud. Jane put carrots and onions into the basket. Then Amy saw a little puppy near the fruit store. (b) She ran to it and petted its soft head. "Amy, come back! We need to finish shopping," Jane called. (c) She sounded a little angry because it was getting late. Amy said goodbye to the puppy. On the way home, (d) she kept talking about the cute dog, and Jane just laughed.
question: (a)~(d) 가 가리키는 대상 중 나머지 셋과 다른 것은?
explain_ko: (c) 는 Amy 를 부른 언니 Jane 이고, 나머지는 모두 Amy 이다.

passage: Mrs. Taylor had a lot of old jeans in her closet. They were too small for her children now. She didn't want to throw them away. One day, she had an idea. She cut the jeans into pieces and sewed the pieces together. In a few hours, she made three pretty bags. The bags were blue and had big pockets on the front. Her children loved [them] and took them to school every day. Soon, their friends asked Mrs. Taylor to make bags for them, too. She is now thinking of starting a small bag shop.
question: 글의 [them] 이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 아이들이 좋아해서 매일 학교에 가져간 것은 엄마가 만든 가방 세 개이다.

passage:
W: Dad, are you going to the supermarket now?
M: Yes. We need some milk and eggs. Do you need anything?
W: I have to make cookies for the school festival tomorrow. Could you buy some butter for me?
M: Sure. How much do you need?
W: Just one box. I also need chocolate chips, but I can buy them at the store near my school.
M: Okay. I'll get the butter.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 남자에게 부탁한 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: Could you buy some butter for me?로 버터를 부탁했다. 우유와 달걀은 아빠가 원래 사려던 것이고, 초콜릿 칩은 여자가 직접 사겠다고 했다.

passage:
M: Wow, this science project looks hard.
W: Don't worry. We can finish it together. First, we need some pictures of the planets.
M: I can find them on the Internet.
W: Good. And I'll write the report.
M: What about the poster?
W: Let's make it tomorrow in the art room.
M: Okay. Then I'll start looking for the pictures right now.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 대화 직후에 할 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 남자는 지금 바로 행성 사진을 찾겠다고 했다(right now). 보고서는 여자가 쓰고, 포스터는 내일 만든다.

passage:
M: Hi, Kate. Are you going home now?
W: Yes. Why?
M: I have a soccer game after school, so I can't walk my dog today. Could you walk him for me? You live next door.
W: Sure. I love your dog. When should I take him out?
M: At about five. And please give him some water after the walk.
W: No problem.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 여자에게 부탁한 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: Could you walk him for me?로 개 산책을 부탁했다. 축구 경기는 남자가 산책을 못 하는 까닭이고, 먹이를 사 달라는 말은 없다.

passage:
W: Mr. Brown, I'd like to join the school newspaper club.
M: Great! We need a new writer. Do you like writing?
W: Yes. I write in my diary every day.
M: Good. First, fill out this form and bring it to me on Monday. Also, please write a short story about your school life.
W: Okay. I'll write the story tonight.
M: Thanks. I can't wait to read it.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 오늘 밤에 할 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 여자는 학교생활 이야기를 오늘 밤에 쓰겠다고 했다(I'll write the story tonight). 신청서는 월요일에 낸다.

passage:
M: Jenny, when is the school sports day?
W: It was on May tenth, but the teacher changed the date.
M: Really? Why?
W: It will rain a lot that week. So it's on May seventeenth now.
M: Good. I have new running shoes, and I want to wear them that day.
W: Me too. Let's practice together this weekend.
question: 대화를 듣고, 체육대회 날짜를 고르시오.
explain_ko: 원래 5월 10일이었지만 비 때문에 5월 17일로 바뀌었다. 5월 10일은 바뀌기 전 날짜다.

passage:
W: Hey, Chris. Let's study for the math test together on Saturday.
M: Good idea. Where do you want to meet? How about the city library?
W: It's closed this Saturday. What about the coffee shop next to the bank?
M: It's too noisy there. Let's meet at my house. My mom said it's okay.
W: Great. I'll bring some snacks.
question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 만나기로 한 장소를 고르시오.
explain_ko: 도서관은 토요일에 닫고 커피숍은 시끄러워서 남자의 집에서 만나기로 했다.

passage:
W: Tony, my family is going to Hawaii this summer.
M: Wow, when are you leaving?
W: We're leaving on July twenty-fifth, and we're coming back on July twenty-ninth.
M: That sounds great. What are you going to do there?
W: We're going to swim at the beach and ride horses.
M: Cool. Don't forget to take lots of pictures.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 여행을 떠나는 날짜를 고르시오.
explain_ko: 7월 25일에 떠나서 7월 29일에 돌아온다. 7월 29일은 돌아오는 날이다.

passage: M: Hello, everyone. This is your music teacher, Mr. White. Our school music concert will be on Friday at three. We usually have the concert in the gym, but workers are fixing the gym this week. So the concert will be in the school hall on the first floor. Please come and enjoy the music with your friends. Your parents can come, too. Thank you.
question: 방송을 듣고, 음악회가 열리는 장소를 고르시오.
explain_ko: 평소에는 체육관에서 하지만 이번 주에 체육관을 고치고 있어서 1층 강당(school hall on the first floor)에서 연다.

passage:
W: Hello, this is Jina. Can I speak to Mr. Lee?
M: Speaking. What's up, Jina?
W: I have a dentist appointment on Thursday afternoon. So I can't come to your guitar class that day.
M: I see. Do you want to come on another day?
W: Yes. Can I come on Friday instead?
M: Sure. Come at four.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 전화한 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 목요일 치과 때문에 기타 수업을 금요일로 옮기려고 전화했다. 치과 예약은 이미 되어 있는 일이다.

passage:
W: Hello, Tasty Noodle House. How can I help you?
M: Hi. I had lunch at your restaurant about an hour ago. I think I left my cap there.
W: What does it look like?
M: It's a blue cap with a white letter on it.
W: Just a moment, please. Yes, we have it here.
M: Great. I'll come and get it this evening.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 전화한 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 식당에 모자를 두고 온 것 같다며(I left my cap there) 찾으려고 전화했다. 점심은 이미 먹었다.

passage: M: Good morning, students. This is your science teacher, Mr. Park. As you know, we are having a science fair next month. Any student can take part in it. If you want to join, please write your name on the list in front of the science room by this Friday. You can work alone or with a friend. I'm looking forward to your great ideas.
question: 방송을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 다음 달 과학 박람회에 참가하려면 금요일까지 명단에 이름을 쓰라고 안내한다. 박람회는 아직 열리지 않아서 수상자 발표가 아니다.

passage:
M: Hello, Olivia. This is Daniel.
W: Hi, Daniel. What's up?
M: My family is having a barbecue party in our garden this Saturday. Would you like to come?
W: I'd love to. What time?
M: At five in the evening. You can bring your brother, too.
W: Great. Should I bring anything?
M: No, just come and have fun.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 전화한 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: Would you like to come?으로 토요일 바비큐 파티에 초대하려고 전화했다. 뭘 가져갈지 묻자 아무것도 필요 없다고 했다.

passage:
M: Amy, why are you in such a hurry? You look worried.
W: I'm late for my violin lesson. The bus didn't come on time today.
M: Oh no. What time does your lesson start?
W: At four. It's already three fifty.
M: The music school is far from here. Why don't you take a taxi?
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 이어질 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Good idea. I'll get one right now.
No, the bus is my favorite.
explain_ko: 택시를 타라고 제안했으므로 좋은 생각이라며 바로 타겠다는 답이 알맞다. 수업 시각은 이미 한 말을 되풀이한 것이다.

passage:
W: Excuse me. Can you help me? I'm looking for a gift for my grandfather.
M: Sure. What does he like?
W: He likes gardening. He works in his garden every morning, even on hot summer days.
M: Then how about this hat? It keeps the sun off his face.
W: That's nice. How much is it?
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 이어질 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: You can wear it every morning.
explain_ko: 모자 가격을 물었으므로 값을 말하는 답이 알맞다. 정원 가꾸기와 할아버지 선물은 여자가 한 말이다.

passage:
M: Hey, Yuna. You don't look well today.
W: I have a bad cold. My throat hurts a lot, and I have a fever.
M: That's too bad. Did you see a doctor?
W: Not yet. I have to finish my art homework first. I have to hand it in tomorrow.
M: You should go to the doctor first. Your health comes first.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 이어질 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: That's too bad. Get well soon.
No, I don't have any homework.
You're right. I'll go to the hospital now.
I finished my art homework yesterday.
explain_ko: 숙제보다 병원에 먼저 가라고 충고했으므로 그 말에 따르겠다는 답이 알맞다. Get well soon은 아픈 사람에게 하는 말이라 여자가 할 말이 아니다.

passage:
W: Sam, the school field trip is next Wednesday. Are you excited?
M: Yes! We're going to the science museum, right?
W: That's right. Did you give the permission form to Ms. Green?
M: Oh no, I forgot. It's still in my bag.
W: You have to give it to her by tomorrow. Without it, you can't go on the trip.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 이어질 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Yes, I really enjoyed the field trip.
The museum opens at nine o'clock.
No, I don't have a school bag.
Thanks for telling me. I'll give it to her today.
explain_ko: 내일까지 동의서를 내야 한다고 알려 주었으므로 고맙다며 오늘 내겠다는 답이 알맞다. 현장 학습은 아직 가지 않았으므로 과거형 답은 틀리다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
accomplish
explain_ko: accomplish는 '성취하다, 완수하다'라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Her parents always _____ her to try new things without fear.
explain_ko: 두려움 없이 새로운 것을 시도하도록 이끈다는 뜻이므로 encourage(격려하다)가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
willing to give more money, help, or time than is usual
explain_ko: 보통보다 더 많이 베푼다는 뜻은 generous(관대한, 후한)이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
Forgetting his lines on stage made him feel [embarrassed].
explain_ko: embarrassed(창피한)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 ashamed(부끄러운)이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
accurate
explain_ko: accurate는 '정확한'이라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Investors should not _____ small changes in the market price.
explain_ko: 작은 변화를 무시하면 안 된다는 문맥이므로 ignore(무시하다)가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
to allow someone to do something officially
explain_ko: 공식적으로 허락한다는 뜻은 permit(허락하다)이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The company needs [reliable] data before making a big decision.
explain_ko: reliable(믿을 수 있는)과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 trustworthy(신뢰할 수 있는)이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
ambitious
explain_ko: ambitious는 '야심 있는, 야망이 큰'이라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
The young painter was _____ to show her new artwork to the public.
explain_ko: 자신의 작품을 보여주고 싶어 한다는 문맥이므로 eager(열망하는)가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
a result or effect of an action or event
explain_ko: 어떤 행동의 결과라는 뜻은 consequence(결과)이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The colors used in the painting [vary] depending on the light.
explain_ko: vary(달라지다)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 change(바뀌다)이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
characteristic
explain_ko: characteristic은 '특징, 특성'이라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Water is _____ for almost every living thing on Earth.
explain_ko: 거의 모든 생명체에 꼭 필요하다는 문맥이므로 essential(필수적인)이 알맞다.

question:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
to make someone agree to do something by giving good reasons
explain_ko: 이유를 들어 동의하게 만든다는 뜻은 persuade(설득하다)이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The scientists made a [significant] discovery about the disease.
explain_ko: significant(중요한, 의미 있는)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 important(중요한)이다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
I _____ in this town since I was five.
explain_ko: since(~이래로)와 함께 과거부터 지금까지 계속을 나타내므로 현재완료 have lived. lived는 단순 과거, have live는 과거분사가 아님.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: They have just arrived at the station.
She has visited Canada last year.
Have you ever seen a rainbow?
explain_ko: last year처럼 분명한 과거 시점은 현재완료와 쓸 수 없으므로 She visited Canada last year. 나머지는 경험·완료·결과 용법을 바르게 씀.

question:
두 문장을 한 문장으로 바꿀 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Max started to play the piano three years ago. He still plays it.
→ Max _____ the piano for three years.
explain_ko: 3년 전에 시작해 지금도 하므로 계속 용법 현재완료 has played. played는 지금도 한다는 뜻이 없고, has plays는 과거분사가 아니며, is played는 수동태.

question:
다음 우리말과 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
너는 말을 타 본 적이 있니?
choices: You have ever ridden a horse?
Have ever you ridden a horse?
Have you ridden ever a horse?
Have you ever ridden a horse?
explain_ko: 현재완료 경험 의문문은 Have + 주어 + ever + 과거분사. 나머지는 ever의 위치가 틀리거나 의문문 어순이 아님.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
I'm thirsty. I need something cold _____.
explain_ko: -thing + 형용사 뒤에서 명사를 꾸미는 형용사적 용법 to drink(마실 차가운 것). to drinking은 to 뒤가 원형이 아니고, drink·drinking은 명사를 꾸밀 수 없음.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Give me a chair to sit on.
She has no friends to talk.
He went to the store to buy some milk.
I was glad to see my old teacher.
explain_ko: '~와 이야기할 친구'는 talk 뒤에 전치사가 필요하므로 friends to talk with(to). 나머지는 목적·감정의 원인, 전치사가 있는 형용사적 용법을 바르게 씀.

question:
두 문장을 한 문장으로 바꿀 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Amy studies hard. She wants to pass the test.
→ Amy studies hard _____ the test.
explain_ko: '~하기 위해'라는 목적은 부사적 용법 to부정사 to pass. for 뒤에는 동사원형을 쓸 수 없고, pass·passing은 목적의 뜻을 나타내지 못함.

question:
다음 우리말과 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
우리는 오늘 끝내야 할 숙제가 많다.
choices: We have a lot of homework finish to today.
We have a lot of to finish homework today.
We have to a lot of homework finish today.
We have a lot of homework to finish today.
explain_ko: 형용사적 용법 to부정사는 꾸미는 명사 뒤에 옴 → homework to finish. 나머지는 to부정사의 위치가 틀림.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
This bridge _____ in 1990.
explain_ko: 다리는 지어지는 대상이고 1990년은 과거이므로 과거 수동태 was built. built만 쓰면 다리가 무언가를 지었다는 뜻, is는 현재, build는 과거분사가 아님.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: The letter was written by my grandmother.
The window was broke by the ball.
These cookies were made by Leo.
English is spoken in many countries.
explain_ko: 수동태는 be + 과거분사이므로 was broken이 맞음(broke는 과거형). 나머지는 과거분사 spoken·written·made를 바르게 씀.

question:
다음 문장을 수동태로 바꿀 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Many tourists visit the old palace.
→ The old palace _____ by many tourists.
explain_ko: 능동태가 현재이고 새 주어가 단수(The old palace)이므로 is visited. was는 시제가 다르고, are는 수 불일치, visits는 능동태.

question:
다음 우리말과 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
그 교실은 학생들에 의해 청소된다.
choices: The classroom is by the students cleaned.
The classroom cleaned is by the students.
The classroom is the students cleaned by.
The classroom is cleaned by the students.
explain_ko: 수동태는 주어 + be + 과거분사 + by + 행위자 순서. 나머지는 be동사·과거분사·by의 위치가 틀림.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Take an umbrella _____ it rains this afternoon.
explain_ko: '오후에 비가 오면'이라는 조건이므로 if. because는 아직 오지 않은 비를 이유로 삼아 어색하고, that·but은 뜻과 쓰임이 맞지 않음.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: When I got home, my mom was in the kitchen.
I think that he is honest.
She was late because she missed the bus.
If it will snow tomorrow, we will make a snowman.
explain_ko: 조건을 나타내는 if절은 미래 일도 현재시제로 쓰므로 If it snows tomorrow. 나머지는 that·when·because를 바르게 씀.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
I was sick, so I stayed home.
= I stayed home _____ I was sick.
explain_ko: so 앞이 이유이므로 이유를 나타내는 because. if는 조건, when은 때를 나타내 원래 문장의 인과 관계를 살리지 못하고, that은 부사절을 이끌지 않음.

question:
다음 우리말과 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
나는 그가 내일 올 것이라고 믿는다.
choices: I believe that he will come tomorrow.
That I believe he will come tomorrow.
I that believe he will come tomorrow.
I believe he that will come tomorrow.
explain_ko: 목적어절을 이끄는 that은 동사 believe 바로 뒤, 절의 맨 앞에 옴. 나머지는 that의 위치가 틀림.

passage: The octopus is one of the smartest animals in the sea. It has a large brain for its size, and it also has nerve cells in its eight arms. Because of this, each arm can move and feel things on its own. Octopuses are also great at hiding. They can change the color of their skin in less than a second to match the rocks or sand around them. Scientists have seen octopuses open jars to get the food inside. Sadly, most octopuses live for only one or two years.
question: 문어에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 병을 열어 안에 든 먹이를 꺼낸 적이 있다
1초도 안 되어 피부색을 바꿀 수 있다
explain_ko: most octopuses live for only one or two years 라고 했으므로 대부분 1~2년만 산다.

passage: A rainbow appears when sunlight and rain meet. Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters a raindrop, the light bends. Each color bends a little differently, so the colors spread out. Then the light bounces off the back of the raindrop and comes out toward our eyes. That's why we see bands of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and violet. To see a rainbow, you must stand with the sun behind you. This is why rainbows often appear in the late afternoon after a shower.
question: 무지개에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 모든 색은 빗방울 속에서 똑같이 꺾인다
무지개를 보려면 해를 등지고 서야 한다
햇빛은 한 가지 색으로만 이루어져 있다
explain_ko: stand with the sun behind you 와 일치. 햇빛은 여러 색이고, 색마다 꺾이는 정도가 다르며, 주로 늦은 오후에 보인다.

passage: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity. They are made of special materials that create an electric current when light hits them. Many families now put solar panels on their roofs to save money on electricity bills. Solar power is clean because it does not produce smoke or harmful gases. However, it also has some weak points. Solar panels make less electricity on cloudy days and none at night. For this reason, some homes use batteries to store extra electricity during the day. That way, they can still use it after the sun goes down.
question: 태양광 판에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 지붕에 태양광 판을 다는 가정이 많다
낮에 남는 전기를 배터리에 저장하기도 한다
explain_ko: none at night 라고 했으므로 밤에는 전기를 만들지 못한다. 그래서 배터리에 저장해 둔다.

passage: A mosaic is a picture made of many small pieces. Artists have used stones, glass, and shells to make mosaics for thousands of years. In ancient times, people often put mosaics on floors and walls because they lasted much longer than paintings. To make a mosaic, an artist first draws a design. Then he or she sticks the small pieces onto the surface one by one. Some large mosaics have more than a million pieces, so they can take years to finish. Today, you can find mosaics in subway stations, parks, and even at the bottom of swimming pools.
question: 모자이크에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 옛날에는 그림보다 오래가서 바닥과 벽에 많이 쓰였다
먼저 조각을 붙인 다음 도안을 그린다
explain_ko: they lasted much longer than paintings 와 일치. 유리도 재료이고, 도안을 먼저 그리며, 지하철역·공원·수영장에서도 볼 수 있다.

passage: These days, many families eat dinner together, but they don't really talk. Parents check emails on their phones, and children watch videos. Mealtime is one of the few times when the whole family is together. It is a great chance to share stories about the day and to listen to one another. If we keep looking at our screens, we will miss these precious moments. So I suggest a simple rule for every home: no phones at the table. Put your phone in another room and enjoy a real conversation with your family.
question: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 가족과 식사할 때는 휴대 전화를 쓰지 말아야 한다
부모는 자녀가 보는 영상을 확인해야 한다
가족은 매일 저녁을 함께 먹어야 한다
explain_ko: no phones at the table 이라는 규칙을 제안한다. 함께 먹는 것은 이미 하고 있는 일로 전제되어 있다.

passage: Many students are afraid of making mistakes. They don't raise their hands in class because they worry about giving the wrong answer. However, mistakes are an important part of learning. When you make a mistake, your brain notices that something is wrong and works harder to fix it. This process helps you remember the right answer for a long time. Think about how you learned to ride a bike. You probably fell many times before you could ride well. So the next time you make a mistake, don't feel bad. It means you are learning.
question: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 자전거는 어릴 때 배우는 것이 좋다
정답을 오래 기억하려면 여러 번 써 보아야 한다
수업 시간에 손을 자주 들어야 한다
explain_ko: mistakes are an important part of learning 이 요지이다. 손 들기와 자전거는 도입과 예시이다.

passage: If you want a pet, where will you get one? Many people buy dogs and cats from pet shops. But thousands of animals are waiting for a home in animal shelters. Most of them are healthy and friendly, and they just need someone to love them. Some shelter animals have stayed there for years because people prefer cute puppies from stores. When you adopt a pet from a shelter, you save a life and make room for another animal in need. So before you buy a pet, please visit a local shelter first.
question: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 강아지보다 나이 든 개를 길러야 한다
반려동물을 사기 전에 보호소 입양을 먼저 생각해야 한다
보호소 동물의 건강 검진을 늘려야 한다
explain_ko: 마지막 문장 before you buy a pet, please visit a local shelter first 가 주장이다.

passage: Most of us don't like feeling bored. As soon as we have nothing to do, we turn on the TV or start a game. But boredom is not always a bad thing. When you are bored, your mind starts to wander freely. It connects ideas that seem to have nothing to do with each other. This is often how new and creative ideas are born. Many people say their best ideas came to them while they were waiting for a bus or taking a shower. So the next time you feel bored, don't rush to fill the time. Let your mind play.
question: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 지루하지 않도록 늘 바쁘게 지내야 한다
텔레비전은 생각을 정리하는 데 쓸모가 있다
지루함은 창의적인 생각을 떠올리는 데 도움이 될 수 있다
explain_ko: 지루할 때 생각이 자유롭게 떠돌며 새로운 생각이 나온다는 글이다. 늘 바쁘게 지내라는 것은 정반대이다.

passage: Many people think sharks are dangerous killers. Movies often show them attacking swimmers. In fact, most sharks are _____ to humans. There are more than 500 kinds of sharks, and only a small number of them have ever attacked people. The whale shark, the largest fish in the world, eats only tiny sea creatures. Sharks are much more in danger from us than we are from them. Every year, people catch millions of sharks for food. Also, sharks help keep the ocean healthy by eating sick and weak fish. We should not fear sharks so much. Instead, we should protect them.
question: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: In fact 뒤에 사람들의 생각(위험하다)과 반대되는 내용이 오고, 사람을 공격한 종은 적다고 하므로 harmless(해가 없는)가 알맞다.

passage: In some towns, there is a special kind of library. There, you can borrow tools, tents, and even cooking machines instead of books. Why is this a good idea? Most people use a drill only a few times a year. It sits in a box for the rest of the time. When people _____ things like this, they don't need to buy their own. They save money, and fewer products are made and thrown away. This kind of library also helps neighbors get to know each other. It makes the whole town a little friendlier.
question: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 물건을 빌려 쓰는 도서관 이야기이고, 자기 것을 살 필요가 없다고 하므로 share(함께 쓰다)가 알맞다.

passage: Some psychologists suggest keeping a gratitude journal. Every night before bed, you write down three good things that happened that day. They don't have to be big. A friend's kind words, a delicious lunch, or a sunny afternoon is enough. At first, it might feel strange. But after a few weeks, people who do this start to notice more good things around them. They feel happier and sleep better. Some people also write a short thank-you note to someone once a week. In short, taking a few minutes to feel _____ each day can change the way you see your life.
question: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: gratitude journal(감사 일기)에 하루의 좋은 일을 적는 습관이므로 thankful(감사하는)이 알맞다.

passage: In a rowing race, eight people sit in a long, narrow boat and pull their oars. A race is usually two kilometers long and takes about six minutes. You might think that the strongest rowers always win. But that is not true. If one rower pulls a little too early or too late, the boat slows down and starts to shake. All eight people must move at exactly the same time, like one body. That is why rowers practice for hours to match every stroke. In this sport, _____ matters more than the power of any single person.
question: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 여덟 명이 한 몸처럼 같은 때에 움직여야 한다는 내용이므로 teamwork 가 알맞다. 가장 힘센 선수가 이기는 것은 아니라고 했으므로 strength 는 틀리다.

passage: Dolphins have an unusual way of sleeping. ① Because they need to come up to the surface to breathe, they cannot fall into a deep sleep like humans. ② Instead, they let one half of their brain sleep while the other half stays awake. ③ Dolphins are also famous for their friendly behavior toward people and often appear in aquarium shows. ④ After about two hours, the two halves switch, so each side gets enough rest. In this way, dolphins can keep breathing and watch for danger even while they are asleep. Some birds, such as ducks, can sleep in a similar way.
question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
explain_ko: 돌고래가 뇌의 반쪽씩 자는 방법을 설명하는 글인데, 사람에게 친근하고 수족관 쇼에 나온다는 문장은 잠과 관계가 없다.

passage: Walking is one of the easiest ways to stay healthy, and almost anyone can do it. ① The first running shoes were made more than a hundred years ago. ② Just thirty minutes of walking a day can make your heart and lungs stronger. ③ It also helps you control your weight and lowers your stress. ④ Best of all, you don't need special equipment or an expensive gym membership to do it. So why not walk to school or take the stairs instead of the elevator today? Your body will feel the difference soon.
question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
explain_ko: 걷기가 건강에 좋은 까닭을 말하는 글인데, 최초의 운동화가 만들어진 시기는 관계가 없다.

passage: Cities are often hotter than the countryside around them. ① Roads and buildings made of concrete absorb heat from the sun during the day and release it slowly at night. ② Many people move to cities because there are more jobs and better schools. ③ Air conditioners and cars in cities also give off a lot of extra heat. ④ In addition, cities have fewer trees and plants, which normally cool the air by releasing water. To solve this problem, some cities are planting more trees and building gardens on rooftops. Light-colored roofs that reflect sunlight can also help.
question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
explain_ko: 도시가 더 더운 까닭(콘크리트·에어컨과 자동차·나무 부족)을 말하는 글인데, 일자리와 학교 때문에 도시로 이사한다는 문장은 관계가 없다.

passage: Long ago, before money existed, people traded goods directly. A farmer with extra rice might trade it for a fisher's fish. ① However, this system had a big problem. ② The fisher might not want rice at that moment, so the trade could not happen. ③ To solve this, people began to use things that everyone valued, such as shells, salt, or metal. ④ Today, many people prefer to pay with their phones rather than carry cash. These objects became the first forms of money, and they made trading much easier. Later, people made coins and paper money, which were even easier to carry.
question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
explain_ko: 물물교환의 문제와 최초의 돈이 생긴 과정을 설명하는 글인데, 오늘날 휴대 전화로 결제한다는 문장은 흐름에서 벗어난다. 뒤 문장의 These objects 도 조개·소금·금속을 가리킨다.

passage:
W: Mike, I'm going to skip breakfast again today. I'm not hungry in the morning.
M: You skip breakfast a lot these days. That's not good for you.
W: Why not? I just eat a big lunch.
M: When you don't eat breakfast, it's hard to focus in class. Your brain needs energy in the morning.
W: Maybe you're right. I often feel tired before lunch.
M: Try eating something small, like a banana or some yogurt.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 아침을 거르면 수업에 집중하기 어렵다며 조금이라도 먹으라고 한다. 점심을 많이 먹는다는 것은 여자의 말이다.

passage:
M: Mom, I'm going to the store to buy some snacks.
W: Okay. Take this cloth bag with you.
M: Why? The store gives us plastic bags.
W: Plastic bags take hundreds of years to break down. They're really bad for the Earth.
M: But it's just one bag.
W: If everyone thinks like that, there will be tons of plastic. We should use our own bags when we go shopping.
M: Okay, I'll take it.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 쇼핑은 꼭 필요할 때만 해야 한다.
장을 볼 때는 자기 장바구니를 써야 한다.
비닐봉지는 여러 번 다시 써야 한다.
explain_ko: 비닐봉지가 지구에 해로우니 쇼핑할 때 자기 가방을 써야 한다고 말한다(We should use our own bags). 비닐봉지를 다시 쓰자는 말은 없다.

passage:
W: Dad, I can't sleep well these days.
M: Do you use your phone in bed?
W: Yes, I usually watch videos before I go to sleep.
M: That can be the problem. The light from the screen keeps your brain awake.
W: Really? I didn't know that.
M: You should put your phone away at least thirty minutes before bed. Try reading a book instead.
W: Okay. I'll try that tonight.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 밤에 책을 너무 많이 읽으면 안 된다.
잠이 안 올 때는 영상을 보는 것이 좋다.
자기 전에는 휴대 전화를 멀리 두어야 한다.
explain_ko: 화면 불빛이 뇌를 깨어 있게 하니 자기 30분 전에는 휴대 전화를 치우라고 한다. 영상을 보는 것은 여자의 습관이고, 책은 오히려 권했다.

passage:
M: Ms. Harris, I have to give a speech in front of the class next week. I'm really nervous.
W: That's natural. Did you finish writing your speech?
M: Yes, I did. I'm going to read it from my paper.
W: I think you should practice it out loud many times. Then you won't need to look at the paper much.
M: Out loud? Even at home?
W: Yes. Practice in front of your family. It will help you feel more confident.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 발표는 소리 내어 여러 번 연습해야 한다.
발표문은 종이를 보고 읽는 것이 좋다.
explain_ko: 소리 내어 여러 번 연습하라고 한다(practice it out loud many times). 종이를 보고 읽겠다는 것은 남자의 계획이다.

passage:
M: Hello. I'd like to buy tickets for the water park.
W: Sure. Adult tickets are thirty dollars, and children's tickets are twenty dollars.
M: I need two adult tickets and one child ticket.
W: Okay. Do you have a membership card? Members get ten percent off.
M: No, I don't. I'll get one next time.
W: All right. How would you like to pay?
M: By credit card, please.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 어른 30달러×2 + 어린이 20달러 = 80달러. 회원 카드가 없어서 10% 할인은 받지 못한다(할인하면 72달러).

passage:
W: Excuse me. How much are these socks?
M: They're three dollars a pair. If you buy five pairs, you get one more pair for free.
W: Great. I'll take five pairs. And how much is this scarf?
M: It's fifteen dollars.
W: It's a little expensive, but I like the color. I'll take it, too.
M: Okay. So you'll get six pairs of socks and one scarf.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 양말 3달러×5켤레 = 15달러(여섯 번째는 무료) + 목도리 15달러 = 30달러. 여섯 켤레 값을 모두 내면 33달러로 잘못 계산한다.

passage:
M: Hi. I'd like to order two cheese pizzas.
W: Okay. A cheese pizza is twelve dollars. Would you like anything to drink?
M: Yes. Two bottles of orange juice, please.
W: They're two dollars each. Will you eat here or take the food home?
M: I'll take it home. My family is waiting for me.
W: Then you get two dollars off your order. It will be ready in fifteen minutes.
M: Great. Thank you.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 피자 12달러×2 + 주스 2달러×2 = 28달러, 포장이라 2달러 할인되어 26달러. 할인을 빼먹으면 28달러가 된다.

passage:
W: Hello. I'd like to buy this science magazine and this novel.
M: Okay. The magazine is eight dollars, and the novel is twenty dollars.
W: I have this coupon. Can I use it?
M: Let me see. Yes, you can get five dollars off the novel.
W: Great. Oh, can I also get one of these bookmarks?
M: Sure. Bookmarks are free for all customers this week.
W: Wonderful. Thank you.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 잡지 8달러 + 소설 20달러 - 쿠폰 5달러 = 23달러. 책갈피는 무료다. 쿠폰을 빼먹으면 28달러가 된다.

passage:
W: Hi, Leo. I heard you joined the photography club.
M: Yes. It's really fun. We meet every Tuesday after school.
W: Where do you meet?
M: In the computer room on the third floor. There are about fifteen members in the club.
W: What do you do there?
M: We take pictures around the school and share them. Next month, we're going to have a photo show.
question: 대화를 듣고, 사진 동아리에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 요일(화요일), 장소(3층 컴퓨터실), 회원 수(약 15명)는 나오지만 회비는 나오지 않는다.

passage: M: Hello, everyone. Today I'd like to tell you about koalas. Koalas live in Australia. They eat only the leaves of a special kind of tree. They sleep about twenty hours a day because their food doesn't give them much energy. A baby koala stays in a pocket on its mother's belly for about six months. After that, it rides on its mother's back. Isn't that interesting?
question: 담화를 듣고, 코알라에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 사는 곳(호주), 먹이(특별한 나무의 잎), 잠자는 시간(약 20시간)은 나오지만 수명은 나오지 않는다. 6개월은 새끼가 주머니에 있는 기간이다.

passage: W: Hello, residents. We are having the Riverside Food Festival this Saturday. It starts at eleven in the morning and ends at eight in the evening. You can enjoy food from ten different countries. There will also be a cooking contest for kids. Tickets are five dollars, and children under seven can come in for free. Come and enjoy a fun day with your family.
question: 방송을 듣고, 음식 축제에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 운영 시간(오전 11시~오후 8시), 입장료(5달러), 어린이 요리 대회는 나오지만 주차 안내는 없다.

passage:
M: Look, Grace. I got a new smartwatch for my birthday.
W: Cool! What can it do?
M: It counts my steps every day. It also checks my heart rate while I exercise.
W: Can you make phone calls with it?
M: Yes, I can. And the battery lasts for three days.
W: That's amazing. Who gave it to you?
M: My uncle did. He knows I love running.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 스마트워치에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 배터리(3일), 선물한 사람(삼촌), 전화 기능은 나오지만 가격은 나오지 않는다.

passage:
M: Hannah, what are you doing this weekend?
W: I'm going to volunteer at the animal shelter. I go there every month.
M: Really? What do you do there?
W: I clean the dog houses and walk the dogs. Sometimes I wash them, too. The dogs are always happy to see me.
M: That sounds meaningful. I love dogs, too. Can I go with you this time?
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 이어질 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: No, I don't have a dog at home.
I clean the dog houses every month.
It was really meaningful last week.
Of course. I'll tell the manager about you.
explain_ko: 이번에 같이 가도 되는지 물었으므로 물론이라며 담당자에게 말해 두겠다는 답이 알맞다. 개집 청소는 앞에서 한 말이고, 집에 개가 있는지는 묻지 않았다.

passage:
W: Brian, how was your trip to Rome?
M: It was great. I visited a lot of old churches and palaces.
W: What was the best part?
M: I liked the night view of the big fountain near the palace. The lights were so beautiful.
W: I want to go there someday.
M: You should. It's a great place to learn about history.
W: When is the best time to visit?
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 이어질 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: I think spring is the best. The flowers are beautiful then.
I visited there with my family.
Yes, I learned a lot about history.
It takes about two hours by train.
explain_ko: 언제 가면 가장 좋은지 물었으므로 계절을 말하는 답이 알맞다. 기차로 걸리는 시간은 '얼마나 걸리는지'에 대한 답이다.

passage:
M: Hi, can I help you?
W: Yes. I bought this laptop here last week, but it keeps turning off by itself.
M: I'm sorry to hear that. Let me check it. Hmm, it seems that the battery has a problem.
W: Can you fix it today? I need it for my homework.
M: We need to send it to our main service center. It will take about five days. Or we can give you a new one.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 이어질 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: I bought it here last week.
I'd like a new one, please. I can't wait five days.
Sure. I'll fix it by myself tomorrow.
explain_ko: 5일 수리와 새 제품 교환 중 하나를 고르라고 했으므로 숙제 때문에 기다릴 수 없어 새 것을 원한다는 답이 알맞다. 산 시점은 앞에서 이미 한 말이다.

passage:
W: Kevin, you look tired. Did you sleep well?
M: Not really. I stayed up late to watch the baseball game.
W: Did your team win?
M: No, they lost by one point. I was so disappointed.
W: That's too bad. By the way, we have a math test after lunch. Are you ready?
M: Oh no, I totally forgot about it.
W: Don't worry. We still have some time. Do you want to study my notes together?
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 이어질 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: I watched the game until midnight.
My team won the game last night.
Yes, please. That would help me a lot.
No, I'm not tired at all.
explain_ko: 노트를 같이 보자고 제안했으므로 고맙게 받아들이는 답이 알맞다. 팀은 졌고, 밤늦게 경기를 본 것은 앞 내용일 뿐 제안에 대한 답이 아니다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
attitude
explain_ko: attitude는 '태도'라는 뜻이다. habit(습관)·goal(목표)·personality(성격)와 구별한다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
I should _____ to Mina for breaking her umbrella.
explain_ko: 우산을 망가뜨린 일에 대해 사과해야 한다는 뜻이므로 apologize(사과하다)가 알맞다. refuse·arrive·belong은 'to 사람 for 잘못'과 어울리지 않는다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
able to wait calmly for a long time without getting angry
explain_ko: 화내지 않고 차분히 오래 기다릴 수 있다는 뜻은 patient(참을성 있는)이다. honest(정직한)·brave(용감한)는 다른 성품이다.

question:
The [purpose] of this trip is to learn about local history.
[ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
explain_ko: purpose(목적)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 aim(목표, 목적)이다. result(결과)와 혼동하지 않는다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
recommend
explain_ko: recommend는 '추천하다'라는 뜻이다. refuse(거절하다)·compare(비교하다)·reserve(예약하다)와 구별한다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Jiho was _____ because the concert was canceled at the last minute.
explain_ko: 기대하던 공연이 막판에 취소되었으므로 disappointed(실망한)가 알맞다. excited·thankful·proud는 취소된 상황과 맞지 않는다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
a person who does work to help others without getting paid
explain_ko: 돈을 받지 않고 남을 돕는 일을 하는 사람은 volunteer(자원봉사자)이다. customer(손님)·passenger(승객)는 다른 사람이다.

question:
The small town grew [rapidly] after the new train station opened.
[ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
explain_ko: rapidly(빠르게)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 quickly이다. slowly는 반대말이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
attempt
explain_ko: attempt는 '시도하다'라는 뜻이다. 철자가 비슷한 attend(참석하다)와 헷갈리기 쉽다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Most jobs _____ good communication skills.
explain_ko: 대부분의 직업이 좋은 의사소통 능력을 '필요로 한다'는 뜻이므로 require가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
a person who legally belongs to a country and has rights there
explain_ko: 한 나라에 법적으로 속해 권리를 가진 사람은 citizen(시민, 국민)이다. tourist(관광객)는 잠시 방문한 사람이다.

question:
It looked like an [ordinary] box, but there was a secret door inside.
[ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
explain_ko: ordinary(평범한)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 usual(보통의)이다. strange(이상한)는 반대에 가깝다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
responsible
explain_ko: responsible은 '책임감 있는, 책임이 있는'이라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Regular exercise is an _____ way to stay healthy.
explain_ko: 규칙적인 운동은 건강을 지키는 '효과적인' 방법이라는 뜻이므로 effective가 알맞다. awful(끔찍한)은 문맥과 반대된다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
to find a number or an amount by using math
explain_ko: 수학을 써서 수나 양을 구한다는 뜻은 calculate(계산하다)이다. 끝소리가 비슷한 decorate·translate·celebrate와 구별한다.

question:
She spent the [entire] weekend reading a fantasy novel.
[ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
explain_ko: entire(전체의)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 whole(전부의)이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
I have a friend _____ can speak three languages.
explain_ko: 선행사 a friend(사람)가 주어 역할을 하는 관계대명사 자리이므로 who. which는 사물용, he·they는 접속 기능이 없어 문장이 두 개로 끊긴다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: The bag which you bought is very nice.
The girl which is singing on the stage is my sister.
This is the cake that my mom baked yesterday.
I know a boy who plays the violin very well.
explain_ko: 선행사 The girl은 사람이므로 which가 아니라 who나 that을 써야 한다. 나머지는 선행사에 맞는 관계대명사를 바르게 썼다.

question:
다음 두 문장을 한 문장으로 바르게 연결한 것은?
The man is a doctor. He lives next door.
choices: The man who he lives next door is a doctor.
The man who lives next door he is a doctor.
The man which lives next door is a doctor.
The man who lives next door is a doctor.
explain_ko: He를 주격 관계대명사 who로 바꿔 The man 뒤에 붙인다. 관계절 안에 he를 남기거나, 사람에 which를 쓰거나, 주절에 he를 또 쓰면 틀린다.

question:
다음 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
우리가 어제 본 영화는 정말 재미있었다.
choices: The movie was that we watched yesterday really fun.
The movie we that watched yesterday was really fun.
The movie that we watched yesterday was really fun.
The movie that watched we yesterday was really fun.
explain_ko: 선행사 The movie 바로 뒤에 that + 주어 + 동사(we watched)가 오고 그 뒤에 본동사 was가 온다. 관계절 속 주어·동사 순서나 that 위치가 바뀌면 틀린다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
My mom made me _____ my room before dinner.
explain_ko: 사역동사 make는 목적격보어로 동사원형을 쓴다. to clean은 want·tell 같은 동사에 쓰는 형태라 대표 오답이다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: I heard someone singing in the hall.
She let her brother use her laptop.
The coach wanted us run faster.
We saw the birds fly over the lake.
explain_ko: want는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 쓰므로 wanted us to run이 맞다. 지각동사 hear·see 뒤 원형/-ing, 사역동사 let 뒤 원형은 모두 바르다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
My teacher said to me, "Please close the window."
= My teacher asked me _____ the window.
explain_ko: ask + 목적어 + to부정사 구조이므로 to close. ask는 사역동사가 아니어서 원형 close를 쓸 수 없다.

question:
다음 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
선생님은 우리가 일찍 집에 가게 해 주셨다.
choices: The teacher us let go home early.
The teacher let us go home early.
The teacher let go us home early.
The teacher let us home go early.
explain_ko: 주어 + let + 목적어(us) + 동사원형(go) 순서. 목적어가 동사원형 뒤로 가거나 let 앞으로 가면 틀린다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
_____ is important to drink enough water every day.
explain_ko: 뒤의 to drink ~가 진주어이므로 가주어 It이 필요하다. That·This는 가주어로 쓰지 않고, There는 is 뒤에 명사가 와야 한다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Can you tell me how use this machine?
She didn't decide where to go for the holiday.
It was not easy to find the museum.
It is fun to learn new songs.
explain_ko: '의문사 + to부정사'이므로 how to use가 맞다. 나머지는 가주어 it ~ to부정사, where to go를 바르게 썼다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
I don't know what I should say to her.
= I don't know _____ to her.
explain_ko: '의문사 + 주어 + should + 동사원형'은 '의문사 + to부정사'로 바꿀 수 있다. to 뒤에는 동사원형이 오고, 의문사가 앞에 온다.

question:
다음 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
외국어를 배우는 것은 쉽지 않다.
choices: It is to learn not easy a foreign language.
It is not easy to learn a foreign language.
To it is not easy learn a foreign language.
It is not to learn easy a foreign language.
explain_ko: 가주어 It + is not easy + 진주어 to learn ~ 순서. to부정사구가 형용사보다 앞에 끼어들면 틀린다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
Do you know the boy _____ a red cap?
explain_ko: 소년이 모자를 '쓰고 있는' 능동 관계이므로 현재분사 wearing이 the boy를 뒤에서 꾸민다. worn은 수동 의미, wore·wears는 동사라 한 문장에 동사가 둘이 된다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: The broken cup was on the table.
This is a picture painting by my grandfather.
Who is the girl dancing with Mike?
There are many people waiting for the bus.
explain_ko: 그림은 할아버지에 의해 '그려진' 것이므로 과거분사 painted가 맞다. 나머지는 능동(-ing)·수동(p.p.) 의미에 맞게 분사를 썼다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
The girl who is reading a book is Emma.
= The girl _____ a book is Emma.
explain_ko: '주격 관계대명사 + be동사'를 빼면 현재분사 reading이 명사를 뒤에서 꾸민다. is reading·reads를 쓰면 동사가 두 개가 된다.

question:
다음 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
탁자 위에서 자고 있는 고양이를 봐.
choices: Look at the cat on sleeping the table.
Look at sleeping the cat on the table.
Look at the cat sleeping on the table.
Look at the sleeping on the table cat.
explain_ko: 분사가 수식어구(on the table)와 함께 길어지면 명사 뒤에서 꾸민다: the cat sleeping on the table.

passage:
Dear Ms. Rivera,
My name is Lucy Chen, and I am a second-year student. First, I want to thank you and the kitchen staff for making our lunches every day. The food is always warm and fresh. However, I have a small problem. I do not eat meat, and neither do several of my friends. On many days, the main dish has meat in it, so we eat only rice and a little salad. By the afternoon, we often feel hungry and tired in class. Could you please add a vegetarian choice to the lunch menu, even two or three times a week? Dishes with tofu or beans would be great. Thank you for reading my letter.
Best regards,
Lucy Chen
question: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 급식에 채식 메뉴를 추가해 달라고 요청하려고
explain_ko: 고기를 먹지 않는 학생들을 위해 일주일에 두세 번이라도 채식 메뉴를 넣어 달라는 부탁이 핵심이다. 감사 인사는 글을 시작하는 말일 뿐 목적이 아니다.

passage:
Hello, Mr. Porter,
Last Tuesday, I brought my blue bike to your shop because the brakes did not work well. Your staff fixed them, and I paid thirty dollars. At first, everything seemed fine. But after only three days, the back brake started to make a loud noise again. Yesterday, it almost did not stop the bike on a steep hill. It was really dangerous. I still have the receipt from your shop. Could you check my bike again this week? I can bring it to your shop on Thursday after school. Please let me know if that time is okay for you.
Best regards,
Ethan Walsh
question: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 수리한 자전거 브레이크를 다시 점검해 달라고 요청하려고
explain_ko: 고친 브레이크가 다시 고장 나 이번 주에 다시 봐 달라는 글. 영수증 언급 때문에 환불을 고르기 쉽지만 환불 요구는 없음.

passage: Jenna stood in front of the drama club's board with her friends. The teacher was going to post the list of roles for the school play. Jenna practiced her lines every night for two weeks. She really wanted to play the main character. Her hands were cold, and her heart was beating fast. "What if my name isn't there?" she thought. Finally, the teacher came out and put up the paper. Jenna closed her eyes for a second. Then she opened them and looked at the top line. There was her name next to the main role! Her friends cheered and hugged her. Jenna smiled brightly. Her hard work finally paid off.
question: 다음 글에 드러난 Jenna의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 손이 차갑고 가슴이 뛰다가(긴장) 주인공으로 뽑혀 노력의 결실에 뿌듯해함. excited → disappointed 는 반대 흐름.

passage: It was Leo's first camping trip with his family. After dinner, everyone went into the tent to sleep. Leo lay in his sleeping bag, but he could not close his eyes. Outside, the forest was dark and very quiet. Suddenly, he heard something moving near the tent. Crunch, crunch. Something was walking on the dry leaves. Leo pulled the sleeping bag over his head and held his breath. "Is it a bear?" he whispered. His dad took a flashlight and slowly opened the tent. There was a small raccoon with its face inside their snack bag! It looked up at them with round eyes. Leo burst into laughter, and the raccoon ran away with a cookie.
question: 다음 글에 드러난 Leo의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 곰일까 봐 숨죽이다가(무서움) 과자 봉지에 얼굴을 넣은 너구리를 보고 웃음을 터뜨림(재미있어함).

passage: In autumn, many trees change from green to yellow, orange, and red. Why does this happen? During spring and summer, leaves are full of a green material called chlorophyll. It helps the tree make food from sunlight. Leaves also have yellow and orange colors, but the strong green color covers them. When autumn comes, the days get shorter and cooler.
