The tree stops making chlorophyll, and the green color slowly breaks down. Then the yellow and orange colors that were hidden all summer finally appear. Some trees, like maples, also make new red colors in autumn. Soon after, the leaves fall to the ground, and the tree rests until spring.
question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: The Best Places to See Autumn Leaves
Why Trees Grow Faster in Summer
Hidden Colors: Why Leaves Change in Autumn
How Trees Drink Water Through Their Roots
explain_ko: 초록색 엽록소가 사라지면서 여름 내내 숨어 있던 노란색·주황색이 드러나는 과정을 설명하므로 '숨은 색깔: 가을에 잎의 색이 바뀌는 이유'가 알맞다.

passage: Why do zebras have black and white stripes? For a long time, people thought the stripes helped zebras hide in tall grass. But lions can easily find zebras on the open plains. Now scientists have a new idea. In Africa, there are many biting flies, and they can make animals sick. In one study, scientists watched flies near zebras and horses. The flies flew around both animals. However, they landed on the horses much more often. When the flies came close to the zebras, they seemed confused by the stripes and flew away. The scientists even put striped coats on some horses, and fewer flies landed on them. So the stripes may work like a natural bug spray!
question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Why Horses and Zebras Live Together
Stripes: A Zebra's Shield Against Flies
How Zebras Hide from Lions in Tall Grass
The Dangers of Biting Flies to Humans
explain_ko: 파리가 줄무늬에 헷갈려 얼룩말에게 잘 앉지 못한다는 연구를 소개하므로 '줄무늬: 파리를 막는 얼룩말의 방패'. 풀숲에 숨는다는 것은 글이 부정한 옛 생각이다.

passage: Every morning and night, we brush our teeth with a toothbrush. But people did not always have one. Thousands of years ago, people chewed on small sticks from trees. They chewed one end until it became soft like a brush, and then they rubbed their teeth with it. Later, in China, people made brushes with hard animal hair. They tied the hair to handles made of bone or bamboo. These brushes worked well, but the hair was often rough and dirty. Less than a hundred years ago, a company began to use nylon, a kind of plastic, for the brush. Nylon was soft, clean, and cheap. Soon, almost every family could buy toothbrushes like the ones we use today.
question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How to Brush Your Teeth the Right Way
The Dangers of Eating Too Much Sugar
From Sticks to Nylon: The Story of the Toothbrush
explain_ko: 나뭇가지 → 동물 털 칫솔 → 나일론 칫솔로 이어지는 칫솔의 역사를 다루므로 '나뭇가지에서 나일론까지: 칫솔 이야기'가 알맞다.

passage: Many students use the same easy password for every website, like their birthday or "12345." It is simple to remember, but it is also simple to guess. Some computer programs can try millions of passwords in just one second, so a short password can be broken very quickly. Also, if one website loses your password, bad people can use it to open all your other accounts. So how can you make a strong password? First, make it long. A sentence of four or five words, like "purple frogs eat cold pizza," is hard to guess but easy to remember. Second, use a different password for each important website. A few extra seconds can keep your information safe.
question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Keep It Long and Different: Making Safe Passwords
Why Computers Are Faster Than People
How to Remember Your Friends' Birthdays
explain_ko: 쉬운 비밀번호의 위험을 말한 뒤 길게, 사이트마다 다르게 만들라고 조언하므로 '길고 다르게: 안전한 비밀번호 만들기'가 알맞다.

passage:
Have you ever put maple syrup on your pancakes? This sweet syrup comes from the inside of maple trees. Here is how people make it.

(A) Through this tube, a clear liquid called sap drips slowly into a bucket. It looks like water, and it is not very sweet yet. Farmers collect the sap every day for a few weeks.

(B) First, in early spring, farmers make a small hole in the trunk of a maple tree. Then they put a short tube into the hole.

(C) Finally, the sap is boiled for many hours. Most of the water goes into the air, and thick, sweet syrup is left in the pot. It takes about forty liters of sap to make just one liter of syrup!
question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: (B) 먼저(First) 나무에 구멍을 내고 관을 꽂음 → (A) 이 관(this tube)으로 수액이 떨어짐 → (C) 마지막으로(Finally) 수액을 오래 끓여 시럽을 만듦.

passage:
Cutting onions often makes people cry. The onion is not sad, of course. So why do tears come to your eyes?

(A) Your eyes feel the gas and try to wash it away, so they make tears. To cry less, you can put the onion in the refrigerator before you cut it. The cold slows down the chemicals.

(B) When you cut an onion with a knife, you break many tiny cells inside it. These broken cells let out special chemicals.

(C) The chemicals mix together and quickly turn into a gas. This gas floats up into the air and reaches your eyes.
question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: (B) 양파를 자르면 세포가 터져 화학 물질이 나옴 → (C) 그 물질이 기체가 되어 눈에 닿음 → (A) 눈이 그 기체(the gas)를 씻어 내려고 눈물을 만듦.

passage:
Sam was the shortest player on his school basketball team. During games, he usually sat on the bench and watched the other players.

(A) From then on, he came to the gym an hour early every morning. He shot a hundred balls before class, even when his arms hurt.

(B) A few months later, in the final game, the coach called his name. Sam made three long shots in a row, and his team won the game. Everyone ran to him and cheered.

(C) One day, the coach told him, "You can't grow taller overnight, but you can become a great shooter." Sam thought about these words all night and made a decision.
question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 코치의 조언(C) → From then on 매일 연습(A) → 몇 달 뒤 결승에서 활약(B). From then on 이 C 뒤에 와야 함.

passage:
Last Saturday, Mina went to a pottery class for the first time. She wanted to make a cup for her mom's birthday.

(A) On her second try, the cup stood straight. The teacher said it had to dry for a week before it went into the hot oven. Mina couldn't wait to give it to her mom.

(B) First, the teacher gave her a ball of soft, wet clay. Mina put it on the spinning wheel and pressed it gently with both hands.

(C) Slowly, the clay rose up and became the shape of a cup. But when she pushed too hard, one side fell down, so she had to start again.
question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 점토를 받아 물레에 올림(B) → 컵 모양이 되다 한쪽이 무너져 다시 시작(C) → 두 번째 시도(On her second try)에 성공(A).

passage: Most people drink water only when they feel thirsty. However, thirst is actually a late signal. By the time you feel thirsty, your body has already lost some of the water it needs. Even a small lack of water can make you tired and give you a headache. It can also make it hard to focus in class. That is why doctors say we should drink water _____. For example, keep a water bottle on your desk and take a sip every hour. Also, drink a glass of water with each meal. These small habits will keep your body and mind healthy all day long.
question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: only when our throat is dry
right after we get a headache
explain_ko: 목마름은 늦은 신호이므로 목마르기 전에 틈틈이 마시라는 글. '식사 때만(only)'은 매시간 마시라는 예시와 맞지 않음.

passage: Many teenagers look at their phones in bed before they sleep. They watch videos or chat with friends until late at night. But the bright light from the screen tells your brain that it is still daytime. So your body does not get ready for sleep, and you stay awake longer. Then you feel tired and sleepy the next morning. To sleep better, try to _____ at least an hour before bed. You can charge it in the living room instead of your bedroom. Read a paper book or listen to calm music instead. Your sleep will get deeper, and your mornings will feel much brighter.
question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 화면 빛이 잠을 방해하므로 자기 한 시간 전에는 휴대폰을 치우라는 내용. 짧은 영상도 화면을 보는 것이라 답이 아님.

passage: Some nights the moon looks like a big round ball. Other nights it looks like a thin smile, and sometimes we cannot see it at all. Does the moon really change its shape? No, it doesn't. The moon is always round, and it does not make its own light. It only shines because sunlight hits it. At any time, the sun lights up one half of the moon. As the moon travels around the Earth, we see that bright half from different angles. When we can see the whole bright side, we see a full moon. When we can see only a small part of it, the moon looks thin. So the moon's shape never changes. We just see _____.
question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: new clouds covering it each night
the shadow of the sun on it
different amounts of its bright side
explain_ko: 달은 늘 둥글고 햇빛을 받는 절반이 밝은데, 지구 둘레를 돌면서 그 밝은 쪽을 다른 각도에서 보게 된다는 설명이므로 '밝은 쪽의 서로 다른 부분(양)'을 보는 것이다.

passage: When you travel to another country, you don't need to speak the language perfectly. Still, learning just a few simple words can make a big difference. Words like "hello," "thank you," and "excuse me" are easy to remember. You can learn these words from a phrase book or a free app before your trip. When you use them, local people often smile and become friendlier. They know you are making an effort to respect their culture. Sometimes a shop owner may even give you a helpful tip about the town. Of course, you will make some mistakes, but that is okay. People will still be happy to help you. In the end, a few words in the local language can _____.
question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: make your trip much more enjoyable
make you speak like a native speaker
save you a lot of money
help you pass a language test
explain_ko: 간단한 현지어 몇 마디가 현지인을 친절하게 만들어 여행을 더 즐겁게 한다는 흐름. 완벽하게 말할 필요 없다고 했으므로 '원어민처럼'은 오답.

passage:
W: Hi, Tom. Are you coming to the soccer practice after school?
M: No, I can't go today, Jenny.
W: Why? Did you hurt your leg again?
M: No, my leg is fine now. I have to take care of my little sister.
W: Oh, where are your parents?
M: My mom is working late, and my dad is on a business trip in Chicago.
W: I see. Do you want me to tell the coach?
M: Yes, please. Tell him I'll come on Thursday.
W: Okay. Don't worry about it.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 오늘 축구 연습에 갈 수 없는 이유로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 엄마는 늦게까지 일하시고 아빠는 출장 중이라 여동생을 돌봐야 한다고 했다. 다리는 이제 괜찮다고 했으므로 '다리를 다쳐서'는 오답.

passage:
M: Hey, Sora. Where are you going?
W: I'm going to the city library.
M: Are you going to return the books you borrowed last week?
W: No, I already returned them. I need a book about honeybees.
M: Honeybees? Is it for your science report?
W: Yes. I have to write about how bees help plants grow.
M: That sounds interesting. Why don't you just search the Internet?
W: My teacher said we should use at least one book.
M: I see. Good luck with your report.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 도서관에 가는 이유로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 과학 보고서에 쓸 벌에 관한 책을 빌리려고
explain_ko: 벌이 식물을 자라게 돕는 내용의 과학 보고서를 쓰려고 벌에 관한 책이 필요하다고 했다. 지난주 책은 이미 반납했다고 했으므로 반납은 오답.

passage:
W: Minho, you look tired these days. Are you okay?
M: I'm fine. I just get up at six every morning now.
W: Six? Do you study before school?
M: No. My family moved to a new apartment last month. It's on the other side of the city.
W: Oh, so it takes longer to get to school.
M: Right. I have to take two buses, and the trip takes about an hour.
W: Why didn't you change schools?
M: I love my friends here, and I have only one more year.
W: I see. I'm glad you're still here.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 요즘 아침 일찍 일어나는 이유로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 지난달 도시 반대편으로 이사해 버스 두 번, 한 시간이 걸려서 6시에 일어난다. 공부하냐는 질문에는 아니라고 했고, 전학은 하지 않기로 했다.

passage:
M: Hello, this is Riverside Art Museum. How may I help you?
W: Hi. I booked a tour for this Saturday at two, but I'd like to change it.
M: Sure. May I ask why?
W: My school has a special event that day. I have to play the violin in the school concert.
M: Oh, I see. Which day would you like instead?
W: Is next Sunday available?
M: Yes, we have a tour at eleven in the morning.
W: Perfect. I'll take it.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 미술관 관람 예약을 바꾸려는 이유로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 토요일 오후 두 시에 수업이 있어서
explain_ko: 토요일에 학교 음악회에서 바이올린을 연주해야 해서 예약을 바꾼다고 했다. 미술관 휴관이나 수업 이야기는 나오지 않았다.

passage:
W: Dad, can you help me choose a new backpack for school?
M: Sure. Let's look at this list together. How much do you want to spend?
W: Mom said no more than fifty dollars.
M: Okay, then this one is too expensive. What about the weight?
W: I carry lots of books, so the bag itself should be light. It should be less than one kilogram.
M: That makes sense. Then there are two left. Which color do you like, black or blue?
W: Blue is my favorite color.
M: Then let's order this one.
question:
다음 표를 보면서 대화를 듣고, 여자가 구입할 책가방을 고르시오.
   모델 | 가격 | 무게 | 색
① A | $45 | 0.8kg | 검정
② B | $38 | 1.2kg | 파랑
③ C | $42 | 0.9kg | 파랑
④ D | $55 | 0.7kg | 파랑
explain_ko: 50달러 이하(D 제외), 1kg 미만(B 제외) 중 파란색인 C 모델. B는 파란색이지만 무게 조건에서 빠진다.

passage:
W: Jake, what are you looking at?
M: A list of summer classes at the community center. I want to take one.
W: Let me see. You have taekwondo on Mondays and Wednesdays, right?
M: Yes, so I can't take classes on those days.
W: Do you prefer morning or afternoon classes?
M: Morning. I want to go swimming in the afternoon.
W: Then there are two choices. Which one interests you more?
M: I'm really interested in robots. I'll take that one.
W: It's sixty dollars. Is that okay?
M: Yes. I saved enough money.
question:
다음 표를 보면서 대화를 듣고, 남자가 신청할 여름 강좌를 고르시오.
   강좌 | 요일 | 시간 | 수강료
① 로봇 만들기 | 화·목 | 오전 | $60
② 요리 | 월·수 | 오전 | $50
③ 로봇 만들기 | 화·목 | 오후 | $55
④ 사진 | 화·목 | 오전 | $40
explain_ko: 월·수 제외(요리 제외), 오전 수업(오후 로봇 강좌 제외) 중 로봇에 관심 있다고 한 60달러 강좌. 오후 로봇 강좌는 시간 조건에서 빠진다.

passage:
M: Look, Amy. We can rent bikes here and ride around the lake.
W: Great! Should we get two bikes or one bike for two people?
M: Let's ride one together. It will be more fun.
W: Okay. How much should we spend? I don't want to pay more than ten dollars an hour.
M: Me neither. Then we can't take this one.
W: Right. Oh, we have sandwiches and water. We need a basket to carry them.
M: Good point. Then this is the only one left.
W: Perfect. Let's rent it.
question:
다음 표를 보면서 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 빌릴 자전거를 고르시오.
   자전거 | 종류 | 시간당 요금 | 바구니
① A | 1인용 | $6 | 있음
② B | 2인용 | $9 | 없음
③ C | 2인용 | $12 | 있음
④ D | 2인용 | $8 | 있음
explain_ko: 2인용(A 제외), 시간당 10달러 이하(C 제외), 바구니 있음(B 제외)을 모두 만족하는 D 자전거.

passage:
M: Our class wants to buy a plant for the classroom. Can you help me choose, Jisu?
W: Sure. How much money do we have?
M: We collected twenty dollars, so it should cost less than that.
W: Okay. Remember, nobody is at school during vacation. We can't water it very often.
M: Right. So we should cross out this one. It needs water every day.
W: Where will we put it?
M: On the windowsill next to my desk. It's not very wide.
W: Then we need a small one. This one is perfect.
question:
다음 표를 보면서 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 구입할 식물을 고르시오.
   식물 | 가격 | 물 주기 | 크기
① 로즈메리 | $15 | 매일 | 소
② 산세베리아 | $18 | 2주에 한 번 | 소
③ 고무나무 | $25 | 1주에 한 번 | 대
④ 선인장 | $10 | 한 달에 한 번 | 대
explain_ko: 20달러 미만(고무나무 제외), 물을 자주 안 줘도 됨(로즈메리 제외), 작은 크기(선인장 제외)를 만족하는 산세베리아. 선인장은 싸고 물도 적게 들지만 크기가 크다.

passage: W: Hello, students. This is your vice principal. Our school talent show will be held on Friday, November eighth, in the school hall. It will start at two in the afternoon. Students can sing, dance, play an instrument, or do a magic show. Each act must be shorter than five minutes. You can perform alone or with your friends. If you want to take part, please sign up with your homeroom teacher by October twenty-fifth. The top three acts will get movie tickets. Parents are also welcome to come and watch. We hope to see many great performances.
question: 다음을 듣고, 장기 자랑 대회에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
choices: 혼자 또는 친구와 함께 참가할 수 있다.
explain_ko: 공연은 5분보다 짧아야 한다고 했으므로 10분까지 허용된다는 것은 일치하지 않는다. 장소, 참가 방법, 학부모 관람은 방송 내용과 같다.

passage:
M: Emma, what are you reading?
W: A notice about the school cooking contest. I want to enter it with my friend Yuna.
M: Cool. When is it?
W: It's on November third in the school cafeteria.
M: What do you have to cook?
W: This year's theme is healthy snacks. We're going to make fruit and yogurt cups.
M: Sounds delicious. Do you have to buy the food yourselves?
W: Yes, but the school gives each team ten dollars for it.
M: What do the winners get?
W: The winning snack will be on the school lunch menu next month.
M: Wow. Good luck!
question: 대화를 듣고, 학교 요리 대회에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
choices: 우승한 간식이 다음 달 급식 메뉴에 나온다.
explain_ko: 학교가 팀마다 10달러를 준다고 했으므로 20달러는 일치하지 않는다. 장소, 주제, 우승 혜택은 대화 내용과 같다.

passage: M: Do you love fresh fruit? Sunny Hill Farm is opening its strawberry fields to visitors this spring. The program runs every weekend from April fifth to May twenty-fifth. You can pick strawberries from ten in the morning to four in the afternoon. The price is eight dollars for adults and five dollars for children, and you can take home one basket of strawberries. You don't need to bring anything, because we will give you baskets and gloves. Please book your visit on our website at least one day before. Come and enjoy a sweet day with us!
question: 다음을 듣고, 딸기 따기 체험에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
choices: 적어도 하루 전에 웹사이트에서 예약해야 한다.
explain_ko: 바구니와 장갑은 농장에서 준다고 했으므로 직접 가져와야 한다는 것은 일치하지 않는다. 기간, 어른 요금, 예약 방법은 방송 내용과 같다.

passage:
W: Hi, Daniel. I heard you joined a new club.
M: Yes, I joined the badminton club last month.
W: How often do you meet?
M: Twice a week, on Tuesdays and Fridays after school.
W: Where do you practice?
M: In the school gym. Our coach used to be a professional player.
W: Wow. Do you need your own racket?
M: No, the club lends rackets to new members. But I bought my own shoes.
W: Maybe I should join, too.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 가입한 배드민턴 동아리에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
choices: 신입 회원은 라켓을 직접 사야 한다.
explain_ko: 동아리가 신입 회원에게 라켓을 빌려준다고 했으므로 직접 사야 한다는 것은 일치하지 않는다. 남자가 산 것은 신발이다.

passage: W: Jack and Mina are in the same class. They have a group presentation tomorrow. Jack was supposed to make the slides, but he got sick and missed school today. Mina calls Jack to ask how he is feeling. Jack says he still has a fever, and he is worried about the slides. Mina has some free time this evening, and she is good at making slides. She wants Jack to get some rest. In this situation, what would Mina most likely say to Jack?
question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Mina가 Jack에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Let's meet after school and make the slides together.
Don't worry. I'll make the slides for you.
Why didn't you finish the slides yesterday?
Can you send me the slides by tonight?
explain_ko: 아픈 Jack이 쉬도록 시간이 있는 Mina가 대신 슬라이드를 만들어 주겠다고 하는 것이 알맞다. 오늘 밤까지 보내 달라는 말은 쉬게 하려는 의도와 반대다.

passage: M: Brian and his friend Kate are eating lunch in the park. After they finish, Kate puts her plastic bottle and paper cup into the same trash can. Brian notices that there are separate bins for recycling right next to it. He knows that plastic can be recycled and used again. He wants Kate to put her bottle in the right bin. In this situation, what would Brian most likely say to Kate?
question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Brian이 Kate에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: You should throw away the paper cup, too.
How about buying a bigger trash can?
Let's pick up the trash around the park.
You should put the bottle in the recycling bin.
explain_ko: Brian은 Kate가 플라스틱 병을 재활용함에 넣기를 바란다. 종이컵도 버리라는 말은 이미 한 행동이라 맞지 않는다.

passage: W: Sophia is traveling in a small city with her family. It is their last day of the trip. They are standing in front of a beautiful old church. Everyone wants to take a family picture together, but there is nobody to hold the camera. Just then, Sophia sees a young man walking by. He doesn't look busy. She decides to ask him for help. In this situation, what would Sophia most likely say to the man?
question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Sophia가 남자에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Would you like me to take your picture?
Do you know when this church was built?
Excuse me, could you take a picture of us?
Excuse me, could you show me the way to the church?
explain_ko: 가족 모두 사진에 나오고 싶어서 지나가는 남자에게 사진을 찍어 달라고 부탁하는 상황이다. 남자의 사진을 찍어 주겠다는 말은 방향이 반대다.

passage: M: Lucas loves playing games on his phone. He even plays them while he is walking to school. This morning, he crossed the street without looking up from his phone. A bike almost hit him, and the rider shouted at him. Lucas's friend Ella saw everything, and she was really scared. She knows that many accidents happen when people use their phones on the street. She wants Lucas to stop looking at his phone while he is walking. In this situation, what would Ella most likely say to Lucas?
question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Ella가 Lucas에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: You shouldn't use your phone while you're walking.
You should play games after you finish your homework.
Why don't you buy a new phone?
You'd better ride a bike to school.
explain_ko: 걸으면서 휴대 전화를 보다가 자전거에 부딪힐 뻔한 Lucas에게 걸을 때는 전화를 쓰지 말라고 하는 상황이다. 숙제 뒤에 게임하라는 말은 안전과 관계없다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
observe
explain_ko: observe는 '관찰하다'라는 뜻이다. give up(포기하다)·persuade(설득하다)·invent(발명하다)와 구별한다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
I am truly _____ for all the help you gave me last year.
explain_ko: 도움을 받은 것에 대해 '고마워하는' 마음이므로 grateful이 알맞다. 'be ~ for 도움'과 어울리는 것은 grateful뿐이다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
a family member who lived long before your grandparents
explain_ko: 조부모보다 훨씬 전에 살았던 집안 사람은 ancestor(조상)이다.

question:
The old sailor's stories about the sea always [fascinated] the children.
[ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
explain_ko: fascinate(매료시키다)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 amazed(매혹하다, 놀라게 하다)이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
exhausted
explain_ko: exhausted는 몹시 지쳐서 '기진맥진한' 상태를 나타낸다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Sorry, there are no seats _____ for tonight's show.
explain_ko: 오늘 밤 공연에 '이용할 수 있는(남은)' 좌석이 없다는 뜻이므로 available이 알맞다. 철자가 비슷한 valuable(귀중한)과 헷갈리지 않는다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
worth a lot of money or being very useful and important
explain_ko: 돈의 가치가 크거나 매우 유용하고 중요하다는 뜻의 낱말은 valuable이다.

question:
Heavy traffic is a [frequent] problem on this road during rush hour.
[ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
explain_ko: frequent(잦은, 빈번한)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 common(흔한)이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
ashamed
explain_ko: ashamed는 잘못을 해서 '부끄러운' 감정을 나타낸다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Tom was so _____ about the test results that he couldn't sleep.
explain_ko: 결과가 걱정되어 잠을 못 잤으므로 anxious(불안한, 걱정하는)가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
not thinking that you are better or more important than other people
explain_ko: 자신이 남보다 낫거나 중요하다고 여기지 않는 태도는 humble(겸손한)이다. proud는 오히려 반대에 가깝다.

question:
He felt [jealous] when his friend got a better score than him.
[ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
explain_ko: jealous(질투하는)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 envious(부러워하는)이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
independent
explain_ko: independent는 '독립적인'이라는 뜻이다. dependent(의존하는)와 반대 의미다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
This new washing machine is more _____ ; it uses less water and electricity.
explain_ko: 물과 전기를 덜 쓰면서 일을 잘 처리한다는 뜻이므로 efficient(효율적인)가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
always thinking about other people's feelings and needs
explain_ko: 다른 사람의 감정과 필요를 늘 생각하는 것을 나타내는 낱말은 considerate(배려하는)이다.

question:
Dad decided to [purchase] a new laptop for my birthday.
[ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
explain_ko: purchase(구입하다)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 buy이다. sell(팔다)은 반대말이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
_____ I need now is a cup of hot tea.
explain_ko: 선행사가 없고 '~하는 것'이라는 뜻으로 주어 자리를 이끄는 관계대명사 What. That·Which는 선행사가 있어야 하고 Who는 사람을 묻는다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Tell me what you saw last night.
I met a girl who hair was very long.
This is what I wanted to buy.
He has a dog whose tail is very short.
explain_ko: '그녀의 머리카락'이라는 소유 관계이므로 who가 아니라 whose가 맞다. 나머지는 what(~하는 것)과 whose를 바르게 썼다.

question:
두 문장을 한 문장으로 만들 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
I know a boy. His father is a pilot.
= I know a boy _____ father is a pilot.
explain_ko: His(소유격)를 대신하므로 소유격 관계대명사 whose. who·which·that은 뒤에 주어나 목적어가 빠진 절이 와야 한다.

question:
다음 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
그가 나에게 말한 것은 사실이었다.
choices: What told he me was true.
He what told me was true.
What he told was me true.
What he told me was true.
explain_ko: What + 주어 + 동사(he told me)가 한 덩어리로 주어가 되고, 그 뒤에 was true가 온다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
When I arrived at the station, the train _____ already.
explain_ko: 내가 도착한 과거 시점보다 기차가 떠난 일이 먼저이므로 과거완료 had left. 현재완료는 과거 시점(arrived)과 함께 쓰지 않는다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: He had been lived in Busan before he moved to Seoul.
I had never seen snow before I visited Canada.
It has been raining since this morning.
We have been playing soccer for two hours.
explain_ko: 과거완료는 had lived, 과거완료진행은 had been living이다. had been lived는 수동 형태라 자동사 live에 쓸 수 없다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Jisu started to practice the piano two hours ago. She is still practicing it.
= Jisu _____ the piano for two hours.
explain_ko: 과거에 시작해 지금도 계속하는 동작이므로 현재완료진행 has been practicing. for two hours와 is practicing은 함께 쓰지 않고, had practiced는 과거 기준이다.

question:
다음 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
내가 집에 왔을 때, 남동생은 이미 저녁을 먹었었다.
choices: When I came home, my brother had eaten already dinner.
When my brother came home, I had already eaten dinner.
When I came home, had my brother already eaten dinner.
When I came home, my brother had already eaten dinner.
explain_ko: had + already + p.p. + 목적어 순서. already가 동사와 목적어 사이에 끼면 틀리고, 마지막 문장은 누가 먹었는지 뜻이 바뀌었다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
Can you tell me where _____?
explain_ko: 간접의문문은 '의문사 + 주어 + 동사' 어순이므로 where the library is. is the library는 직접의문문 어순이다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Please tell me who broke the window.
I'm not sure if he will come to the party.
I wonder what does she want for her birthday.
Do you know when the concert starts?
explain_ko: 간접의문문에서는 does를 쓰지 않고 what she wants가 맞다. who가 주어인 간접의문문은 who broke처럼 그대로 쓴다.

question:
다음 두 문장을 한 문장으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?
Do you know? + How old is your teacher?
choices: Do you know how old does your teacher is?
Do you know how old your teacher is?
Do you know how your teacher is old?
Do you know how old is your teacher?
explain_ko: how old는 한 덩어리의 의문사로 앞에 두고 그 뒤를 주어 + 동사(your teacher is) 순서로 쓴다.

question:
다음 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
나는 내일 비가 올지 모르겠다.
choices: I don't know if it will rain tomorrow.
I don't know if will it rain tomorrow.
I don't know it will if rain tomorrow.
If I don't know it will rain tomorrow.
explain_ko: 의문사가 없는 간접의문문은 if(~인지) + 주어 + 동사 순서이다. if 뒤를 의문문 어순으로 쓰거나 if를 문장 맨 앞으로 옮기면 틀린다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
This work must _____ by Friday.
explain_ko: 일이 '끝내져야' 하는 수동 의미이므로 조동사 + be + p.p.인 must be finished. 조동사 뒤에는 finished만 올 수 없다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: The boy was made clean the classroom by the teacher.
The baby was named Lily by her parents.
A gift was given to me by my aunt.
The problem can be solved easily.
explain_ko: 사역동사 make의 수동태에서는 원형이 to부정사로 바뀌어 was made to clean이 맞다. 나머지는 4형식·5형식·조동사 수동태를 바르게 썼다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
My uncle bought me a new bike.
= A new bike was bought _____ me by my uncle.
explain_ko: 4형식 직접목적어를 주어로 한 수동태에서 buy는 간접목적어 앞에 for를 쓴다. give·send 같은 동사가 to를 쓰는 것과 헷갈리게 한 오답.

question:
다음 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
그 창문은 지금 열려서는 안 된다.
choices: The window must not opened be now.
The window not must be opened now.
The window must not be opened now.
The window must be not opened now.
explain_ko: 조동사 수동태의 부정은 조동사 + not + be + p.p. 순서이다. not은 조동사 바로 뒤에 온다.

passage:

망원경 관측 활동은 금요일 저녁에만 한다.

passage: The table shows the results of a survey about the favorite after-school activities of students at Hillside Middle School. Each student was asked to choose only one activity. ① For boys, sports were the most popular activity, chosen by 40 percent of them. ② Online games came second among boys, and the percentage was more than twice that of girls who chose online games. ③ Among girls, music was the most popular activity, followed by drawing and reading. ④ The percentage of boys who chose reading was lower than the percentage of boys who chose drawing. Overall, the survey shows that boys and girls at the school have quite different tastes when it comes to after-school activities.
question:
다음 표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Hillside Middle School 학생들이 가장 좋아하는 방과 후 활동 (%)
