explain_ko: 사진 수(최대 2장), 마감(9월 30일 밤 11시 59분), 전시 장소(Town Hall)는 나오지만 수상자 발표 날짜는 없음.

passage: Many teenagers never cook for themselves. When they are hungry, they eat instant noodles or order food on their phones. Their parents often say, "Just study. I will cook for you." However, learning to cook a few simple meals is an important skill for young people. First, when you cook, you know exactly what goes into your food, so you can eat less salt, sugar, and oil. Second, cooking teaches you useful skills like planning, measuring, and solving problems when something goes wrong. Most of all, it prepares you for the day when you will live on your own. Start with easy dishes such as fried rice or an omelet. Cooking even once a week can make you healthier and more independent.
question: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 배달 음식은 건강에 해로우므로 먹지 말아야 한다.
부모는 자녀가 공부할 수 있도록 식사를 챙겨 주어야 한다.
청소년도 간단한 요리를 할 줄 알아야 한다.
요리를 잘하려면 계획과 측정이 가장 중요하다.
explain_ko: 요리를 하면 건강하게 먹고 생활 기술을 익히며 독립을 준비할 수 있으므로 청소년도 간단한 요리를 배워야 한다는 글이다. 계획·측정은 요리로 얻는 기술의 예일 뿐이다.

passage: When a friend tells you about a problem, what do you usually do? Many people try to give advice right away. They want to fix the problem quickly. But often, your friend doesn't need a solution. What they really need is someone who will listen. When you listen carefully without interrupting, your friend feels understood and respected. You can nod, look into their eyes, and ask simple questions like "How did that feel?" Sometimes, just talking about a problem helps a person find their own answer. Good listeners are not the people who talk the most. They are the people who make others feel heard. Next time a friend comes to you with a problem, try to listen first and talk later.
question: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 대화할 때는 상대방의 눈을 보며 말해야 한다.
친구의 문제는 되도록 빨리 해결해 주는 것이 좋다.
자신의 고민은 스스로 해결하는 습관을 길러야 한다.
친구가 고민을 말할 때는 조언보다 주의 깊게 들어 주는 것이 더 도움이 된다.
explain_ko: But often 이후 '해결책보다 들어 줄 사람이 필요하다'가 요지. 빨리 해결해 주려는 태도는 글이 비판하는 쪽.

passage: Why is the sea salty while the water in rivers and lakes is not? The answer begins on land. When rain falls on rocks, it slowly breaks them down. Tiny amounts of salt and other minerals from the rocks mix with the rainwater. Rivers then carry this water, along with the salt, all the way to the sea. River water tastes fresh because the amount of salt in it is very small. In the sea, however, something different happens. The sun heats the ocean, and water rises into the air as vapor. But the salt cannot rise with it, so it stays behind. This has been happening for millions of years. Little by little, the salt has built up, and that is why seawater is so salty today.
question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: why river water is dangerous to drink
how salt ends up and stays in the sea
the ways people collect salt from the sea
how rain helps plants grow on rocks
explain_ko: 빗물이 바위의 소금을 녹여 강을 통해 바다로 옮기고, 물만 증발해 소금이 쌓인다는 설명이므로 '소금이 바다에 모여 남게 되는 과정'이 주제다.

passage: Imagine watching a scary movie with the sound turned off. It probably won't feel very scary. That is because music plays a big role in how we feel during a movie. Slow, low sounds can make us feel nervous even before anything happens on the screen. On the other hand, bright and fast music makes a scene feel exciting or funny. Sad violin music can bring tears to our eyes during a goodbye scene. Even a single note from a piano can change the mood of an entire scene. Movie makers choose music carefully to guide the audience's feelings. In many ways, the music tells us how to feel before the actors do. Next time you watch a movie, pay attention to what you hear.
question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the power of music to shape viewers' feelings in movies
why scary movies are popular among teenagers
how actors prepare for sad scenes
the history of music used in early films
explain_ko: 영화 음악이 관객의 감정을 이끈다는 내용. 무서운 영화는 도입 예시일 뿐 주제가 아님.

passage: Almost everyone has had hiccups. They often start suddenly, and they can be very annoying, especially in a quiet classroom. So what causes them? ( ① ) Below your lungs, there is a large, flat muscle called the diaphragm. When you breathe in, it moves down smoothly and pulls air into your lungs. ( ② ) When this happens, air rushes into your throat very quickly. ( ③ ) A small part in your throat then snaps shut to stop the air, and this makes the funny "hic" sound. ( ④ ) Hiccups often start when you eat too fast, drink fizzy drinks, or feel excited. Most of the time, they go away on their own after a few minutes. Some people drink a glass of water slowly or hold their breath to stop them.
question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

Sometimes, however, this muscle suddenly tightens by itself.
explain_ko: this muscle은 앞에서 소개한 횡격막을 가리키고, 평소에는 부드럽게 움직인다는 문장 뒤에 however로 '가끔 저절로 조인다'가 와야 다음 문장 When this happens로 이어진다.

passage: Long before refrigerators were invented, people still found ways to keep food cold. In winter, they cut large blocks of ice from frozen lakes and rivers. Workers used long saws to do this hard job. ( ① ) They carried the ice to special buildings called ice houses. ( ② ) These buildings were often built partly underground, where the air was cooler. ( ③ ) Also, the walls were very thick, and the ice was covered with straw or sawdust to keep out the heat. ( ④ ) Thanks to this, families could enjoy cold drinks and keep meat fresh even on hot summer days. Some large farms even sold their extra ice to people in nearby towns. Ice houses were used for hundreds of years until electric refrigerators became common.
question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

As a result, the ice could stay frozen for many months.
explain_ko: 지하 건축·두꺼운 벽·짚 덮개라는 방법이 모두 나온 뒤 결과(As a result)가 오고, 이어서 Thanks to this 가 그 결과를 받으므로 ④.

passage: Today, most people think of ketchup as a sweet, red sauce made from tomatoes. It goes well with French fries and hamburgers. ( ① ) It was a salty sauce made from fish, and people in parts of Asia used it to add flavor to their food. ( ② ) About three hundred years ago, British traders tasted this sauce and brought the idea home. ( ③ ) Back in Britain, cooks tried to make it with mushrooms, walnuts, or even oysters. ( ④ ) Tomato ketchup finally appeared in America in the early 1800s. At first, it went bad quickly, so later makers added more sugar and vinegar to help it last longer. That is how the sweet ketchup we know today was born.
question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

However, the very first ketchup did not have any tomatoes in it.
explain_ko: 토마토로 만든 소스라는 오늘날의 생각 뒤에 However로 '처음 케첩엔 토마토가 없었다'가 와야, 그다음 It was a salty sauce made from fish가 그 첫 케첩을 설명하게 된다.

passage: Many young athletes want to start playing right away. They skip the warm-up because it seems boring and slow. ( ① ) However, warming up is one of the best ways to prevent injuries. ( ② ) When your muscles are cold, they are stiff like a rubber band left in the freezer. ( ③ ) Light jogging and stretching raise the temperature of your body and make your muscles soft. ( ④ ) Then they can move smoothly and quickly during the game. Warm muscles also help you jump higher and run faster. Professional players never skip their warm-up, even before a short practice. So spend at least ten minutes warming up before you play. A few minutes of preparation can save you weeks of pain.
question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

If you stretch them suddenly, they can easily tear.
explain_ko: them 은 차갑고 뻣뻣한 근육. 얼린 고무줄 비유 뒤, 준비운동으로 부드럽게 한다는 해결책 앞인 ③.

passage: Why does the price of a popular item sometimes go up so quickly? Let's think about a new toy that every child wants for the holidays. The toy company made only a small number of them. As the holidays come closer, more and more parents rush to the stores. Soon the shelves are empty, and some sellers raise the price. Some people even sell the toy online for twice its original price. Surprisingly, people still buy the toy, even at a higher price. After the holidays, however, fewer people want the toy. Most parents have already bought their gifts. Then stores lower the price to sell the toys left on their shelves. In short, prices usually rise when a product is _____.
question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: wanted by many but made in small numbers
explain_ko: 적게 만들었는데 원하는 사람이 많을 때 값이 오르고, 원하는 사람이 줄면 값이 내림. 명절 뒤에는 오히려 값이 내려감.

passage: During a storm, you see a flash of lightning first. A few seconds later, you hear the loud sound of thunder. But in fact, lightning and thunder happen at the same time. They are created by the same electric spark in the sky. So why don't we notice them together? The answer is that light travels _____. Light moves about 300,000 kilometers in just one second. Sound, however, moves only about 340 meters per second. You can even use this fact to find out how far away a storm is. Count the seconds between the flash and the sound. Then divide the number by three. The answer is roughly the distance in kilometers. For example, if you count six seconds, the storm is about two kilometers away.
question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: at the same speed as sound
explain_ko: 빛은 초속 약 30만 km, 소리는 초속 약 340 m 이므로 빛이 훨씬 빨라 번개가 먼저 보임.

passage: When you meet someone for the first time, how long does it take to form an opinion about them? It may be much shorter than you think. According to some researchers, people decide whether they like someone _____. In that short moment, we notice a person's face, smile, and body language. We usually do this without even knowing it. What's more interesting is that first impressions are hard to change. Even if we learn new facts about the person later, our first feeling often stays. This is why job interviews and first days at a new school can feel so important. So the next time you meet someone new, a warm smile and a friendly hello can make a big difference.
question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: by looking at their school grades
only after they become close friends
explain_ko: 'much shorter than you think', 'In that short moment'가 단서. 긴 대화 뒤라는 선택지는 흐름과 반대.

passage: Every year, a huge amount of food is thrown away around the world. Much of this waste happens not in restaurants or on farms but in our own homes. We often buy too much at the supermarket, especially when there are sales. Then the food goes bad in the refrigerator before we can eat it. Wasted food is not just a waste of money. It also becomes trash that produces harmful gases as it rots. The simplest way to reduce food waste is _____. Before shopping, check what is already in your refrigerator and make a list. Then stick to the list, even when you see a special offer. Small changes like these can protect both your wallet and the planet.
question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 냉장고 확인·목록 작성·목록 지키기 모두 필요한 것만 사라는 뜻. 세일 때 더 사는 것이 음식 낭비의 원인으로 나옴.

passage: M: Good morning, students. This is Ben Carter, your school librarian. I'd like to tell you about a change in the library schedule. Starting next Monday, the library will close for two weeks because we are putting in new bookshelves and computers. During that time, you can't borrow or return books. If you have books from the library, please return them by this Friday. The library will open again on May twentieth with a more comfortable reading space. Thank you for understanding.
question: 다음을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 새 독서 공간의 이용 규칙을 안내하려고
explain_ko: 새 책장과 컴퓨터 설치로 다음 주 월요일부터 2주 동안 도서관이 문을 닫는다는 것을 알리는 방송이다. 새 독서 공간은 다시 열 때의 모습일 뿐 이용 규칙 안내가 아니다.

passage: W: Hello, listeners. Many students study for hours without a break before an exam. They think this is the best way to get good grades. However, our brains get tired when we focus for too long. After about fifty minutes, it becomes hard to remember new information. So I suggest taking a short break of about ten minutes every hour. You can stretch, walk around, or drink some water. These short breaks help your brain rest and remember things better. Try it during your next exam period.
question: 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 공부할 때 규칙적으로 짧은 휴식을 취하면 기억에 도움이 된다.
explain_ko: 한 시간마다 10분 정도 쉬면 뇌가 쉬고 더 잘 기억한다는 것이 요지다. 물 마시기는 쉬는 동안 할 수 있는 예시일 뿐이다.

passage: W: Hello, residents of Green Hill Town. This is Linda Park from the town office. As you know, our town has become hotter every summer. Trees can give us shade and clean air. So this April, we are planning to plant five hundred trees along the river. We need many hands to make this happen. If you'd like to join, please come to the town office at nine on April fifth. We'll give you gloves and tools. Let's make our town greener together.
question: 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 강가에 나무 500그루를 심을 계획이니 4월 5일에 참여해 달라는 방송이다. 더위 이야기는 나무를 심는 이유로 나온 것이다.

passage: M: Hi, everyone. I'm Kevin Moore, and I'm a sports coach. Many students start running or playing soccer as soon as they get to the field. They think warming up is a waste of time. However, cold muscles are stiff, and they can be hurt easily. Before you exercise, spend about ten minutes warming up your body. You can walk fast, jog slowly, or stretch your arms and legs. This makes your muscles warm and soft, so you can move better. It also lowers your chance of getting hurt. Remember, a few minutes of warming up can keep you in the game all season.
question: 다음을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 운동은 매일 같은 시간에 하는 것이 좋다.
운동 전에 준비 운동을 해야 부상을 막을 수 있다.
explain_ko: 굳은 근육은 다치기 쉬우므로 운동 전에 10분쯤 준비 운동을 하라는 것이 요지다. 빨리 걷기·스트레칭은 준비 운동의 예일 뿐이다.

passage:
M: Welcome to Green Leaf Flower Shop. How can I help you?
W: Hi. I'd like to buy some roses for my teacher. Tomorrow is Teachers' Day.
M: Good idea. Red roses are three dollars each, and pink roses are two dollars each.
W: I'll take ten red roses.
M: Okay. Would you like to add a card? It's two dollars.
W: Yes, please. I want to write a thank-you message.
M: Also, we're having a spring sale this week. You can get ten percent off all flowers.
W: Really? Does the card get a discount, too?
M: I'm sorry, but the discount is only for flowers.
W: That's fine. Here's my credit card.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 빨간 장미 10송이 30달러에서 10% 할인해 27달러, 할인 없는 카드 2달러를 더해 29달러. 카드를 빠뜨리면 27달러, 할인을 빠뜨리면 32달러가 되는 함정이 있다.

passage:
W: Welcome to Top Sports. Can I help you?
M: Yes. I'm looking for a soccer ball for my team.
W: How about this one? It's twenty dollars.
M: Good. I'll take two, one for practice and one for games.
W: Okay. Do you need anything else?
M: I also need a water bottle. How much is this one?
W: It's eight dollars. Oh, we're having an event this week. If you buy two balls, you get twenty-five percent off the balls.
M: Great. Does the water bottle get a discount, too?
W: No, only the balls.
M: I see. Here's my money.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 공 2개 40달러에서 25% 할인해 30달러, 할인 없는 물병 8달러를 더해 38달러. 물병까지 할인하면 36달러, 할인을 빠뜨리면 48달러가 되는 함정이 있다.

passage:
M: Hi. My son and I would like to go bowling.
W: Sure. One game is six dollars for adults and four dollars for children. How old is your son?
M: He's twelve.
W: Then he pays the children's price. How many games would you like to play?
M: Two games each, please.
W: Okay. You also need bowling shoes. They're two dollars a pair.
M: We brought our own shoes, so we don't need them.
W: Great. Oh, today is Family Day, so families get five dollars off the total price.
M: That's nice. Here's my card.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
explain_ko: (어른 6달러+어린이 4달러)×2게임=20달러에서 5달러 할인이므로 15달러. 신발은 가져왔으므로 빌리지 않는다. 신발값을 더하면 19달러가 되는 함정이 있다.

passage:
W: Hi. Two tickets for Ocean Adventure at five o'clock, please.
M: Sure. Tickets are twelve dollars each.
W: Can I use this student card? My friend and I are both students.
M: Yes. Students get two dollars off each ticket.
W: Great. We'd also like a popcorn combo.
M: The popcorn combo is eight dollars. It comes with two drinks.
W: Perfect. We'll take one.
M: Would you like butter on the popcorn? It's free.
W: No, thanks. Just plain popcorn.
M: Okay. How would you like to pay?
W: With my phone, please.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 학생 할인으로 표 한 장에 10달러씩 2장 20달러, 팝콘 세트 8달러를 더해 28달러. 할인을 한 장에만 적용하면 30달러가 된다.

passage: W: Today, I'd like to introduce an amazing sea animal, the sea otter. Sea otters live along the coasts of the North Pacific Ocean. They are one of the smallest sea mammals, but they have the thickest fur of any animal. Their fur keeps them warm in cold water. Sea otters mostly eat sea urchins, crabs, and clams. They often use rocks as tools to break open shells. Also, when they sleep, they sometimes hold hands with each other so they don't float away.
question: 다음을 듣고, 해달에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 서식지(북태평양 해안), 먹이(성게·게·조개), 도구 사용(돌로 껍데기 깨기)은 언급됐지만 수명은 나오지 않았다.

passage: M: Hello, students. I'm happy to announce our school's first flea market. It will be held on June tenth in the school playground. You can sell things you don't use anymore, such as books, clothes, and toys. Each class will get one table to sell their items. All the money we make will be given to a local children's hospital. If you want to sell your things, please sign up with your homeroom teacher by June third. Don't miss this chance to share and help others.
question: 다음을 듣고, 학교 벼룩시장에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 장소(운동장), 수익금(어린이 병원 기부), 신청 방법(담임 선생님께 신청)은 언급됐지만 물건 가격 제한은 나오지 않았다.

passage: W: Hello, class. Today we're going to learn about silk, one of the oldest kinds of cloth in the world. Silk is made from the thread of silkworms. A silkworm makes a small ball called a cocoon, and one cocoon can have a thread about one kilometer long. It takes about three thousand cocoons to make one silk dress. Silk is very light but strong, and it keeps you cool in summer and warm in winter. Long ago, people carried it on long roads across Asia to sell it. Today, silk is used to make ties, scarves, and even special thread for doctors.
question: 다음을 듣고, 비단에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
choices: 옷 한 벌에 드는 고치 수
explain_ko: 재료(누에고치의 실), 옷 한 벌에 드는 고치 수(약 3,000개), 오늘날의 쓰임(넥타이·스카프·의료용 실)은 언급됐지만 가격은 나오지 않았다.

passage: M: Are you looking for a fun way to stay healthy? Join our new family yoga class at Maple Community Center. The class is for parents and children aged seven and older. It meets every Sunday morning from ten to eleven. Our instructor has taught yoga for over fifteen years. You don't need to bring anything, because we provide mats and water. The class is limited to twenty families, so sign up early at the front desk. Enjoy a healthy weekend with your family!
question: 다음을 듣고, 가족 요가 수업에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 대상(부모와 7세 이상 자녀), 시간(일요일 10시~11시), 인원(20가족)은 언급됐지만 수강료는 나오지 않았다.

passage:
W: Jason, did you hear about the school's new rule on phones?
M: Yes. We have to put our phones in a box before class starts.
W: What do you think about it?
M: At first, I didn't like it. But now I think it's helpful. I can focus better in class.
W: Really? I still feel nervous without my phone.
M: Why? Are you waiting for important messages?
W: Not really. I just check it out of habit.
M: I used to be like that, too. Why don't you try leaving your phone at home this weekend, just for one day?
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 대한 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: No, I don't think the new rule is fair.
Sure. I'll call you on Saturday then.
That sounds hard, but I'll give it a try.
Right. I put it in the box before class.
explain_ko: 주말에 하루 휴대 전화를 두고 지내 보라는 제안에 한번 해 보겠다고 답하는 것이 자연스럽다. 토요일에 전화하겠다는 말은 제안과 모순된다.

passage:
M: Mom, I've finished packing for the school trip.
W: Good. Did you pack a raincoat? The weather report said it might rain on the second day.
M: Oh, I forgot. I'll put it in my bag now.
W: And what about your medicine? You often get carsick on long bus rides.
M: Right. I'll bring some. Where is it?
W: It's in the kitchen drawer. By the way, what time do you have to be at school tomorrow?
M: By seven thirty. The bus leaves at eight.
W: That's early. You'd better go to bed now.
M: Okay. Can you wake me up at six, just in case my alarm doesn't go off?
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 대한 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Of course. I'll knock on your door at six.
No problem. The medicine is in the drawer.
Sure. I'll pack your raincoat right away.
Don't worry. The bus leaves at eight.
explain_ko: 6시에 깨워 달라는 부탁에 6시에 문을 두드리겠다고 답하는 것이 알맞다. 나머지는 앞에서 나온 내용을 되풀이한 오답이다.

passage:
W: Hi, Noah. You look worried. What's wrong?
M: I have to read three novels for English class, but I can't even finish one.
W: Why not? Are the books too difficult?
M: Not really. I just get bored after a few pages and start looking at my phone.
W: How about joining a book club? I'm in one at the city library.
M: A book club? How will that help?
W: We read the same book and talk about it every two weeks. When people are waiting to talk about the story, you keep reading.
M: That makes sense. Would you let me know when your next meeting is? I'd like to try it.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 대한 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Really? I didn't know you liked English class.
I'm sorry, but I've never read a novel.
Thanks. I'll finish the novel tonight.
Sure. I'll text you the date tonight.
explain_ko: 다음 모임 날짜를 알려 달라는 부탁에 오늘 밤 문자로 알려 주겠다고 답하는 것이 알맞다. 소설을 다 읽겠다는 말은 남자가 할 말이다.

passage:
M: Hey, Claire. What are you looking at on your computer?
W: I'm looking at used cameras on a second-hand shopping site.
M: Used cameras? Why don't you buy a new one?
W: New ones are too expensive. This one is only half the price, and it looks almost new.
M: But you should be careful. Some sellers don't tell the truth about their products.
W: I know. That's why I'm going to meet the seller in person and check the camera first.
M: Good idea. When are you meeting him?
W: This Saturday afternoon. Actually, you know a lot about cameras. Could you come with me and check it?
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 대한 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Right. New cameras are too expensive.
Sure. I'm free on Saturday afternoon.
No thanks. I already have a camera.
Okay. I'll sell my camera online.
explain_ko: 토요일 오후에 함께 가서 카메라를 봐 달라는 부탁에 그때 시간이 된다고 수락하는 것이 알맞다. 카메라가 이미 있다는 말은 부탁을 잘못 이해한 답이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
tradition
explain_ko: tradition은 오래 이어져 온 '전통'이라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
We should turn off the lights when we leave the room to _____ energy use.
explain_ko: 불을 끄는 것은 에너지 사용을 '줄이기' 위한 것이므로 reduce가 알맞다. increase(늘리다)는 반대다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
damage to the air, water, or land caused by harmful substances
explain_ko: 해로운 물질 때문에 공기·물·땅이 망가지는 것은 pollution(오염)이다. 철자가 비슷한 population(인구)과 구별한다.

question:
[Frankly], I didn't enjoy the movie very much.
[ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
explain_ko: frankly(솔직히)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 honestly(솔직히 말해서)이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
evidence
explain_ko: evidence는 사실임을 보여 주는 '증거'라는 뜻이다. rumor(소문)와 구별한다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Everyone on the team should _____ ideas to make the school festival a success.
explain_ko: 축제 성공을 위해 모두가 아이디어를 '내놓아야(기여해야)' 한다는 뜻이므로 contribute가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
to give money, food, or other things to help a person or group
explain_ko: 사람이나 단체를 돕기 위해 돈·음식 등을 주는 것은 donate(기부하다)이다.

question:
It was [obvious] that Ben was tired because he kept yawning.
[ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
explain_ko: obvious(분명한, 명백한)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 clear이다. doubtful(의심스러운)은 반대에 가깝다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
appropriate
explain_ko: appropriate는 상황에 '적절한, 알맞은'이라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
It is hard to _____ on homework when the TV is loud.
explain_ko: TV 소리가 크면 숙제에 '집중하기' 어렵다는 뜻이므로 concentrate (on)이 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
the power to change how someone thinks or behaves
explain_ko: 다른 사람의 생각이나 행동을 바꾸는 힘은 influence(영향, 영향력)이다.

question:
Several volunteers will [assist] the elderly at the festival.
[ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
explain_ko: assist(돕다)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 help이다. ignore(무시하다)는 반대에 가깝다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
reputation
explain_ko: reputation은 사람들이 어떤 사람·곳에 대해 갖는 '평판, 명성'이라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
The two classes had to _____ to finish the mural before the deadline.
explain_ko: 마감 전에 벽화를 끝내려면 두 반이 '협력해야' 했다는 뜻이므로 cooperate가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
honest and really meaning what you say or feel
explain_ko: 정직하고 말이나 감정에 진심이 담긴 것은 sincere(진실한, 진심 어린)이다.

question:
An [enormous] whale suddenly jumped out of the water.
[ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
explain_ko: enormous(거대한)와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은 huge이다. tiny(아주 작은)는 반대말이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
If I _____ a bird, I could fly over the mountains.
explain_ko: 현재 사실과 반대되는 가정(가정법 과거)이므로 if절에 were, 주절에 could + 원형. am·will be는 실제로 가능한 조건에 쓴다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: If it were sunny, we could go on a picnic.
If he has more time, he would learn to cook.
What would you do if you found a lost puppy?
If I knew her number, I would call her.
explain_ko: 주절이 would이므로 가정법 과거로 if절도 과거형 had를 써야 한다. 나머지는 if절 과거형 + 주절 would/could + 원형으로 바르다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
As I don't have enough money, I can't buy the jacket.
= If I _____ enough money, I _____ buy the jacket.
explain_ko: 현재 사실의 반대이므로 긍정·부정을 바꾸고 시제를 한 단계 과거로: had ... could. 부정을 그대로 두거나 현재형을 쓰면 틀린다.

question:
다음 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
만약 내가 너라면, 나는 그에게 사과할 텐데.
choices: If were I you, I would say sorry to him.
If I were you, I say would sorry to him.
If I you were, I would say sorry to him.
If I were you, I would say sorry to him.
explain_ko: If + 주어 + were + 보어, 주어 + would + 동사원형 순서. would는 동사원형 앞에 온다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
This is the park _____ I first met my best friend.
explain_ko: 선행사가 장소(the park)이고 뒤 절이 완전하므로 관계부사 where. which를 쓰려면 in which처럼 전치사가 필요하다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Tell me the reason why you were late.
This is how I make pancakes.
This is the way how he solved the puzzle.
I remember the day when we moved to this town.
explain_ko: the way와 how는 함께 쓰지 않고 둘 중 하나만 쓴다(the way he solved / how he solved). 나머지 관계부사는 선행사에 맞게 썼다.

question:
두 문장을 한 문장으로 만들 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
This is the house. My grandparents lived in it.
= This is the house _____ my grandparents lived.
explain_ko: in it(장소)을 대신하는 관계부사 where. which만 쓰면 in이 빠져 틀리고, 전치사 뒤에는 that을 쓰지 않는다.

question:
다음 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
나는 그녀가 울고 있었던 이유를 모른다.
choices: I don't know why the reason she was crying.
I don't know the reason why she was crying.
I don't know the reason she why was crying.
I don't know the reason why was she crying.
explain_ko: 선행사 the reason + why + 주어 + 동사 순서. why 뒤를 의문문 어순(was she)으로 쓰면 틀린다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
_____ the news, she started to cry.
explain_ko: 주어가 뉴스를 '들은' 능동 관계이므로 현재분사로 시작하는 분사구문 Hearing. She heard는 접속사 없이 두 절을 이어 틀리고, Heard는 수동 의미다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Opened the door, he saw a big box.
Walking along the beach, we found some pretty shells.
Smiling brightly, the girl waved at us.
Having no money, he couldn't buy lunch.
explain_ko: 그가 문을 '연' 능동 관계이므로 Opening이 맞다. 과거분사 Opened는 문이 열려진 수동 의미가 된다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
When he entered the room, he turned on the light.
= _____ the room, he turned on the light.
explain_ko: 접속사와 같은 주어를 지우고 동사를 현재분사로 바꾼다: Entering. 주어를 남기거나 수동형(Entered, Being entered)을 쓰면 틀린다.

question:
다음 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
음악을 들으면서 그는 숙제를 했다.
choices: Listening to music, did he his homework.
Listening to music, he did his homework.
Listening music to, he did his homework.
To music listening, he did his homework.
explain_ko: 분사구문 Listening to music 뒤에 주절 주어 + 동사(he did)가 온다. 주절을 의문문 어순으로 쓰면 틀린다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
The box was _____ heavy that I couldn't lift it.
explain_ko: '너무 ~해서 …하다'는 so + 형용사 + that. too는 to부정사와 짝이고, such는 뒤에 명사가 와야 한다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: This soup is too hot to eat now.
It is kind for you to help me.
He ran so fast that nobody could catch him.
It is hard for children to sit still for a long time.
explain_ko: kind처럼 사람의 성격을 나타내는 형용사 뒤 의미상 주어는 of + 목적격이므로 of you가 맞다. hard 뒤에는 for를 쓴다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Mina is too young to watch the movie.
= Mina is so young that she _____ watch the movie.
explain_ko: too ~ to는 '너무 ~해서 …할 수 없다'이므로 so ~ that + 주어 + can't. 시제가 현재(is)이므로 can't를 쓴다.

question:
다음 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 바르게 배열한 문장은?
그 질문은 내가 답하기에 너무 어려웠다.
choices: The question was too difficult me for to answer.
The question was too for me difficult to answer.
The question was too difficult for me to answer.
The question was difficult too for me to answer.
explain_ko: too + 형용사 + for + 목적격(의미상 주어) + to부정사 순서. 의미상 주어는 to부정사 바로 앞에 온다.

passage:
Dear Ms. Carter,
I am the leader of the history club at Westbrook Middle School. Our members have been studying the ancient cultures of the Mediterranean this semester, and we are very excited about your museum's new exhibition on ancient Greek pottery. We are planning to visit the museum on Friday, November 14, with twenty students and two teachers. Although we have read a lot about the topic, we believe that an expert's explanation would help us understand the works more deeply. So I would like to ask whether one of your museum guides could lead a tour for our group. If possible, we would prefer a tour that starts around 10 a.m. and lasts about an hour. We look forward to hearing from you.
Sincerely,
Daniel Brooks
question: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 박물관 단체 관람 때 해설사의 안내를 요청하려고
박물관 단체 관람 날짜를 바꿔 달라고 요청하려고
새 전시회를 본 학생들의 감상을 전하려고
역사 동아리 학생들의 작품 전시를 제안하려고
explain_ko: So I would like to ask ~ 이하에서 가이드의 해설 투어를 요청함. 방문 날짜는 알리기만 할 뿐 변경 요청이 아님.

passage:
To the Editor,
Every weekend, I walk along the lake in Pinewood Park, and I often see families throwing bread to the ducks. I know they do this out of kindness, and the children clearly enjoy it. However, bread is actually harmful to ducks. It fills their stomachs but gives them almost none of the nutrients they need. Ducks that eat too much bread can become weak and sick. In addition, the bread that is not eaten sinks and rots, which makes the lake water dirty. I am writing to ask park visitors to stop giving bread to the birds. If people really want to feed them, they can bring small amounts of peas or oats instead. Let's protect our ducks and our lake together.
Sincerely,
Rachel Kim
question: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 공원에 오리 먹이 판매대를 설치할 것을 건의하려고
공원 방문객들에게 오리에게 빵을 주지 말 것을 당부하려고
오리 먹이 주기 체험 행사를 홍보하려고
explain_ko: I am writing to ask ~ 에 목적이 드러남. 수질 오염은 빵을 주면 안 되는 이유 중 하나일 뿐 공사 요구는 없음.

passage: Chloe was getting ready to meet her friends when she heard a knock on her bedroom door. It was her little brother, Toby, again. All week he had been following her around the house, asking to borrow her things and wanting to know where she was going. "Not now, Toby!" she said sharply, and she shut the door. A few minutes later, she noticed a small box on the floor outside her room. Inside were her favorite headphones, the ones that had broken last month. They were working again, and there was a note in Toby's messy handwriting: "I saved my pocket money and took them to the repair shop. Happy birthday a week early!" Chloe stood still for a moment, holding the box. Then she opened the door and hugged her brother tightly.
question: 다음 글에 드러난 Chloe의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 일주일 내내 따라다니는 동생에게 짜증을 내던 Chloe가(annoyed) 동생이 용돈으로 고쳐 온 헤드폰과 쪽지를 보고 동생을 꼭 안아 준다(touched).

passage: It was Aria's third week at her new school, and she still ate lunch alone. Every day, she sat at the corner table and pretended to read a book while the other students laughed together. She missed her old friends, and the cafeteria felt like the loneliest place in the world. That Wednesday, as she opened her lunch box, someone stopped in front of her table. It was Noah from her science class. "We need one more person for our robot project team," he said. "Would you like to join us? You can sit with us, too." Aria looked up in surprise. For the first time in weeks, she felt warm inside. She picked up her lunch box and followed him, knowing she would never forget his kindness.
question: 다음 글에 드러난 Aria의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 혼자 점심을 먹으며 외로워하다가 먼저 다가온 Noah 의 친절에 고마움을 느낌.

passage: Most people think that procrastination, or putting things off, is simply a problem of laziness. However, psychologists have found that it is often more about feelings than about time management. When a task makes us feel anxious, bored, or unsure of ourselves, our brain looks for a quick way to escape those unpleasant emotions. Checking a phone or cleaning a desk gives us instant relief, so we choose those activities instead. The problem is that the relief does not last, and the task is still waiting for us. Later, we feel even more stressed and guilty. This means that making a better schedule alone may not solve the problem. Instead, we need to learn how to handle the uncomfortable feelings that a task brings.
question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: why lazy people have trouble managing their time
procrastination as a way of avoiding unpleasant feelings
the importance of making a detailed daily schedule
the negative effects of smartphones on students' grades
explain_ko: 미루기는 게으름이 아니라 불쾌한 감정을 피하려는 행동이라는 글. 일정 짜기만으로는 해결되지 않는다고 했으므로 일정표 선택지는 오답.

passage: The ocean may seem like a quiet place, but it is getting louder every year. Large ships, underwater construction, and machines that search for oil all produce loud sounds under the sea. For humans, this noise may not seem serious. For whales and dolphins, however, it can be a big problem. These animals depend on sound to find food, communicate with each other, and travel long distances. Because sound travels far in water, the noise from a single ship can spread over many kilometers. When the ocean is too noisy, whales may lose contact with their groups or fail to find their food. Some even change their travel routes to escape the noise. Scientists warn that we must reduce underwater noise to protect these animals.
question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: ways to build quieter ships for passengers
the growing demand for oil under the sea
the harmful effects of ocean noise on sea animals
how whales use songs to attract their partners
explain_ko: 배·공사·석유 탐사 소음이 소리에 의존하는 고래·돌고래에게 해를 준다는 내용. 석유 탐사는 소음원의 예일 뿐.

passage: Did you know that the color of your plate can change how much you eat? In one experiment, researchers served pasta with white cream sauce to two groups of people. One group got the pasta on white plates, and the other group got it on red plates. The people who used white plates served themselves much more than the others. Why did this happen? When food and plate are similar in color, it is hard for our eyes to see how much food is on the plate. As a result, we tend to serve and eat larger amounts. On the other hand, a strong color contrast makes the amount of food stand out clearly. So if you want to eat less, try choosing plates that are a different color from your food.
question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Can Plate Color Control How Much We Eat?
How to Set a Beautiful Dinner Table
Why Red Is the Most Popular Food Color
Pasta: A Healthy Choice for Dinner
explain_ko: 접시와 음식의 색 대비가 먹는 양에 영향을 준다는 실험 글. 빨간 접시는 실험 조건일 뿐 빨간색의 인기와는 무관.

passage: Today, we think of umbrellas as tools that keep us dry in the rain. Surprisingly, however, the first umbrellas had nothing to do with rain. Thousands of years ago in hot countries such as Egypt and China, people used them to block the strong sunlight. The word "umbrella" itself comes from a Latin word meaning "shade." In those days, umbrellas were also a symbol of power, and often only kings and nobles were allowed to carry them. It was much later that people began to make them waterproof by covering them with oil or wax. Even then, many Europeans thought that carrying one in the rain was strange. It took many years before the umbrella became the everyday rain tool we know today.
question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How to Choose the Right Umbrella
From Sunshade to Rain Guard: The Umbrella's Story
explain_ko: 햇빛 가리개로 시작해 권력의 상징을 거쳐 비 가리개가 된 우산의 역사. 방수 처리는 변화의 한 단계일 뿐.

passage:
Coral reefs are often called the rainforests of the sea because so many living things depend on them. Their bright colors come from tiny algae that live inside the coral.

(A) This is called coral bleaching. A bleached coral is not dead yet, but if the water stays hot for too long, it will starve. That is why rising ocean temperatures are such a serious threat to reefs.

(B) These algae and the coral help each other. The algae make food from sunlight and share it with the coral, and in return, the coral gives them a safe home.

(C) When the ocean water becomes too warm, however, this partnership breaks down. The stressed coral pushes the algae out, and without them, it turns completely white.
question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: algae 소개 → 서로 돕는 관계(B) → this partnership 이 깨져 하얗게 됨(C) → 이를 백화 현상이라 함(A).

passage:
A caterpillar and a butterfly look completely different, but they are actually the same animal at different stages of its life. The change happens in a few clear steps.

(A) When it is big enough, the caterpillar hangs from a branch and forms a hard shell around itself. This is called a chrysalis. Inside it, the caterpillar's body breaks down and is slowly rebuilt into something new.

(B) After about two weeks, the shell splits open, and a butterfly climbs out. At first, its wings are soft and wet, so it rests in the sun until they dry. Then it flies away to look for flowers.

(C) First, a tiny caterpillar comes out of an egg on a leaf. It eats almost all day long and grows very quickly. In fact, it grows so fast that it has to change its skin several times.
question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: (C) 먼저(First) 알에서 애벌레가 나와 빨리 자람 → (A) 충분히 자라면(big enough) 번데기를 만듦 → (B) 약 2주 뒤 그 껍질(the shell)이 열리고 나비가 나옴.

passage: Owls hunt mostly at night, and they are famous for flying almost without a sound. This silence helps them catch mice that would run away at the smallest noise. ( ① ) When most birds flap their wings, the air rushes over the hard edges of their feathers and makes a whooshing noise. ( ② ) An owl's feathers, however, are different. ( ③ ) Behind these combs, the rest of the feather is soft and fuzzy like velvet, which takes in the little sound that is left. ( ④ ) Engineers have studied these feathers closely. By copying the comb-like edges, they have designed quieter fans for computers and quieter parts for high-speed trains. In this way, a hunter of the night is helping to make our daily lives a little more peaceful.
question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

The front edge of each wing feather has tiny points, like the teeth of a comb, which break the rushing air into smaller, quieter streams.
explain_ko: '올빼미 깃털은 다르다' 뒤에 그 차이(빗살 같은 앞쪽 가장자리)가 나와야, 다음 문장의 these combs가 그것을 가리킬 수 있다.

passage: When you feel cold or watch a scary movie, small bumps may suddenly appear on your arms. We call them goosebumps. ( ① ) Each hair on your skin has a tiny muscle attached to it. ( ② ) When these muscles tighten, the hairs stand up, and the skin around them rises into small bumps. For animals with thick fur, this is very useful. ( ③ ) When a cat is cold, its raised fur traps a layer of warm air near its body. When it is scared, its fur stands up and makes it look bigger to an enemy. ( ④ ) Humans, however, have lost most of their body hair, so goosebumps no longer keep us warm or make us look scary. They are simply a leftover from the distant past, a small sign that our bodies still react like those of our furry ancestors.
question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

The name comes from the skin of a goose, which looks just like this after its feathers are removed.
explain_ko: 주어진 문장은 goosebumps라는 이름의 유래를 설명하므로, 그 이름을 처음 말한 We call them goosebumps 바로 뒤에 와야 한다. 뒤쪽은 털 근육의 원리를 설명하는 흐름이다.

passage: Long ago, Indigenous farmers in parts of North America grew corn, beans, and squash together in the same small hill of soil. At first, this may look messy, but each plant helps the others. The corn grows tall and straight, so the bean plants can climb up its stalk to reach the sunlight. The beans, in turn, add nitrogen to the soil, a nutrient that corn needs to grow well. Meanwhile, the squash spreads its large leaves across the ground. These leaves shade the soil, keep it moist, and stop weeds from growing. Their prickly stems also keep some hungry animals away. Growing these three crops together often produces more food than growing each one alone. Today, some gardeners are trying this old method again. It shows them that _____.
question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: tall plants always win the fight for sunlight
each crop grows best in a field of its own
different plants can help one another grow
weeds are the biggest problem for farmers
explain_ko: 옥수수는 콩의 지지대, 콩은 흙에 양분, 호박은 그늘과 수분을 주어 셋을 함께 심으면 더 많이 수확한다는 글이므로 '서로 다른 식물이 서로의 성장을 도울 수 있다'.

passage: Social media makes it easy to compare ourselves with others. We see friends winning prizes, traveling to amazing places, or getting better grades, and we suddenly feel that we are falling behind. However, such comparisons are rarely fair. We are comparing our everyday lives to the best moments that others choose to share. A healthier way to measure our growth is _____. Ask yourself whether you are a little better than you were a month ago. Maybe you can now run a bit farther, or understand a math idea that once confused you. Focusing on your own progress helps you stay motivated and makes you proud of small steps. After all, the only race you are really running is your own.
question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: comparing yourself with your past self
sharing your best moments on social media
setting the same goals as your friends
explain_ko: 빈칸 뒤 '한 달 전보다 나아졌는지 물어보라'가 단서. 남과 비교하는 선택지는 모두 글이 비판하는 쪽.

passage: Is there a better way to study than simply reading a textbook again and again? In an experiment, students were divided into two groups and asked to study the same short article about the solar system. The first group was told that they would take a test on the material later. The second group was told that they would have to teach the material to other students. In the end, neither group actually taught anyone; both groups simply took the same test. Interestingly, the students who expected to teach scored noticeably higher. They remembered more facts and understood the main ideas better. The researchers explained that when people prepare to explain something to others, they organize the information more clearly and focus on the key points. In other words, simply thinking like a teacher changes the way we learn.
question:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Students who studied with the plan of (A) _____ the material to others were able to (B) _____ it better than those who only prepared for a test.
explain_ko: 가르칠 것을 예상한(설명할 계획) 학생들이 정보를 더 잘 정리해 시험 점수가 높았음 → explaining / understand.

passage: Most liquids become heavier when they freeze into a solid. Water, however, is different. When water freezes, its tiny parts move into a pattern with more empty space between them. As a result, ice is lighter than the same amount of liquid water, so it floats. This simple fact is very important for life on Earth. In winter, a lake starts to freeze at the top, not at the bottom. The layer of ice on the surface works like a blanket. It keeps the cold air away from the water below, so the deeper water stays liquid all winter. Fish and other animals can live safely under the ice until spring comes. If ice sank, lakes would freeze from the bottom up, and many of these animals could not survive.
question:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Because ice is (A) _____ than liquid water, it stays on the surface of a lake and helps the water below stay (B) _____.
explain_ko: 얼음은 같은 양의 물보다 가벼워 떠오르고(A: lighter), 수면의 얼음층이 담요처럼 아래 물을 액체 상태로 지켜 준다(B: liquid).

passage:
W: Kevin, the school art exhibition opens tomorrow. Is everything ready?
M: Almost. We hung all the paintings on the walls this morning.
W: Great. What about the name cards for each painting?
M: Hannah printed them out yesterday, and I put them up next to the paintings.
W: Good. Did you check the lights? Some of them weren't working last week.
M: Yes, the school repairman fixed them this afternoon.
W: Wonderful. Oh, we still need to set up the guest book at the entrance.
M: Don't worry. I'll bring a table from the classroom and set it up right now.
W: Thanks. Then I'll make a sign for the entrance.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 할 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 남자는 교실에서 탁자를 가져와 입구에 방명록을 설치하겠다고 했다. 이름표 출력은 Hannah가 이미 했고, 안내판은 여자가 만들 일이다.

passage:
M: Lisa, what are you reading?
W: It's a flyer for a coding camp for teenagers. I'm thinking of joining.
M: Sounds interesting. When is it?
W: It's during winter vacation, from January eighth to the twelfth.
M: Where is it held?
W: At the Hillside University computer lab. University students will teach us how to make simple games.
M: Cool. How many students can join?
W: Only thirty students. So I have to hurry.
M: Do you need to know anything about coding before you join?
W: No. Beginners are welcome.
M: How can you sign up?
W: I need to fill out an online form and send it by this Friday.
question: 대화를 듣고, 코딩 캠프에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 기간(1월 8일~12일), 장소(대학 컴퓨터실), 인원(30명), 신청 방법은 언급됐지만 참가비는 나오지 않았다.

passage: W: Hello, runners! Are you ready for a special run under the stars? The third Moonlight Night Run will take place on Saturday, September twenty-first, at Lakeside Park. The race will begin at eight in the evening. There are two courses, five kilometers and ten kilometers. Anyone who is twelve or older can join. All runners will receive a T-shirt that shines in the dark and a medal at the finish line. The registration fee is twenty dollars, and all the money will be used to plant trees in the park. You can register on our website until September tenth.
question: 다음을 듣고, Moonlight Night Run에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
choices: 참가 신청은 행사 당일 현장에서만 할 수 있다.
참가비는 공원에 나무를 심는 데 쓰인다.
explain_ko: 9월 10일까지 웹사이트에서 신청한다고 했으므로 현장 신청만 가능하다는 것은 일치하지 않는다.

passage:
M: Hi, Grace. Are you going anywhere for the holiday?
W: Yes. My family is visiting my grandparents in the countryside for four days.
M: Sounds fun. When are you leaving?
W: Tomorrow morning. But I have a problem. Nobody will be home to take care of my turtle.
M: Can't you take it with you?
W: It's a long drive, and turtles get stressed easily. Actually, I was going to ask you for a favor.
M: Sure. What is it?
W: Could you keep my turtle at your house while I'm away? I'll bring its tank and food tonight.
M: No problem. My little brother will love it.
W: Thanks. I'll write down how much food to give it.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 남자에게 부탁한 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 집을 비우는 동안 거북을 남자의 집에서 맡아 달라고 부탁했다. 수조와 먹이는 여자가 직접 가져간다고 했다.

passage: M: Good afternoon, students. This is your vice principal. As you know, the level of fine dust in the air is very high today. Breathing in fine dust can cause coughing and make your eyes itchy. So all outdoor activities, including this afternoon's soccer game, have been canceled for the rest of the day. Physical education classes will be held in the gym instead. When you go home, please wear a mask, and wash your hands and face as soon as you get home. We will let you know when outdoor activities can start again. Thank you.
question: 다음을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 미세먼지로 인한 야외 활동 취소를 알리려고
explain_ko: 미세먼지가 심해 오늘 오후 축구 경기를 포함한 야외 활동을 모두 취소한다는 방송이다. 마스크는 하굣길 당부로 짧게 나올 뿐이다.

passage: W: Hello, listeners. This is Rachel Brown with Money Talk for Teens. Have you ever bought something just because it was on sale, and then never used it? Many people do this. Sales make us feel that we are saving money, but actually we are spending money on things we don't need. Before you buy something on sale, ask yourself one simple question. Would I buy this if it weren't on sale? If the answer is no, don't buy it. This question can help you save a lot of money. Remember, a good deal is only good when you really need the item.
question: 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 할인 상품이라도 정말 필요한지 따져 보고 사야 한다.
할인 기간을 잘 이용하면 돈을 아낄 수 있다.
여러 가게의 가격을 비교한 뒤 사야 한다.
explain_ko: 할인 중이 아니어도 살 물건인지 스스로 물어보고, 필요할 때만 사라는 것이 요지다. 할인을 이용해 돈을 아끼라는 말은 오히려 반대 내용이다.

passage:
M: Hi, Olivia. What are these small pots?
W: Hi, Ethan. They're plants for my room. I just bought them at the flower shop.
M: Why did you buy so many?
W: I read an article about indoor plants. It said taking care of plants can reduce stress.
M: Really? How does that work?
W: When you water plants and watch them grow, you feel calm. Also, green colors are relaxing for your eyes.
M: I've been really stressed about exams lately.
W: Then you should get one, too. I think growing plants is a good way to deal with stress.
M: Maybe I'll give it a try.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 식물은 꽃집에서 직접 보고 사는 것이 좋다.
식물을 기르는 것은 스트레스를 줄이는 데 도움이 된다.
explain_ko: 식물을 돌보면 마음이 차분해져 스트레스를 줄일 수 있다는 것이 여자의 의견이다. 초록색이 눈을 편하게 해 준다고 했을 뿐 시력이 좋아진다고 하지 않았다.

passage:
W: Hi, Alex. How was your basketball tournament?
M: Not good. We lost in the first round.
W: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. What happened?
M: The other team was really strong. And I missed two easy shots at the end of the game.
W: That must have been hard.
M: Yeah. I think we lost because of me. Maybe I should quit the team.
W: Don't say that. Everyone makes mistakes. You practiced harder than anyone this year.
M: But I let my teammates down.
W: Your teammates don't think so. Remember, even the best players miss shots. You'll do better next time.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말의 의도로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 팀을 그만두겠다며 자책하는 남자에게 최고의 선수도 실수한다며 다음엔 잘할 거라고 힘을 북돋우고 있다.

passage:
M: Hi, Sarah. What are you doing this weekend?
W: I'm going to join a beach clean-up at Sunset Beach on Saturday.
M: A beach clean-up? What do you do there?
W: We pick up trash on the beach, like plastic bottles and fishing lines. Last time, we collected more than fifty bags.
M: Wow, that's a lot. Is it hard work?
W: A little, but it feels great to see the clean beach afterward. And sea animals can be safer.
M: That sounds meaningful. I've always wanted to do something for the environment.
W: Then why don't you come with me? The group is always looking for more volunteers.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 대한 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: You're right. Plastic bottles can be recycled.
I'd love to. What time should I meet you?
Sorry, I don't like swimming in the sea.
Really? I didn't know you lived near the beach.
explain_ko: 환경을 위해 무언가 하고 싶었다는 남자에게 함께 가자고 제안했으므로 수락하며 만날 시간을 묻는 것이 알맞다. 수영 이야기는 해변 청소와 관계없다.

passage:
W: Jake, what happened to your phone? The screen is cracked.
M: I dropped it on the stairs this morning. Now the touch screen doesn't work well.
W: That's too bad. Are you going to buy a new one?
M: I don't think so. I bought this phone only six months ago.
W: Then you should get it repaired. There's a repair shop near the subway station.
M: How much does it cost to fix a screen?
W: I'm not sure, but it's usually cheaper than buying a new phone. My sister had the same problem last month.
M: Really? Where did she get it fixed?
W: At the shop I just told you about. She said the staff were kind, and it took only an hour.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 대한 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Then I'll buy the same phone as your sister's.
Sorry, but I don't know where your sister lives.
Great. I'll go there after school today.
Really? I dropped my phone on the stairs, too.
explain_ko: 누나가 친절하고 빠르게 고친 가게를 알려 주었으므로 오늘 방과 후에 가 보겠다는 답이 알맞다. 새 휴대 전화를 사겠다는 말은 앞의 흐름과 맞지 않는다.

passage:
M: Amy, do you have any plans for Sunday?
W: Not really. Why?
M: There's a special exhibition about life in the Middle Ages at the city museum. Do you want to go with me?
W: That sounds interesting. What can we see there?
M: They have old maps, clothes, and even the tools people used for printing books.
W: Wow, I'm doing a history project on printing. It would be really helpful.
M: Great. The museum opens at ten, and there's a free guided tour at eleven.
W: Then let's join the tour. How about meeting at the museum at half past ten?
M: Sounds good. But the museum is very popular on weekends. Should we book the tickets online in advance?
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 대한 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Good idea. I'll check the website right now.
Sure. The guided tour starts at eleven.
No, I've never been to that museum.
Yes. I finished my history project yesterday.
explain_ko: 주말에 붐비니 표를 미리 온라인으로 예매하자는 제안에 지금 웹사이트를 확인하겠다고 답하는 것이 알맞다. 투어 시각은 이미 나온 정보를 되풀이한 것이다.

passage:
M: Jenny, you look upset. Is something wrong?
W: It's about our group project. One of my group members, Chris, hasn't done anything.
M: Really? Did you talk to him about it?
W: Not yet. I don't want to fight with him.
M: I understand, but if you don't tell him, the problem won't be solved.
W: You're right. But what if he gets angry?
M: Just tell him calmly how you feel. Maybe he doesn't know what to do. You could also give him a specific task, like finding pictures for the slides.
W: That's a good point. He's good at design.
M: See? He might be happy to help if you ask him nicely.
question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 대한 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: I'm sorry. I didn't know you were angry.
Thanks. I'll find some pictures for your slides.
Right. Chris and I had a big fight yesterday.
Okay. I'll talk to him at lunch tomorrow.
explain_ko: Chris에게 차분히 부탁해 보라는 조언을 받아들여 내일 이야기해 보겠다고 답하는 것이 알맞다. 어제 크게 싸웠다는 말은 아직 말도 못 했다는 앞 내용과 맞지 않는다.

passage: M: Ryan and Daniel are members of the school soccer team. The final match of the season is next week, and Daniel is one of the best players on the team. During practice yesterday, Daniel hurt his ankle. The doctor told him to rest for at least two weeks. However, Daniel doesn't want to miss the final match, so he keeps coming to practice and running on his hurt ankle. Ryan, the team captain, is worried that Daniel's ankle might get worse. He wants to tell Daniel that his health is more important than one match. In this situation, what would Ryan most likely say to Daniel?
question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Ryan이 Daniel에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: We can't win the final match without you.
You should rest your ankle. Your health comes first.
Let's practice harder to win the match.
Why didn't you tell me you were hurt?
explain_ko: Ryan은 경기보다 건강이 중요하니 발목을 쉬게 하라고 말하고 싶어 한다. 너 없이는 이길 수 없다는 말은 오히려 무리하게 만드는 말이다.

passage: W: Emily goes to a stationery store to buy some pens and a notebook. The total comes to seven dollars, and she gives the clerk a twenty-dollar bill. The store is crowded, and the clerk is very busy with many customers. He quickly hands her only three dollars in change. Emily is about to leave, but she counts the money at the door. She realizes that she should have received thirteen dollars. She wants to politely tell the clerk about his mistake. In this situation, what would Emily most likely say to the clerk?
question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Emily가 점원에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Excuse me, I think you gave me the wrong change.
Excuse me, can I get a discount on these pens?
Excuse me, can I pay with a credit card?
Excuse me, I'd like to exchange this notebook.
explain_ko: 13달러를 받아야 하는데 3달러만 받았으므로 거스름돈이 잘못됐다고 정중히 알리는 말이 알맞다. 할인·교환·카드 결제는 상황과 관계없다.

passage: M: Kevin is having lunch at a restaurant with his friends. He is allergic to nuts, so he always checks the menu carefully. When he orders a chicken salad, he asks the waiter to leave out the nuts. The waiter writes it down and says it's no problem. However, when the salad arrives, Kevin sees small pieces of nuts on top. He knows that even a few nuts could make him very sick. He doesn't want to be rude, but he can't eat the salad. So he wants to ask the waiter politely for a new salad without nuts. In this situation, what would Kevin most likely say to the waiter?
question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Kevin이 종업원에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Excuse me, how long does it take to make the salad?
Excuse me, could you bring me some more nuts?
Excuse me, can I have the bill, please?
Excuse me, could I get a new salad without nuts, please?
explain_ko: 견과류 알레르기가 있는데 샐러드에 견과류가 올라와서 정중히 새 샐러드를 부탁하는 상황이다. 계산서를 달라는 말은 문제를 해결하지 못한다.

passage: W: Olivia and Henry are partners in science class. Today, they are doing an experiment with chemicals that can hurt people's eyes. Before the experiment, the teacher told everyone to wear safety glasses. Olivia puts on her glasses, but Henry leaves his on the desk because he says they are uncomfortable. When Henry starts to pour the chemicals into a glass tube, Olivia gets worried. She remembers the teacher's warning that even a small drop can be dangerous. She wants Henry to protect his eyes before he goes on. In this situation, what would Olivia most likely say to Henry?
question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Olivia가 Henry에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: Let's ask the teacher to do the experiment for us.
I think we should write down the results now.
Wait! You should put on your safety glasses first.
Can you pour the chemicals more slowly?
explain_ko: 눈을 다칠 수 있는 약품을 다루는데 보안경을 쓰지 않은 Henry에게 먼저 보안경을 쓰라고 말하는 것이 알맞다. 천천히 부으라는 말은 눈 보호와 관계없다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
rely
explain_ko: rely on 형태로 쓰여 '의존하다'라는 뜻이다. 나머지는 각각 compare, deliver, refuse에 해당하는 뜻이라 오답이다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
She worked hard to _____ a scholarship for university.
explain_ko: 장학금을 얻으려 노력했다는 문맥이므로 '얻다'라는 뜻의 obtain이 알맞다. refuse(거절하다), waste(낭비하다), ignore(무시하다)는 문맥상 어색하다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
as much as is needed for a particular purpose; enough
explain_ko: '필요한 만큼의, 충분한'이라는 뜻의 풀이이므로 sufficient가 정답이다. scarce(부족한)는 반대 의미다.

question:
문장 속 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The manager gave a [brief] summary of the meeting before everyone left.
explain_ko: brief는 '짧은'이라는 뜻이므로 유의어는 short이다. lengthy는 반대되는 뜻이고 나머지는 의미가 다르다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
emphasize
explain_ko: emphasize는 '강조하다'라는 뜻이다. hide, doubt, compare와 혼동하지 않도록 한다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
In his _____ job, he worked as a graphic designer for five years.
explain_ko: 다섯 해 동안 일했던 과거의 직장을 가리키므로 '이전의'라는 뜻의 previous가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
large or great in amount, extent, or degree
explain_ko: '상당한'이라는 뜻의 풀이이므로 considerable이 정답이다. tiny는 정반대 의미다.

question:
문장 속 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The company promised an [immediate] refund after the product broke down.
explain_ko: immediate는 '즉각적인'이라는 뜻이므로 instant가 가장 비슷하다. delayed는 반대되는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
distinguish
explain_ko: distinguish는 '구별하다'라는 뜻이다. confuse(혼동하다)와 반대되는 의미이므로 헷갈리지 않도록 한다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Heavy traffic jams often _____ during the holiday season.
explain_ko: 명절 기간에 교통 체증이 '발생한다'는 문맥이므로 occur가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
unwilling and hesitant to do something
explain_ko: '꺼리는, 마지못한'이라는 뜻이므로 reluctant가 정답이다. eager는 정반대 의미다.

question:
문장 속 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The airline charged an [additional] fee for the extra luggage.
explain_ko: additional은 '추가의'라는 뜻이므로 extra가 가장 비슷하다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
evaluate
explain_ko: evaluate는 가치나 수준을 '평가하다'라는 뜻이다. suggest(제안하다)·adapt(적응하다)와 구별한다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
She has a _____ interest in ancient history rather than modern events.
explain_ko: 고대 역사'만' 특별히 관심 있다는 문맥이므로 '특정한'이라는 뜻의 particular가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
relating to a city or densely populated area
explain_ko: '도시의'라는 뜻이므로 urban이 정답이다. rural은 반대되는 '시골의'라는 뜻이다.

question:
문장 속 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
Getting enough sleep is [crucial] for teenagers' growth and health.
explain_ko: crucial은 '매우 중요한, 결정적인'이라는 뜻이므로 vital이 가장 비슷하다. minor·optional은 반대 의미다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
The number of students who use the new library _____ increasing every month.
explain_ko: 주어의 핵은 The number(단수)이므로 is. students에 끌려 are를 고르기 쉽다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: The keys to the storage room was left on the teacher's desk.
Each of the players has a different role on the team.
What the scientists discovered in the cave surprises many people.
Walking in the park every morning helps me clear my mind.
explain_ko: 주어의 핵이 The keys(복수)이므로 were가 맞다. 동명사구·Each of·What절 주어는 단수 동사로 모두 맞다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
It is difficult to find parking spaces near the stadium.
= Finding parking spaces near the stadium _____ difficult.

passage: The fog came in faster than Ethan had expected. Only twenty minutes earlier, he had been enjoying a clear view of the valley from the ridge, but now he could barely see the trees a few meters ahead. He stopped and looked around, trying to find the yellow paint marks that showed the trail. There were none. His phone had no signal, and the air was growing colder with every minute. His heart began to pound as he realized that he did not know which way he had come. He took a deep breath and walked slowly downhill, checking every rock and tree trunk. Then, through the gray mist, he noticed a small wooden sign with a yellow arrow on it. Beside it, he could hear the sound of the stream that ran past the parking lot. Ethan let out a long breath, and his shoulders finally relaxed as he followed the arrow back to his car.
question: 다음 글에 드러난 Ethan의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?

passage: Margaret Ellison was born in 1868 in a small fishing town on the northern coast of Scotland. As a child, she spent hours collecting shells and seaweed on the beach, and she kept careful notes about everything she found. Because women were not allowed to study at the local university at that time, she learned biology from books borrowed from a retired doctor. In 1895, she began to draw detailed pictures of sea plants, and her drawings were so accurate that scientists in London asked to use them in their textbooks. Later, she opened a small school for girls in her hometown, where she taught science free of charge. She never married, and she spent most of her savings on microscopes for her students. Ellison published her only book, a guide to the seaweeds of Scotland, when she was sixty-two years old. She died in 1941, and the school she founded still operates today.
question: Margaret Ellison에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

passage: Every morning, millions of teenagers drag themselves out of bed before sunrise and sit in their first class half asleep. Many adults assume that these students are simply lazy or stay up too late playing games. However, research on sleep shows that during adolescence, the body's internal clock naturally shifts later. This means that most teenagers cannot fall asleep easily before eleven o'clock at night, no matter how hard they try. When school begins at eight, they are forced to wake up in the middle of their natural sleep cycle. The result is not only tired faces in the classroom but also poorer memory, weaker concentration, and a higher risk of car accidents among teenage drivers. Some schools that moved their starting time to nine have reported better attendance and higher grades. If we truly care about students' learning and safety, schools must start later in the morning so that teenagers can get the sleep their bodies need.
question: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 청소년은 밤늦게 게임을 하는 습관을 고쳐야 한다.
청소년 운전자에 대한 안전 교육을 강화해야 한다.

passage: Many students believe that the best way to finish a difficult task is to work on it for hours without stopping. They feel guilty whenever they take a break, as if resting were a sign of weakness. Yet our brains are not built to focus on one thing for a very long time. After about an hour of continuous effort, attention begins to drift, and we start making careless mistakes without noticing them. A short break of five to ten minutes can reverse this decline. Standing up, stretching, or looking out the window gives the brain a chance to recover its energy. When we return to the task, we often see the problem from a fresh angle and find solutions that we missed before. In other words, stepping away from our work for a moment is not wasted time. It is a practical strategy that helps us keep our minds sharp and use our study time more wisely.
question: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

passage: Hummingbirds live life at an extraordinary pace. Their wings can beat dozens of times per second, and their hearts may race at more than a thousand beats per minute while they fly. To support this activity, they must visit hundreds of flowers a day, drinking nectar almost constantly. This creates a serious danger at night, when they cannot feed. A bird that burns energy so quickly could easily starve before morning, especially on cold nights. Hummingbirds solve this problem by entering a deep, sleep-like state. Their body temperature drops sharply, their heartbeat slows to a small fraction of its normal rate, and their breathing becomes so slow that they may appear to be dead. In this state, they use only a tiny amount of the energy they would otherwise need. When the sun rises, they gradually warm their bodies again by shivering, and within an hour they are ready to start feeding.
question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: why hummingbirds prefer flowers with sweet nectar
how hummingbirds save energy during the night
the danger that cold weather poses to flowers
how fast hummingbirds can fly during migration
explain_ko: 에너지를 빨리 쓰는 벌새가 먹이를 먹지 못하는 밤에 체온·심박을 크게 낮춰 에너지를 아끼는 방법을 설명하므로 '벌새가 밤에 에너지를 아끼는 방법'이 주제다.

passage: For centuries, lighthouses guided ships with the light of burning wood, candles, or oil lamps. The problem was that most of this light spread out in every direction and was wasted, so sailors could see it only from a short distance. Placing a large glass lens in front of the flame could focus the light, but such a lens had to be extremely thick and heavy, and it absorbed much of the light that passed through it. In the early nineteenth century, a French scientist found a clever solution. He divided the lens into a series of thin rings of glass, each shaped to bend the light in the right direction. Together, the rings worked like one giant lens but used only a small portion of the glass. Lighthouses with this new design could be seen from more than thirty kilometers away, giving ships far more time to steer clear of dangerous rocks.
question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Rings of Glass: A Brighter Light for Lighthouses
The Dangers of Oil Lamps at Sea
How Glass Is Made from Sand
explain_ko: 두껍고 무거운 렌즈 대신 얇은 유리 고리를 이어 붙여 등대 불빛을 멀리 보내게 된 발명을 다루므로 '유리 고리: 등대를 더 밝게 한 빛'이 알맞다.

passage: Today, it is hard to imagine a dinner table without forks, but this tool was not always welcome in Europe. For centuries, most Europeans ate with a knife and their fingers, and they considered this perfectly polite. ① When forks first arrived from the Byzantine Empire in the eleventh century, many people saw them as a strange and unnecessary luxury. ② Some religious leaders even criticized the fork, arguing that food was a gift from God and should be touched only by human hands. ③ Silver is a soft metal, so craftsmen have used it to make jewelry and coins for thousands of years. ④ Only gradually, as ideas about cleanliness and good manners changed, did the fork spread from wealthy families in Italy to ordinary households across the continent. By the eighteenth century, in many parts of Europe, eating without a fork had become a sign of poor manners rather than normal behavior.

passage:
Before the nineteenth century, a doctor who wanted to listen to a patient's heart had only one option: to press an ear directly against the patient's chest.

(A) One day in 1816, a French doctor facing this situation rolled a few sheets of paper into a tight tube and placed one end on the patient's chest. To his surprise, the heartbeat sounded much louder and clearer than it ever had through his ear alone.

(B) He soon replaced the paper with a hollow wooden tube, and later inventors added flexible rubber tubes and a piece for each ear. The basic idea, however, remains the same in the instrument that hangs around doctors' necks today.

(C) This method had obvious problems. It was uncomfortable and embarrassing for both people, and the sounds were often too faint to be useful, especially when the patient had a thick layer of clothing or fat.
question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: (C) 귀를 가슴에 대는 이 방법(This method)의 문제 → (A) 이런 상황에서 한 의사가 종이를 말아 대어 보니 소리가 또렷함 → (B) 그(He)가 종이를 나무 관으로 바꾸고, 뒤에 고무관·양쪽 귀꽂이가 더해져 오늘의 청진기가 됨.

passage: Volcanoes are usually thought of as forces of destruction, and for good reason. ( ① ) When a volcano erupts, it can bury nearby farms under thick layers of hot ash, killing crops and forcing families to leave their land. ( ② ) Volcanic ash contains minerals such as potassium, magnesium, and phosphorus, which plants need in order to grow. ( ③ ) As rain and wind slowly break the ash down, these minerals are released into the ground, where the roots of plants can absorb them. ( ④ ) This is why farmers in many parts of the world have chosen to live in the shadow of active volcanoes despite the danger. They know that the land around a volcano can produce harvests far larger than those from ordinary soil. For them, the risk of an eruption is the price they pay for unusually fertile fields.
question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

explain_ko: 화산재가 농장을 덮는 파괴를 설명한 문장 바로 뒤에서 however 로 '그 재가 비옥한 흙이 된다'로 전환한 뒤, 재에 든 광물 설명이 이어져야 한다. 'the same ash that destroyed the fields'는 농장 파괴 문장 바로 뒤라야 자연스럽다.

passage:
Many marathon runners describe a moment, usually around the thirtieth kilometer, when their legs suddenly feel heavy and each step becomes a struggle.

(A) Once these stores run low, the body must rely mainly on fat for fuel. Fat contains plenty of energy, but the body turns it into usable fuel much more slowly, so the runner is forced to slow down no matter how determined he or she is.

(B) To avoid this, experienced runners eat meals rich in carbohydrates in the days before a race and take in sports drinks while running. In this way, they can delay the moment when their supply of glycogen runs out.

(C) Runners call this experience hitting the wall. It happens because the muscles depend heavily on a stored form of sugar called glycogen, and the body can hold only a limited amount of it.
question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 다리가 무거워지는 순간을 '벽에 부딪힘'이라 부르고 글리코겐 저장량이 한정되어 있다는 (C), 그 저장량(these stores)이 줄면 지방을 쓴다는 (A), 이를 피하는 방법 (B) 순서이다.

passage: Walk across almost any park or college campus, and you will notice narrow dirt paths cutting through the grass where no path was planned. Planners call them desire lines. They appear because people naturally choose the most direct or convenient route, and when enough of them walk the same way, the grass wears away. For many years, the usual response was to put up fences or signs telling people to stay on the paved paths. These efforts rarely worked for long. Some designers now take a different approach. When a new campus opens, they plant grass everywhere and wait several months to see where people actually walk. Only then do they pave the routes that have appeared. The result is a network of paths that people are happy to use, because it follows their real habits instead of fighting them. In a sense, these designers succeed by [letting the walkers draw the map].
question: 다음 글에서 [ ] 로 표시된 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

사람들이 실제로 다니는 길을 보고 그에 맞게 길을 설계하는 것

passage: Imagine that two stalls at a farmers' market are selling the same kind of strawberries at the same price. At the first stall, dozens of boxes are piled high on the table. At the second, only two boxes remain. Most shoppers, when asked which strawberries look more delicious, point to the second stall. The fruit is identical, so what makes the difference? The answer is that we tend to believe that things which are hard to get must be worth more. When something is in short supply, we assume that many other people must have wanted it, and this makes us want it too. Advertisers understand this tendency very well. That is why they use phrases such as limited edition or only three left in stock to push customers into buying quickly. In short, our judgment of an object's value is often shaped less by its actual quality than by its _____.
question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

passage: We usually think of forest fires as pure disasters, and many of them do cause terrible damage. In some forests, however, fire is a natural and even necessary event. Certain kinds of pine trees, for example, produce cones that are sealed shut with a thick, sticky resin. These cones can hang on the branches for years without opening. Only the intense heat of a fire melts the resin, allowing the cones to open and release their seeds. The timing is perfect for the young trees. The fire has burned away the older plants that would block the sunlight, and the ash left behind makes the soil rich in nutrients. When people put out every small fire for decades, such forests can actually suffer, because few new trees appear and dry wood builds up until a huge fire becomes unavoidable. For these trees, fire is not simply an enemy; they actually _____.
question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: drop their seeds early to avoid its heat
grow faster when fires are prevented
need people to plant their seeds by hand
depend on it to start their next generation

passage: Many people believe that complete silence is the best environment for creative work. However, a series of experiments suggests otherwise. Researchers asked participants to come up with new ideas for products while listening to background noise at different volumes. Some worked in near silence, some heard a moderate level of noise similar to that of a busy coffee shop, and others were exposed to very loud noise. The participants in the moderate-noise group produced the most original ideas. According to the researchers, a certain amount of noise slightly distracts the mind, which makes people think in a more abstract way instead of focusing narrowly on details. This broader way of thinking helps them connect ideas that seem unrelated. When the noise was too loud, however, the participants had trouble processing information, and their creativity dropped sharply.
question:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
A(n) (A) level of background noise can boost creativity by encouraging (B) thinking, while too much noise makes it harder to process information.
explain_ko: 커피숍 정도의 적당한(moderate) 소음이 추상적(abstract)으로 생각하게 해 창의성을 높였다. 세부에 좁게 집중하는 것은 반대 개념이므로 detailed 는 틀리고, 거의 조용한 조건은 효과가 덜했으므로 low 도 틀리다.

passage: M: Hello, listeners. This is Doctor Harris with Health Tips. These days, many students look at screens for hours to study or play games. You can also blink slowly a few times to keep your eyes wet. It only takes a moment, but it can protect your eyes for years. Remember, short and regular breaks are the key to healthy eyes.
