다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
inevitable
explain_ko: inevitable은 '피할 수 없는, 불가피한'이라는 뜻이다. optional(선택적인)과 반대되는 의미다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
The new design will _____ several features requested by users.
explain_ko: 사용자가 요청한 기능들을 '포함시킨다'는 문맥이므로 incorporate가 알맞다. eliminate는 반대되는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
having more than one possible meaning; unclear
explain_ko: '애매한, 모호한'이라는 뜻이므로 ambiguous가 정답이다. obvious와 precise는 반대되는 의미다.

question:
문장 속 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The company reported a [substantial] increase in profits this year.
explain_ko: substantial은 '상당한'이라는 뜻이므로 considerable이 가장 비슷하다. minor는 반대되는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
undermine
explain_ko: undermine은 '약화시키다'라는 뜻이다. strengthen(강화하다)과 반대되는 의미다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
The judge criticized the rule for being _____ rather than based on clear evidence.
explain_ko: 명확한 근거 없이 '제멋대로' 정해졌다고 비판하는 문맥이므로 arbitrary가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
real and authentic, not fake or pretended
explain_ko: '진짜의, 진실한'이라는 뜻이므로 genuine이 정답이다. fake는 정반대 의미다.

question:
문장 속 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
Her vacation happened to [coincide] with her sister's graduation ceremony.
explain_ko: coincide는 '동시에 일어나다, 겹치다'라는 뜻이므로 overlap이 가장 비슷하다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
deteriorate
explain_ko: deteriorate는 '악화되다'라는 뜻이다. recover(회복되다)와 반대되는 의미다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
The government decided to _____ more funds to public education.
explain_ko: 공교육에 자금을 '배분한다'는 문맥이므로 allocate가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
to suppose that something is true without proof
explain_ko: '증거 없이 추정하다'라는 뜻이므로 presume이 정답이다. confirm(확인하다)은 의미가 다르다.

question:
문장 속 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
His knowledge of the subject turned out to be quite [superficial].
explain_ko: superficial은 '피상적인'이라는 뜻이므로 shallow가 가장 비슷하다. thorough는 반대되는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
vulnerable
explain_ko: vulnerable은 '취약한, 상처받기 쉬운'이라는 뜻이다. strong(강력한)과 반대되는 의미다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
The detective offered a _____ explanation that matched all the evidence.
explain_ko: 모든 증거와 맞아떨어지는 '그럴듯한' 설명이라는 문맥이므로 plausible이 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
causing a lot of public disagreement or debate
explain_ko: '논란이 많은'이라는 뜻이므로 controversial이 정답이다. neutral(중립적인)은 의미가 다르다.

question:
문장 속 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
It took her a while to fully [comprehend] the complicated instructions.
explain_ko: comprehend는 '이해하다'라는 뜻이므로 understand가 가장 비슷하다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
If I had left home ten minutes earlier, I _____ the train.
explain_ko: If절이 had p.p.인 가정법 과거완료이고 과거 일에 대한 가정이므로 주절은 would have p.p.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: If it hadn't rained yesterday, we would have gone hiking.
If I knew about the party last week, I would have gone.
If he had taken the medicine last night, he would feel better now.
If she had studied harder, she would have passed the test.
explain_ko: last week의 일을 가정하므로 If절은 had known이어야 한다. 마지막 문장은 과거 가정+현재 결과의 혼합가정법으로 맞다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
As I didn't bring my umbrella, I got wet.
= If I _____ my umbrella, I wouldn't have gotten wet.
explain_ko: 과거 사실의 반대이므로 If절은 had p.p.(had brought). brought는 현재 사실 반대가 된다.

question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
내가 어젯밤에 잠을 충분히 잤다면, 지금 피곤하지 않을 텐데.
choices: If I had slept enough last night, I wouldn't be tired now.
If had I slept enough last night, I wouldn't be tired now.
If I had enough slept last night, I wouldn't be tired now.
If I had slept enough last night, I would be not tired now.
explain_ko: 과거 가정(had slept)+현재 결과(wouldn't be)의 혼합가정법. not은 조동사 would 바로 뒤에 온다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
He talks _____ he had traveled all over the world, but he has never left his country.
explain_ko: 사실과 다른 것을 마치 그런 것처럼 말하므로 as if + 가정법 과거완료. because는 뒤 내용(여행한 적 없음)과 모순된다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: But for your advice, I would have made a big mistake.
I wish I can speak French fluently.
She looks as if she had seen a ghost.
I wish I had visited my grandmother more often.
explain_ko: I wish 뒤 현재 사실 반대는 가정법 과거이므로 could speak가 맞다. 나머지는 as if·But for·I wish가 바르게 쓰였다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Without the Internet, our lives would be very different.
= If it _____ for the Internet, our lives would be very different.
explain_ko: 주절이 would be(가정법 과거)이므로 If it were not for. had not been은 주절이 would have p.p.일 때 쓴다.

question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
내가 그 시험을 더 일찍 준비했더라면 좋았을 텐데.
choices: I wish I had prepared for the exam earlier.
I wish had I prepared for the exam earlier.
I wish I prepared had for the exam earlier.
I had wish I prepared for the exam earlier.
explain_ko: 과거 사실에 대한 아쉬움은 I wish + 주어 + had p.p. 순서.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
The ground is wet. It _____ rained last night.
explain_ko: 땅이 젖었다는 근거로 과거를 강하게 추측하므로 must have p.p. can't have는 근거와 반대되고 should have는 후회·유감이다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: She can't have written this letter; she was in the hospital then.
They might have missed the bus this morning.
You should have told me earlier; now it's too late.
He may have forgot his password again.
explain_ko: 조동사 + have 뒤에는 과거분사가 와야 하므로 forgotten이 맞다. 나머지 과거분사는 모두 바르다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
I'm sure that Tom left his bag in the classroom.
= Tom _____ left his bag in the classroom.
explain_ko: 과거 일에 대한 확신은 must have p.p. should have는 '했어야 했는데'라는 유감이라 뜻이 달라진다.

question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
너는 그렇게 많은 돈을 쓰지 말았어야 했다.
choices: You shouldn't so much money have spent.
You shouldn't have spent so much money.
You shouldn't spent have so much money.
You have shouldn't spent so much money.
explain_ko: '~하지 말았어야 했다'는 shouldn't + have + p.p. 순서.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
The fact _____ he apologized first shows that he is mature.
explain_ko: 빈칸 뒤가 완전한 문장이고 The fact의 내용을 설명하므로 동격 that. which·what은 불완전한 문장을 이끈다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Whether we will go camping depends on the weather.
There is a rumor that the school will build a new gym.
If he is telling the truth is not important to me.
I'm not sure if she will come to the meeting.
explain_ko: 주어 자리의 명사절은 if로 시작할 수 없어 Whether가 맞다. 목적어 자리의 if, 동격 that은 바르다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Did he lock the door? I don't remember.
= I don't remember _____ he locked the door.
explain_ko: 의문사 없는 의문문을 명사절로 바꾸면 whether(if). that은 확정된 사실이 되어 뜻이 달라진다.

question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
그녀가 그 대회에서 우승했다는 소식이 우리를 놀라게 했다.
choices: The news that she had won the contest surprised us.
The news that had she won the contest surprised us.
That the news she had won the contest surprised us.
The news she that had won the contest surprised us.
explain_ko: 동격 that절은 The news 바로 뒤에 that + 주어 + 동사 순서로 온다.

passage:
Dear Mr. Harrison,
I am a science teacher at Lincoln High School, and I am writing on behalf of our school's Young Engineers Club. Every spring, our club members spend several months designing small inventions that solve everyday problems, such as a shower timer that saves water or a backpack that charges a phone with solar energy. This year, we plan to hold our first public science fair on May 18 so that students can present their work to the local community. Unfortunately, our school budget does not cover the cost of display tables, electrical equipment, and printed materials for the event. As the owner of a hardware store that has served our town for decades, you have always shown a deep interest in young people's education. We would be truly honored if your store could sponsor the fair by providing some of the equipment we need. In return, we would gladly display your store's name on all of our posters and programs.
Sincerely,
Rachel Kim
question: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 포스터에 가게 광고를 싣는 비용을 문의하려고
학교 예산 부족 문제에 대한 해결책을 건의하려고
과학 박람회에 필요한 장비를 후원해 달라고 요청하려고
explain_ko: 예산이 부족하니 가게에서 장비를 제공해 박람회를 후원해 달라는 부탁이 목적이다. 포스터에 가게 이름을 싣는 것은 후원의 보답으로 제안한 것이다.

passage: For weeks, Leo had been counting the days until the meteor shower. According to the news, it would be the brightest one in nearly a decade, with as many as a hundred shooting stars an hour. He had borrowed his uncle's telescope, packed a bottle of hot chocolate, and convinced his father to drive him to a hill far from the city lights. As they set up their chairs in the darkness, Leo could hardly sit still, imagining the sky bursting with streaks of light. Around midnight, however, a thin layer of clouds began to spread from the west. At first he told himself it would pass, but within half an hour the whole sky had turned a dull gray. Not a single star was visible. Leo stared upward for a long time, then slowly folded his chair and put the telescope back in its case without saying a word.
question: 다음 글에 드러난 Leo의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 유성우를 기대하며 가만히 있지 못하다가(excited) 구름에 별이 가려져 말없이 짐을 싸므로(disappointed) 설렘 → 실망이다.

passage: The axolotl is a type of salamander that is found naturally in only one place in the world: a system of lakes and canals near Mexico City. Unlike most salamanders, which leave the water and live on land as adults, the axolotl usually spends its entire life underwater. It keeps many of the features it had when it was young, including the feathery gills that stick out from both sides of its head. Perhaps its most remarkable ability is that it can regrow lost body parts. If an axolotl loses a leg, a completely new one, with bones and muscles, will grow back over several weeks. Scientists study this ability closely, hoping it may someday help people recover from serious injuries. Sadly, the wild population has decreased sharply because of water pollution and the spread of the city. Today, the axolotl is far more common in laboratories and home aquariums than in its natural habitat.
question: axolotl에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 잃어버린 다리를 몇 주에 걸쳐 다시 자라게 할 수 있다.
수질 오염과 도시 확장으로 야생 개체 수가 크게 줄었다.
다 자라면 대부분의 도롱뇽처럼 물 밖 육지로 올라와 산다.
자연 상태에서는 멕시코시티 근처의 호수와 운하에서만 발견된다.
explain_ko: 대부분의 도롱뇽과 달리 axolotl 은 평생 물속에서 산다고 했으므로 육지로 올라온다는 설명은 틀리다.

passage:

When

question: Maple Hill River Clean-Up Day에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 14세 미만 어린이는 보호자와 함께 와야 한다.
참가한 학생은 봉사 시간 확인서를 받는다.
explain_ko: 'The event will be held even in light rain'이므로 약한 비에도 행사는 열린다. 보호자 동반, 장갑·봉투 제공, 봉사 확인서는 모두 일치.

passage: Before buying almost anything today, from a pair of headphones to a new backpack, most of us check the online reviews first. At first glance, this seems like a smart habit, since the experiences of hundreds of other customers should be more reliable than an advertisement. But reviews are far less trustworthy than they appear. Some sellers pay people to write glowing comments about their products, while others post negative reviews about their competitors. Even honest reviews can mislead us, because people who are extremely happy or extremely angry are much more likely to write one than those who are simply satisfied. As a result, the star rating often reflects the opinions of a small and unusual group. Rather than letting a number decide for us, we should read reviews with a critical eye, compare several sources, and, whenever possible, examine the product ourselves before we make a decision.
question: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 판매자는 거짓 리뷰를 작성하는 행위를 중단해야 한다.
온라인 리뷰를 그대로 믿지 말고 비판적으로 판단해야 한다.
제품을 살 때는 광고보다 별점을 우선 참고해야 한다.
소비자는 제품을 사용한 뒤 반드시 리뷰를 남겨야 한다.
explain_ko: 마지막 문장에서 숫자(별점)에 맡기지 말고 비판적으로 읽고 비교하라고 주장한다. 거짓 리뷰는 근거로 든 사례일 뿐 판매자에게 하는 주장은 아니다.

passage: Many people believe that the standard language they learn at school is the only correct form of their language, and that regional dialects are simply careless or broken versions of it. Linguists who study dialects have found otherwise. Every dialect follows its own consistent rules of pronunciation, vocabulary, and grammar, just as the standard form does. A sentence that sounds wrong to an outsider is often perfectly regular within the dialect, used in the same way by thousands of speakers. In fact, the standard language itself usually began as the dialect of one powerful region, such as the area around a capital city, and gained its status for political reasons rather than because it was more logical. Dialects also keep old words and expressions that have disappeared elsewhere. When we laugh at someone's way of speaking, then, we are not correcting a mistake but dismissing an orderly system of communication that deserves respect.
question: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 사투리는 고유한 규칙을 지닌 언어이므로 존중받아야 한다.
외국어를 배울 때는 지역별 발음 차이에 주의해야 한다.
표준어는 사투리보다 논리적이므로 학교에서 가르쳐야 한다.
사투리에 남은 옛말을 연구해 지역의 역사를 밝혀야 한다.
explain_ko: 사투리도 표준어처럼 일관된 규칙을 가진 언어 체계이므로 비웃지 말고 존중해야 한다는 글이다. 옛말 보존은 근거 중 하나일 뿐이고, 표준어가 더 논리적이라는 것은 글이 부정한 내용이다.

passage: Every spring and autumn, billions of birds travel thousands of kilometers between their breeding grounds and their winter homes. Many of these species fly at night, using the moon and stars to find their way. For millions of years, this system worked well, but the bright lights of modern cities have created a serious problem. When birds pass over a brightly lit area, they often become confused and begin circling the illuminated buildings instead of continuing their journey. Some crash into windows, while others waste so much energy that they are too weak to complete their migration. Researchers estimate that hundreds of millions of birds die this way each year in North America alone. In response, several cities have started programs asking the owners of tall buildings to turn off unnecessary lights during the busiest migration seasons. These simple actions have been shown to reduce the number of bird deaths significantly.
question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the difficulty of counting birds during migration seasons
the reasons tall buildings consume too much electricity
the harmful effects of artificial light on birds that migrate at night
the ways birds use the stars to choose their winter homes
explain_ko: 도시의 밝은 불빛이 밤에 이동하는 새들을 혼란에 빠뜨려 죽게 한다는 문제와 대책이 주제이다. 별을 이용한 길 찾기는 도입부 배경일 뿐이다.

passage: Most of the apps on your phone did not cost you a single cent. You can send messages, watch videos, and play games all day without paying anything. But the companies that create these apps spend enormous amounts of money on programmers, servers, and customer support, so they must earn money somehow. In most cases, they do it by collecting information about you. They record what you search for, which videos you watch, and even where you go, and then use this data to show you advertisements designed specifically for you. Some apps are also carefully designed to keep you scrolling as long as possible, because every extra minute you spend on the screen means more ads and more profit. In other words, you are paying after all, not with money but with your personal information and your attention. Understanding this hidden deal is the first step toward using technology more wisely.
question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: The Rising Cost of Smartphones for Teenagers
How to Design an App That Everyone Wants to Download
Why Advertisements Are Disappearing from the Internet

Suppose a store displays a jacket with a price tag that reads three hundred dollars, crossed out and replaced by one hundred fifty dollars.

(A) Most shoppers will feel that they are getting a great deal, even if they would never have paid one hundred fifty dollars for the same jacket had they seen that price alone. The original price makes the sale price seem reasonable by comparison.

(B) Once this anchor is set, all later numbers are judged in relation to it. Understanding this tendency can help consumers ask a simpler and more important question: is this item actually worth the money I am about to spend?

(C) This happens because of a mental shortcut called anchoring. When we make judgments about numbers, we rely heavily on the first figure we encounter, even when that figure has little to do with the real value of the item.

A brick must therefore be narrow enough to grip comfortably and light enough to lift thousands of times a day. passage: Why do some brilliant experts make poor teachers? One reason is that once we have mastered a skill, it becomes very difficult to remember what it was like not to know it. A professional pianist no longer thinks about where to place each finger, and an experienced programmer reads complicated code as easily as a newspaper. When such experts try to explain their field to beginners, they often skip important steps, use unfamiliar terms, and wonder why their students look confused. They are, in a sense, [standing on the roof and forgetting that they ever needed a ladder]. The basic steps that once took them months of effort now seem so obvious that they no longer notice them. The best teachers are those who make a conscious effort to return to the beginner's point of view, recalling their own early struggles and building the ladder again, one step at a time, for their students.

passage: In a forest, trees may look like independent individuals competing for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Beneath the ground, however, a very different picture appears. The roots of many trees are connected by thin threads of fungi that spread through the soil like an underground web. Through this network, trees can transfer sugar, water, and even chemical warning signals to one another. Studies have shown that large, old trees sometimes send nutrients to young trees growing in deep shade, where they cannot produce enough food on their own. When one tree is attacked by insects, neighboring trees may receive signals that help them prepare their defenses. The fungi also benefit, receiving sugar from the trees in exchange for helping them absorb minerals. passage: Modern airplanes are equipped with autopilot systems that can handle most of a flight without human help. These systems have made flying safer in many ways, since they never get tired or distracted. Yet safety experts have noticed an unexpected side effect. Because pilots now spend so little time actually controlling their aircraft, their manual flying skills can gradually weaken. When the automatic system suddenly fails, often in bad weather or during an emergency, pilots must take control in the most difficult conditions, exactly when their skills are least practiced. Similar patterns appear in everyday life. Drivers who depend on parking sensors may lose their sense of distance, and students who use spell checkers may stop noticing their own spelling mistakes. Likewise, people who always rely on navigation apps often struggle to find their way even in a familiar city when their phone battery dies. passage: Along many sandy coasts, strong winds constantly blow sand inland from the beach. For most plants, being buried under sand would mean death, but certain beach grasses actually grow better when this happens. When sand piles up around them, these grasses respond by sending new shoots upward and spreading their roots more widely. In fact, studies have found that the plants become weak and unhealthy in places where fresh sand no longer arrives. At the same time, the grasses shape their own surroundings. Their leaves slow down the wind, causing it to drop the sand it carries, and their long roots hold the growing pile in place. Over many years, this partnership between plant and sand can build dunes several meters high. These dunes protect the towns and farmland behind them from storm waves, which is why coastal managers often plant beach grass rather than build expensive sea walls.

explain_ko: 오늘 이웃에게 가서 이야기해 보라는 제안에 숙제 끝나고 찾아가겠다는 응답이 자연스러움. 자전거는 아직 돈을 모으는 중이고, 개는 이웃의 개.

passage:
W: Hello, Justin. How is Max doing today?
M: He's eating a little more, but he still doesn't want to go for walks.
W: Let me take a look. Hmm, his stomach is much better than last week.
M: Great. So can I give him his usual dog food again?
W: Not yet. His stomach is still weak, so keep giving him the soft food for one more week.
M: One more week? But he doesn't seem to like the soft food much.
W: I understand, but if you change his food too soon, he could get sick again.
M: Hmm, then is there anything I can do to help him eat better?
W: You can warm the soft food a little. Dogs love the smell of warm food. And please bring him back next Friday for a check-up.
question:
대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 대한 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Man: _____
choices: Great. I'll stop giving him the soft food then.
Don't worry. He loves going for long walks.
Thanks. I'll give him his usual food tonight.
Okay. I'll bring him back next Friday.
explain_ko: 다음 금요일에 검진받으러 다시 데려오라는 수의사의 말에 그러겠다는 응답이 자연스러움. 원래 사료는 아직 안 된다고 했고, 산책을 싫어한다고 했음.

passage: W: Lucas and Nora are classmates who take the same bus to school every morning. Recently, Nora has been late for the bus several times, so they both almost missed the first class. This morning, Lucas waited for her at the bus stop again, and they barely made it to school on time. Lucas found out that Nora often stays up late watching videos on her phone. He doesn't want to go to school without her, but he is worried that they will be late again. So he wants to suggest that Nora go to bed earlier so that she can get up on time. In this situation, what would Lucas most likely say to Nora?
question:
다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Lucas가 Nora에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Lucas: _____
choices: Can you recommend some fun videos to watch?
Let's take a taxi to school from tomorrow.
Why don't you go to bed earlier so you can wake up on time?
I'm sorry I was late for the bus this morning.
explain_ko: Lucas는 Nora에게 일찍 자서 제시간에 일어나라고 제안하려 함. 늦은 사람은 Nora이므로 Lucas가 사과하는 말은 어색함.

passage: M: Victor works at an outdoor equipment store. One day, a man named Mr. Hill comes in to buy a tent for his first family camping trip. He says they will camp at a campground near the city only a few times a year in summer. He picks up the most expensive tent in the store because it looks strong. Victor knows this tent is designed for climbers in snowy mountains, and it is heavy and hard to set up. He thinks a lighter tent that is easy to set up would be better for a beginner. So he wants to recommend a simpler tent that fits Mr. Hill's needs. In this situation, what would Victor most likely say to Mr. Hill?
question:
다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Victor가 Mr. Hill에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Victor: _____
choices: I think a simpler tent would be better for your family trips.
I'm afraid we're out of tents right now.
This tent is the best choice for snowy mountains.
You should also buy sleeping bags for your family.
explain_ko: Victor는 초보 가족 캠핑에는 가볍고 치기 쉬운 단순한 텐트를 권하려 함. 설산용이라는 말은 사실이지만 권하려는 내용이 아님.

passage: M: Good morning, class. Today, we can simply open the refrigerator to get cold food. But how did people keep food fresh in the past? Let's look at some ways. Long ago, people in cold regions cut large blocks of ice from frozen lakes in winter. They stored the ice in underground rooms covered with straw, and it lasted until summer. In Korea, people built stone houses to store ice. In hot, dry areas, people used clay pots. They put one pot inside a larger one and filled the space between them with wet sand. As the water dried, it cooled the food inside. Now, let's discuss which method was the most effective.
question: 다음을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: why ice melts faster in hot, dry areas
ways people kept food cold before refrigerators
how to store food safely in summer today
the history of the modern refrigerator
explain_ko: 얼음 창고, 석빙고, 젖은 모래를 넣은 겹 항아리 등 냉장고 이전의 음식 보관법을 소개함. 현대 냉장고의 역사는 다루지 않음.

passage: W: Hello, everyone. The New Year is celebrated in many different ways around the world. Today, I'll introduce some interesting traditions. In Spain, people eat twelve grapes at midnight, one for each ring of the clock. They believe it brings good luck for the twelve months ahead. In Denmark, people throw old plates at the doors of their friends and family. The more broken plates you find, the more friends you have. In Brazil, many people wear white clothes and jump over seven waves at the beach. And in Japan, people ring temple bells one hundred and eight times. Now, think about how your family celebrates the New Year.
question: 다음을 듣고, 언급된 나라가 아닌 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 스페인·덴마크·브라질·일본의 새해 풍습이 소개되었고 멕시코는 나오지 않음.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
inherent
explain_ko: inherent는 '내재된, 본래 가지고 있는'이라는 뜻이다. external(외부의)과 반대되는 의미다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
The scientist kept a _____ record of every experiment she conducted.
explain_ko: 모든 실험을 빠짐없이 기록했다는 문맥이므로 '꼼꼼한'이라는 뜻의 meticulous가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
to prove that a statement or theory is wrong
explain_ko: '반박하다'라는 뜻이므로 refute가 정답이다. support(지지하다)는 반대되는 의미다.

question:
문장 속 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The feeling of excitement she had was [transient], fading within a day.
explain_ko: transient는 '일시적인, 덧없는'이라는 뜻이므로 temporary가 가장 비슷하다. permanent는 반대되는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
notion
explain_ko: notion은 '개념, 관념'이라는 뜻이다. evidence(증거)와 혼동하지 않도록 한다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Auditors found a _____ between the reported sales and the actual receipts.
explain_ko: 보고된 매출과 실제 영수증 사이의 '차이'가 발견되었다는 문맥이므로 discrepancy가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
possible to do easily or conveniently
explain_ko: '실현 가능한'이라는 뜻이므로 feasible이 정답이다. impossible은 정반대 의미다.

question:
문장 속 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
He remained [dubious] about the salesman's claims despite the guarantee.
explain_ko: dubious는 '의심스러워하는'이라는 뜻이므로 skeptical이 가장 비슷하다. confident는 반대되는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
relinquish
explain_ko: relinquish는 '포기하다, 넘겨주다'라는 뜻이다. obtain(획득하다)과 반대되는 의미다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
New witness testimony helped to _____ the original account of the accident.
explain_ko: 새 증언이 기존 진술을 '뒷받침했다'는 문맥이므로 corroborate가 알맞다. contradict는 반대되는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
to make a problem or bad situation worse
explain_ko: '악화시키다'라는 뜻이므로 exacerbate가 정답이다. relieve(완화하다)는 반대되는 의미다.

question:
문장 속 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
New regulations were introduced to [mitigate] the effects of air pollution.
explain_ko: mitigate는 '완화하다'라는 뜻이므로 ease가 가장 비슷하다. worsen은 반대되는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
culminate
explain_ko: culminate는 '절정에 달하다, 마침내 ~에 이르다'라는 뜻이다. begin(시작되다)과는 다른 의미다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Clean water is _____ for the survival of every living creature.
explain_ko: 모든 생물의 생존에 '필수불가결하다'는 문맥이므로 indispensable이 알맞다. optional은 반대되는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
seeming to be present everywhere at the same time
explain_ko: '어디에나 있는'이라는 뜻이므로 ubiquitous가 정답이다. rare(드문)는 정반대 의미다.

question:
문장 속 [ ] 안의 낱말과 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The theory was supported by [empirical] data collected over ten years.
explain_ko: empirical은 '경험적인, 실증적인'이라는 뜻이므로 observed(관찰된)가 가장 비슷하다. theoretical은 반대되는 뜻이다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
_____ arrives first will get a free drink.
explain_ko: 빈칸은 arrives의 주어이면서 사람을 가리키므로 Whoever. Whomever는 목적격이라 주어 자리에 올 수 없다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: However you are busy, you should call your parents.
You may take whichever seat you prefer.
Whatever you decide, I will support you.
However tired you are, you should brush your teeth before bed.
explain_ko: '아무리 ~해도'의 however는 바로 뒤에 형용사가 와야 하므로 However busy you are가 맞다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
No matter what happens, don't lose hope.
= _____ happens, don't lose hope.
explain_ko: No matter what = Whatever. However는 형용사·부사를 이끌고 Whoever는 사람을 가리켜 뜻이 맞지 않는다.

question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
아무리 열심히 노력해도, 그는 그 상자를 열 수 없었다.
choices: He however tried hard, he couldn't open the box.
Hard however he tried, he couldn't open the box.
However he tried hard, he couldn't open the box.
However hard he tried, he couldn't open the box.
explain_ko: However + 형용사/부사 + 주어 + 동사 순서. hard가 however 바로 뒤에 와야 한다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
Never _____ such a beautiful sunset before.
explain_ko: 부정어 Never가 문장 앞에 오면 조동사 + 주어로 도치한다. did I saw는 조동사 뒤 원형이 아니라 틀리다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: On the hill stands an old church.
Little did I know that he was planning a surprise party.
Not only she is smart, but she is also kind.
I don't like horror movies, and neither does my brother.
explain_ko: Not only가 문장 앞에 오면 도치해 Not only is she smart가 되어야 한다. 장소 부사구 도치·neither 도치는 바르다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
My sister can't swim, and I can't swim either.
= My sister can't swim, and neither _____.
explain_ko: 앞 문장의 조동사가 can이므로 neither + can + 주어. 일반동사가 아니므로 do는 쓰지 않는다.

question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
공원 한가운데에 큰 분수가 있었다.
choices: In the middle of the park a large fountain were.
Was in the middle of the park a large fountain.
In the middle of the park was a fountain large.
In the middle of the park was a large fountain.
explain_ko: 장소 부사구가 앞으로 나가면 동사 + 주어로 도치하고, 주어 a large fountain(단수)에 맞춰 was.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
It was in 2019 _____ my family moved to this city.
explain_ko: It was ~ that 강조 구문으로 부사구 in 2019를 강조한다. which·what은 강조 구문에 쓰지 않는다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: It was Jake that broke the window yesterday.
She did finish the report before the deadline.
It is patience that most beginners lack.
explain_ko: 강조의 do 뒤에는 동사원형이 오므로 does look이 맞다. 나머지 do 강조와 it ~ that 강조는 바르다.

question:
at the station을 강조하여 바꿔 쓸 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Mina met Mr. Park at the station.
= It was at the station _____ Mina met Mr. Park.
explain_ko: 부사구를 강조할 때는 It was ~ that을 쓴다. who는 사람을 강조할 때만 가능하다.

question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
나는 네 도움에 정말로 감사한다.
explain_ko: 강조의 do는 주어 뒤, 동사원형 앞에 둔다. Do I ~는 의문문 어순이다.

question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
My hobbies are reading novels, playing the guitar, and _____ in the mountains.
explain_ko: and로 연결된 앞의 두 요소가 동명사(reading, playing)이므로 hiking으로 맞춘다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: You can either call me or send me a text message.
She likes to swim, to jog, and riding a bike.
The teacher asked us to read the chapter and answer the questions.
He is not only smart but also humble.
explain_ko: to swim, to jog와 병렬이므로 to ride가 되어야 한다. 나머지는 형용사·동사원형끼리 바르게 연결되었다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
He enjoys cooking. He also enjoys baking bread.
= He enjoys both cooking and _____ bread.
explain_ko: both A and B는 같은 형태로 맞추므로 cooking과 병렬인 baking. enjoy는 동명사를 목적어로 취한다.

question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
그 운동은 체력뿐만 아니라 집중력도 향상시킨다.
choices: The exercise not only improves strength but also concentration.
The exercise improves not only strength also but concentration.
The exercise improves strength not only but also concentration.
The exercise improves not only strength but also concentration.
explain_ko: not only 뒤와 but also 뒤에 같은 품사(명사 strength, concentration)가 와야 한다. 둘째 것은 동사와 명사가 짝지어져 병렬이 깨진다.

passage:
Dear Festival Volunteers,
Thank you once again for signing up to help at this year's Willow Bay Lantern Festival, which will take place on Saturday, September 27. We know that many of you have been preparing for weeks, and we truly appreciate the time and energy you have given to make this community event a success. Olivia Grant, Festival Coordinator
question: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 폭풍으로 인해 축제 날짜가 연기되었음을 공지하려고
해안 산책로 복구 작업에 자원봉사를 요청하려고
축제 장소와 자원봉사자 집결 장소가 바뀌었음을 알리려고
explain_ko: 산책로 파손으로 축제를 Central Square 에서 열고 집결 장소도 바뀐다고 알리는 글이다. 날짜와 시작 시각은 그대로라고 했으므로 연기 공지는 틀리다.

passage: Hannah had not wanted to come. Her grandfather had bought two tickets to a jazz concert for her birthday, and she had accepted them only to avoid hurting his feelings. As they took their seats in the small, dimly lit club, she glanced at her phone and calculated how long she would have to sit there before they could leave. The first few minutes seemed to confirm her fears; the music sounded messy, with no clear melody she could follow. Then the saxophone player stepped forward alone. He began with a soft, trembling note that grew slowly into a melody so full of longing that the whole room fell silent. Hannah realized she had put her phone away without noticing. Her eyes were fixed on the stage, and she found herself leaning forward, trying to catch every note. When the song ended, she was the first to start clapping, and she turned to her grandfather with shining eyes.
question: 다음 글에 드러난 Hannah의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
explain_ko: 억지로 와서 시간만 재다가(bored) 색소폰 연주에 빠져 몸을 앞으로 기울이고 가장 먼저 박수를 치므로(fascinated) 지루함 → 매료됨이다.

passage: Helena Varga, an architect born in 1921 in a small village in Hungary, became known for designing schools that used natural light in creative ways. As a young girl, she attended a crowded, dark classroom where students often suffered from headaches, an experience that later shaped her entire career. After studying architecture in Budapest, she moved to Canada in 1950 and worked for a firm that designed government buildings. Frustrated by the firm's focus on cost rather than comfort, she started her own company in 1958. Her schools were famous for large windows facing north, which let in steady light without the heat of direct sunshine, and for classrooms arranged around open courtyards. Varga also insisted that teachers and students be consulted before any design was finalized, a practice that was rare at the time. By the time she retired in 1986, she had designed more than forty schools, several of which are still in use today.
question: Helena Varga에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 설계를 확정하기 전에 교사와 학생의 의견을 들었다.
어린 시절 어둡고 붐비는 교실에서 공부했다.
직사광선을 최대한 들이도록 남쪽으로 큰 창을 낸 학교를 설계했다.
explain_ko: 직사광선의 열 없이 고른 빛이 들도록 북쪽을 향한 큰 창을 냈다고 했으므로, 남쪽 창으로 직사광선을 최대한 들였다는 설명은 틀리다.

passage:
Oakwood Community Garden: Plot Applications for 2027
Would you like to grow your own vegetables and flowers? Oakwood Community Garden is now accepting applications for next year's garden plots.
Plot Information
- Small plot (2 m by 3 m): $40 per year
- Large plot (4 m by 3 m): $70 per year
- Each household may rent only one plot.
Application Period
- January 5 to January 25
- Applications must be submitted online through the Oakwood District website.
Selection
- If there are more applicants than plots, gardeners will be chosen by random drawing on February 1.
- Residents who rented a plot this year and kept it well maintained will be given priority.
Rules
- Chemical pesticides are not allowed anywhere in the garden.
- All gardeners must attend a one-hour orientation session in March.
- Plots that are left unattended for more than four weeks may be given to another applicant.
Garden tools and water are provided free of charge to all gardeners.
question: Oakwood Community Garden 텃밭 신청에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 한 가구가 텃밭을 두 개까지 빌릴 수 있다.
텃밭에서는 화학 살충제를 사용할 수 없다.
농기구와 물은 따로 요금을 내고 사용한다.

passage: News headlines about science often sound remarkably certain. One week, we read that coffee protects the heart; a few months later, another article warns that it increases the risk of heart disease. Readers who follow these stories may conclude that scientists cannot make up their minds, or worse, that science itself cannot be trusted. The real problem, however, lies not in the research but in the way it is reported. Most individual studies produce limited and temporary results, based on a particular group of people under particular conditions, and the researchers themselves usually describe their conclusions with careful limits. When journalists remove these limits to create exciting headlines, they present early findings as final truths. To protect public trust in science, reporters must clearly explain how large a study was, what it could and could not show, and how its results fit with earlier research, rather than hiding the uncertainty that is a natural part of scientific progress.
question: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 독자는 과학 기사보다 전문 학술지를 읽어야 한다.
커피의 건강 효과에 관한 연구를 더 많이 진행해야 한다.
과학자는 연구 결과를 일반 대중에게 직접 발표해야 한다.
과학 기사는 연구 결과의 한계와 불확실성을 함께 전달해야 한다.

passage: We usually assume that having more options makes us happier. After all, a wider selection seems to increase the chance of finding exactly what we want. In reality, however, an abundance of choices can leave us feeling worse. When a shopper faces forty kinds of shampoo or two hundred streaming series, comparing every option becomes exhausting, and many people end up postponing the decision or choosing nothing at all. Even those who do make a choice are often less satisfied with it, because they can easily imagine that one of the many options they rejected might have been better. The more alternatives there are, the stronger this sense of possible regret becomes. For this reason, people who deliberately limit their options, for example by deciding in advance to consider only three products, often feel more content with their decisions than those who search endlessly for the perfect one.
question: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

explain_ko: 선택지가 많으면 비교에 지쳐 결정을 미루고, 골라도 후회가 커져 만족이 줄어든다는 것이 요지이다. 선택지가 많을수록 좋다는 것은 글이 반박하는 통념이다.

passage: When we think about the invention of writing, we often imagine poets recording their songs or kings announcing their victories. The earliest writing systems, however, seem to have developed for far more practical purposes. In ancient Mesopotamia, farmers and temple officials needed a way to keep track of grain, sheep, and other goods that were stored, traded, or paid as taxes. At first, they used small clay tokens of different shapes, each representing a certain item. Over time, they began pressing marks onto clay tablets instead, and these marks gradually became standard symbols for both objects and numbers. Only much later were the same symbols used to record names, laws, and stories. In other words, the ability to write, which we now connect with literature and history, may have grown out of the everyday need to count goods and to remember who owed what to whom.
question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

the methods ancient farmers used to increase grain production
the practical origins of writing in economic record keeping
the role of poetry in the development of ancient languages
explain_ko: 문자가 시나 왕의 기록이 아니라 곡식·가축·세금을 기록하려는 실용적 필요에서 생겼다는 것이 주제이다. 시와 왕은 글이 부정하는 통념으로 나온다.

passage: Scientific journals are filled with reports of successful experiments, but they reveal only a small part of how science actually works. Behind every published discovery lie countless attempts that produced nothing useful: chemical reactions that failed to occur, instruments that gave meaningless readings, and hypotheses that turned out to be completely wrong. It is tempting to regard these results as wasted effort, and many researchers quietly throw them away. Yet failures often contain valuable information. An experiment that does not work as expected can reveal a hidden flaw in an accepted theory or point toward something no one had considered. Moreover, when failed results are not shared, other scientists may spend years repeating the same unsuccessful approach. For these reasons, some scientists are now calling for journals and databases that publish negative results, arguing that knowing what does not work is just as important as knowing what does.
question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

How to Design an Experiment That Always Succeeds

explain_ko: 실패한 실험도 귀중한 정보를 담고 있어 공유되어야 한다는 내용이므로 '과학에는 실패도 필요하다'가 알맞다. 우연한 발견 이야기는 나오지 않는다.

passage: Most metals, once bent, stay bent until someone forces them back into shape. A group of materials known as shape-memory alloys, however, behaves in a surprising way. ① An alloy of nickel and titanium, for example, can be twisted into almost any form when it is cool, yet it returns to its original shape once it is warmed. ② Gold has been prized for jewelry for thousands of years because it never rusts and can be hammered into extremely thin sheets. ③ This unusual ability comes from the way the metal's atoms rearrange themselves when the temperature changes, as if they remember their earlier structure. ④ Engineers now use this property in eyeglass frames that spring back after being sat on and in tiny medical tubes that open up inside blood vessels. Such metals show that the value of a material can depend as much on how it changes as on how strong it is.

passage:
Imagine a lake shared by the fishermen of a small village, where the fish population can remain stable only if the total catch stays below a certain level.

(A) This situation, in which individuals acting in their own interest destroy a shared resource, is often called the tragedy of the commons. It explains why problems such as overfishing and air pollution usually require rules or agreements that limit the behavior of everyone involved.

(B) However, every other fisherman follows the same logic, and soon the total catch far exceeds what the lake can support. Within a few years, the fish population collapses, and the entire village loses its main source of income.

(C) Each fisherman knows this, but he also realizes that if he catches a few extra fish, he alone will enjoy the profit, while the damage to the lake will be shared by everyone. From his individual point of view, taking more seems perfectly reasonable.

passage: For centuries, many European painters worked with tempera, a paint made by mixing colored powder with egg yolk and a little water. ( ① ) Tempera produced bright, long-lasting colors, and some works painted with it still look fresh after more than five hundred years. ( ② ) However, it had one major drawback: it dried within minutes. ( ③ ) Because of this, artists had to apply it in short strokes and could not easily blend one color into another, which is why tempera paintings often have sharp outlines and flat areas of color. Painters also had to work quickly and plan every part of the picture carefully in advance. ( ④ ) This gave artists the freedom to create soft shadows, glowing skin, and the gradual changes of light that we see in nature. As a result, during the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, more and more artists switched to oil, and it eventually became the standard material of European painting. Many of the most admired portraits in history owe their soft, lifelike quality to this change in materials.

passage: Few animals change their surroundings as dramatically as the beaver. By cutting down trees and piling branches and mud across streams, beavers build dams that turn fast-flowing water into quiet ponds. ① Beaver fur was once so valuable in Europe that hats made from it were considered a symbol of wealth and fashion. ② These ponds slow the flow of water, allowing soil and sand to settle and creating wetlands that support a wide variety of plants, insects, fish, and birds. ③ During dry seasons, the water stored behind the dams keeps the surrounding land moist, reducing the risk of wildfires and providing drinking water for other animals. ④ The wetlands also act like giant sponges, absorbing heavy rain and reducing the danger of floods downstream. Because of these benefits, some regions that once treated beavers as pests are now bringing them back to restore damaged landscapes.

passage: Organizations love numbers because numbers seem objective and easy to compare. A hospital might track how quickly patients are seen, and a school might track its average test scores. These measurements can be useful, but problems arise when the numbers themselves become the goal. Suppose a hospital rewards its staff for reducing waiting times. Soon, nurses may begin recording patients as seen the moment they arrive, even if no doctor has examined them yet. Similarly, a school judged only by test scores may spend months drilling students on exam questions while cutting art, music, and discussion. In both cases, the figures improve while the real situation stays the same or even gets worse. Such organizations are, in effect, [polishing the thermometer instead of treating the fever]. A wise leader remembers that a measurement is only a signal of what truly matters, never a substitute for it.

passage: In medical research, new drugs are usually tested by comparing them with a placebo, a pill that looks identical but contains no active ingredient. Surprisingly, a significant number of patients who receive the placebo report real improvements in their symptoms, such as reduced pain or better sleep. Brain scans have shown that this is not simply imagination; in some cases, the brain actually releases natural painkilling chemicals after a person takes a sugar pill. Even the appearance of the treatment matters. Larger pills tend to work better than smaller ones, two pills often work better than one, and an injection generally has a stronger effect than a pill. None of these differences can be explained by the contents of the treatment, since the contents are the same. What changes is how strongly the patient believes the treatment will help. These findings show that the body's response to medicine depends partly on the patient's _____.

passage: Most smartphones now suggest the next word as we type, and many people accept these suggestions to save time. Researchers who study writing have begun to ask whether this convenience changes what we actually say. In one set of experiments, participants wrote short descriptions of photographs, sometimes with a keyboard that offered suggestions and sometimes without one. When suggestions were available, people wrote more quickly, but their descriptions became shorter and relied more heavily on common, predictable words. A person who might have described a meal as "a steaming bowl of spicy noodles" was more likely to write "a good lunch," simply because the keyboard proposed "good" first. Since the suggestions are based on what millions of other users have typed, accepting them again and again may gradually pull individual writing toward the same familiar expressions. The tool, in other words, does not only record our thoughts; it quietly shapes them.

passage: M: Hello, listeners. Welcome back to Study Smart. Many students believe that reading their notes again and again is the best way to prepare for exams. However, rereading often gives you a false feeling that you know the material well. A more effective way is to explain what you've learned to someone else. When you try to teach a topic, you quickly find the parts you don't really understand. You also have to organize the ideas in your own words, which helps you remember them longer. You don't even need a real student. You can explain the lesson to a friend, a family member, or even your pet. So before your next exam, try teaching instead of just reading.
question: 다음을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 시험 전에는 노트를 반복해서 읽어야 한다.
배운 내용을 남에게 설명하는 것이 효과적인 학습 방법이다.
학습 내용은 짧게 나누어 자주 복습해야 한다.
explain_ko: 노트를 다시 읽는 것보다 남에게 가르치듯 설명하는 것이 더 효과적이라는 요지. 반복해서 읽기는 오히려 착각을 준다고 함.

passage:
M: Hi, Amelia. I heard you're moving next month.
W: Yes. I found a new apartment near the university.
M: Why? Is your apartment too small? You have so many books.
W: Not really. It actually has plenty of space.
M: Then is the rent too high?
W: No, it's quite cheap for this area. That's why I've stayed there so long.
M: Hmm, is it because of your noisy neighbor? You told me about the man upstairs.
W: Well, he's still a bit loud, but that's not why. The problem is getting to school. My classes start at eight this semester, and it takes me an hour and a half by bus.
M: That's tiring. Is the new place close?
W: It's a ten-minute walk to my classroom. I'll finally get more sleep.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 이사하려는 이유로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 8시 수업에 버스로 한 시간 반이 걸려서 학교 가까이로 이사한다고 함. 위층 이웃이 조금 시끄럽긴 하지만 그것 때문은 아니라고 분명히 말함.

passage:
M: Olivia, you look nervous. Is something wrong?
W: I have a job interview tomorrow at the bookstore downtown. It's my first interview ever.
M: That's exciting! What kind of job is it?
W: A weekend job at the information desk. I'd help customers find books.
M: You'll be great at that. You read more than anyone I know.
W: Thanks. But I have no idea what they'll ask me.
M: They'll probably ask why you want the job and what kinds of books you like. Think about your answers tonight.
W: Good idea. Oh, and what should I wear? I don't want to look too casual.
M: A clean shirt and pants would be fine. Actually, my sister worked at that bookstore last year. Do you want me to ask her what the interview was like?
question:
대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 대한 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Woman: _____
choices: No thanks. I already got the job last week.
Sorry, but I don't like reading books.
That would be great. Please ask her tonight.
Right. I'll wear my favorite T-shirt.
explain_ko: 그 서점에서 일했던 누나에게 면접이 어땠는지 물어봐 줄까 하는 제안에 좋다며 부탁하는 응답이 자연스러움. 면접은 내일이므로 이미 일자리를 얻었다는 말은 맞지 않음.

passage:
W: Excuse me. Are you the new resident in apartment three oh two?
M: Yes, I moved in last week. I'm Ryan. Nice to meet you.
W: Nice to meet you, too. I'm Linda from next door. I noticed you put your recycling out on Tuesday.
M: Yes. Is that a problem?
W: In our building, recycling is collected only on Thursday mornings. If you put it out early, the wind blows paper and plastic all over the parking lot.
M: Oh, I'm so sorry. I didn't know that. Nobody told me.
W: That's okay. Many new residents make the same mistake. Also, you need to separate glass bottles from plastic ones.
M: I see. Is there a guide somewhere with all the rules?
W: Yes, there's one posted next to the elevator on the first floor.
question:
대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 대한 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Man: _____
choices: Sorry, but I don't live in this building.
Thanks. I'll read it carefully on my way out.
Don't worry. I'll put my recycling out every Tuesday.
Great. I'll take the stairs instead of the elevator.
explain_ko: 1층 엘리베이터 옆에 안내문이 있다는 말에 나가는 길에 읽겠다는 응답이 자연스러움. 수거일은 목요일이므로 화요일마다 내놓겠다는 말은 틀림.

passage:
M: Ms. Clark, do you have a minute? I have an idea for our art club.
W: Of course, Leo. What is it?
M: The wall next to the school cafeteria looks old and gray. I think our club could paint a mural on it.
W: That's a wonderful idea. What would you like to paint?
M: We're thinking of a design that shows students from different countries working together.
W: I like the message. But painting on a school wall needs permission from the principal.
M: I thought so. What should we do to get it?
W: First, you should draw a sketch of the design and write a short plan, including the budget and the schedule.
M: Okay. Could you look over our plan before we show it to the principal?
question:
대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 대한 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Woman: _____
choices: Sorry, I'm not good at drawing people.
Great. The principal already painted the wall.
No, you don't need permission for that.
Sure. Bring it to my office when it's ready.
explain_ko: 교장에게 보이기 전에 계획서를 봐 달라는 부탁에 준비되면 교무실로 가져오라는 응답이 자연스러움. 허락이 필요하다고 앞에서 말했으므로 필요 없다는 말은 모순.

passage:
W: Welcome to the ticket office. How may I help you?
M: Hi. My train to Boston at two o'clock was just canceled. What should I do?
W: I'm sorry. Because of the heavy snow, several trains have been canceled this afternoon.
M: I have to be there by tonight. My sister's wedding is tomorrow morning.
W: I understand. The next available train leaves at five thirty, and there are a few seats left.
M: Five thirty? That's a long wait, but I guess I have no choice.
W: Since your train was canceled, you can change your ticket for free. You'll also get a meal coupon for the station restaurant.
M: That's helpful. Can I get a window seat?
W: Let me check. Yes, there's one window seat left in car number seven. Shall I book it for you?
question:
대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 대한 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Man: _____
choices: Yes, please. I'll take that seat.
Great. I'll take the two o'clock train then.
No, thanks. I've already had dinner at home.
Sorry, but my sister's wedding was yesterday.
explain_ko: 창가 자리를 예약해 줄지 묻는 말에 그 자리로 하겠다는 응답이 자연스러움. 2시 기차는 취소되었고, 결혼식은 내일임.

passage: W: Chris is the leader of a group project in his economics class. His group has to research how small businesses in their town are using social media. For the past two weeks, one member, Julia, has been working very hard. She has interviewed five shop owners and collected much more information than anyone else. However, the other members have been giving her most of the tasks because she always finishes them quickly. Chris notices that Julia looks exhausted and has fallen behind in her other classes. He thinks the work should be shared more fairly. So he wants to suggest to the group that they divide the remaining tasks equally. In this situation, what would Chris most likely say to the group members?
question:
다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Chris가 모둠원들에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Chris: _____
choices: I think we should change our research topic.
Julia, could you interview a few more shop owners?
Why don't we ask the teacher for more time?
Let's divide the rest of the work equally among all of us.
explain_ko: Chris는 Julia에게 몰린 일을 나누어 남은 일을 똑같이 분담하자고 제안하려 함. Julia에게 인터뷰를 더 부탁하는 것은 정반대.

passage: M: Grace works as a guide at a history museum. Today, she is leading a group of visitors through a room full of old paintings and ancient documents. These items can be damaged by strong light, so the museum allows visitors to take photos only without using the flash. While Grace is explaining a painting, she notices that one visitor, Mr. Evans, keeps taking pictures with his camera's flash on. He seems very excited and doesn't know about the rule. Grace doesn't want to embarrass him in front of the others, but she needs to protect the artworks. So she wants to politely ask him to turn off the flash. In this situation, what would Grace most likely say to Mr. Evans?
question:
다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Grace가 Mr. Evans에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Grace: _____
choices: You can buy postcards of this painting at the gift shop.
Sorry, but taking pictures is not allowed at all here.
Excuse me, but could you please turn off your camera's flash?
Would you like me to take a picture of you?
explain_ko: Grace는 플래시만 꺼 달라고 정중히 부탁하려 함. 이 박물관은 플래시 없는 사진 촬영은 허용하므로 사진 촬영 전면 금지라는 말은 틀림.

passage: W: Good morning, students. Have you ever gone to a supermarket to buy just milk and come home with a full bag? That's not always an accident. Today, we'll look at how stores are designed to encourage shoppers to spend more. First, basic items like milk and eggs are usually placed at the back of the store. To reach them, you have to walk past many other products. Second, expensive brands are often put at eye level, while cheaper ones are on the lower shelves. Also, stores often play slow music, which makes shoppers walk more slowly and look around longer. Finally, candy and snacks are placed near the checkout, where people wait in line. Keep these tricks in mind the next time you go shopping.
question: 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: the importance of making a shopping list
store strategies that lead customers to buy more
reasons why food prices keep rising
explain_ko: 필수품을 안쪽에, 비싼 상품을 눈높이에, 느린 음악, 계산대 옆 간식 등 더 사게 만드는 매장 전략을 설명함. 음악은 예시 하나일 뿐.

passage: M: Hello, class. Today, I'd like to talk about how people made colors before modern paints were invented. In the past, artists had to create colors from natural materials. For example, a deep blue color came from a stone that was ground into fine powder. Because the stone was rare, this blue paint was once more expensive than gold. Red colors were often made from tiny insects that lived on cactus plants. People dried the insects and crushed them to get a bright red. For yellow, some artists used saffron, a flower that also adds flavor to food. And black was usually made from burned wood or bones. These natural colors show how creative people were in the past. Next time, we'll try making our own paint.
question: 다음을 듣고, 물감의 재료로 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
explain_ko: 파란색은 돌, 빨간색은 곤충, 노란색은 꽃(사프란), 검은색은 태운 나무나 뼈로 만들었다고 했고 조개껍데기(shells)는 나오지 않음.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
deprive
explain_ko: deprive는 'deprive A of B' 형태로 'A에게서 B를 빼앗다'라는 뜻이다. supply(공급하다)는 반대에 가깝다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
My grandmother says she can no longer _____ the noise from the construction site next door.
explain_ko: 문맥상 '참다, 견디다'라는 뜻의 tolerate가 알맞다. 나머지는 소음과 어울리지 않는 동사이다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
showing strong dislike or opposition toward someone or something
explain_ko: 적대감을 드러낸다는 뜻의 hostile에 대한 풀이이다. 나머지는 호기심, 관대함, 유창함과 관련된 낱말이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [diminish] 와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The pain began to diminish soon after she took the medicine.
explain_ko: diminish는 '줄어들다, 약해지다'라는 뜻이므로 decrease가 가장 가깝다. intensify(강해지다)는 반대말이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
The professor asked the students to write a more _____ essay, with each paragraph clearly connected to the next.
explain_ko: 문단들이 논리적으로 연결된 글을 요구하므로 '일관성 있는'을 뜻하는 coherent가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
having many small parts or details arranged in a complicated way
explain_ko: 작은 부분과 세부가 복잡하게 얽혀 있다는 뜻의 intricate(복잡한, 정교한)에 대한 풀이이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [retrieve] 와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The diver managed to retrieve the lost ring from the bottom of the pool.
explain_ko: retrieve는 '되찾다, 회수하다'라는 뜻이므로 recover가 가장 가깝다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
discard
explain_ko: discard는 필요 없는 것을 '버리다'라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
very easy to see or notice because it stands out from its surroundings
explain_ko: 주변에서 두드러져 눈에 잘 띈다는 뜻의 conspicuous에 대한 풀이이다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [deliberate] 와 뜻이 가장 비슷한 것은?
The referee said the foul was a deliberate attempt to hurt the other player.
explain_ko: deliberate는 '고의적인, 의도적인'이라는 뜻이므로 intentional이 가장 가깝다. accidental(우연한)은 반대말이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
scrutinize
explain_ko: scrutinize는 '면밀히 조사하다, 자세히 살피다'라는 뜻이다. 대충 훑어보는 것(skim)과 반대다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
Smartphone addiction has become increasingly _____ among teenagers in recent years.
explain_ko: 최근 청소년 사이에 스마트폰 중독이 점점 '널리 퍼졌다'는 뜻이므로 prevalent가 알맞다.

question:
다음 문장에서 [audacious] 와 뜻이 가장 반대되는 것은?
It was an audacious plan to cross the frozen lake at night.
explain_ko: audacious는 '대담한'이라는 뜻이므로 반대말은 '소심한'을 뜻하는 timid이다.

question:
다음 영어 낱말의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
circumvent
explain_ko: circumvent는 규칙이나 문제를 정면으로 부딪치지 않고 '피해 가다, 우회하다'라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
After losing his main client, the freelancer found himself in a _____ financial situation.
explain_ko: 불안정한 재정 상태를 나타내므로 '불안정한, 위태로운'이라는 뜻의 precarious가 알맞다.

question:
다음 영어 풀이에 해당하는 낱말은?
equivalent in effect to something, especially something bad (usually followed by 'to')
explain_ko: tantamount는 'tantamount to'의 형태로 '~와 마찬가지인'이라는 뜻이다.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
About two-thirds of the students in our school _____ to school by bus every morning.
explain_ko: 부분 표현(two-thirds of) 뒤 명사 students 가 복수이므로 동사도 복수 come. comes 는 two-thirds 를 단수로 본 오답.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Half of the pizza was eaten before the guests arrived.
The number of electric cars on the roads have increased sharply.
Most of the information in this report is out of date.
A number of volunteers were waiting outside the gym.
explain_ko: the number of + 복수명사는 '~의 수'로 단수 취급하므로 has increased 가 맞다. a number of 는 복수, most/half of 는 뒤 명사(information, pizza)에 맞춰 단수.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
There are fewer bees in the valley than there were ten years ago.
= The number of bees in the valley _____ over the last ten years.
explain_ko: 주어 The number 는 단수이고 decrease 는 자동사이므로 has decreased. have 는 bees 에 끌린 수일치 오류, has been decreased 는 자동사를 수동태로 쓴 오답.

question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
우리 반 학생의 절반 이상이 그 영화를 이미 봤다.
choices: More than half of the students in our class have already seen the movie.
More than the half of students in our class have already seen the movie.
Half more than of the students in our class have already seen the movie.
More than half of the students in our class have seen already the movie.
explain_ko: '절반 이상'은 more than half of the + 명사 순서이고 already 는 have 와 p.p. 사이. the half of students, seen already the movie 는 어순 오류.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
The old stone bridge is said _____ more than two hundred years ago.
explain_ko: 다리가 '지어진' 수동이고, 말하는 시점(현재)보다 이전 일이므로 완료 수동 부정사 to have been built. to be built 는 시제, to have built 는 태가 틀림.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: The meeting was put off until next Friday.
The little boy was brought up by his grandparents in a small village.
The injured player was taken care by the team doctor.
The singer is believed to be preparing a new album.
explain_ko: 동사구 take care of 를 수동태로 바꿔도 of 를 그대로 둬야 한다(was taken care of by). put off, bring up, be believed to 는 모두 바르다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
People say that the lake contains a rare kind of fish.
= The lake _____ a rare kind of fish.
explain_ko: say 와 contains 가 같은 현재 시점이므로 is said to contain. to have contained 는 이전 시점일 때 쓰는 형태, says to contain 은 수동이 빠진 오답.

question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
그 오래된 규칙은 곧 폐지될 것이다.
choices: The old rule will soon be done with away.
The old rule will be done away soon with.
The old rule will soon be away done with.
The old rule will soon be done away with.
explain_ko: 동사구 do away with(폐지하다)는 수동태에서도 done away with 로 한 덩어리로 둔다. 다른 선택지는 동사구를 쪼개거나 순서를 바꾼 오류.

question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Children today spend far more time on screens than their parents _____ at their age.
explain_ko: 앞의 일반동사 spend 를 받는 대동사가 필요하고, 부모가 그 나이였던 과거이며 주어가 복수이므로 did. were/was 는 be동사라 spend 를 대신할 수 없다.

question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Tom can swim faster than I can.
When asked about the accident, the driver said nothing.
My brother likes spicy food much more than I am.
Though small, the room was very comfortable.
explain_ko: 일반동사 likes 를 대신하는 대동사는 do 이므로 than I do 가 맞다. 부사절 생략(When asked, Though small)과 조동사 대동사(I can)는 바르다.

question:
두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
While she was walking along the beach, she found a strange shell.
= While _____ along the beach, she found a strange shell.
explain_ko: 부사절 주어가 주절 주어와 같으면 '주어+be동사'를 생략할 수 있어 While walking. she walking 은 주어만 남긴 오류, walked 는 능동 진행의 뜻을 잃는다.

question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
원한다면 내 자전거를 써도 돼.
choices: You can use my bike if you want to.
You can use my bike to if you want.
You can use to my bike if you want.
If you want you can use to my bike.

question:

passage:
Dear Mr. Collins,
I am the owner of Brookside Farm, which your students have visited every spring for the past five years as part of their science program. My family has always enjoyed welcoming them, and we are glad that so many young people are curious about where their food comes from. During last Thursday's visit, however, a small group of students left the gate to our sheep pasture open while exploring the farm on their own. Seven sheep wandered onto the road, and it took my son and me nearly three hours to bring them back safely. Fortunately, no one was hurt, but a passing car had to stop suddenly to avoid them. I do not wish to end these visits, which I believe are valuable for both the children and our farm. I would simply ask that, before your next group arrives, the teachers review our basic farm rules with the students, especially the rule that every gate must be closed immediately after passing through it.
Sincerely,
Walter Greene

passage: Leah had spent three weekends building her bridge for the regional engineering fair, and she was sure that no one else's design could match it. Instead of copying the simple triangles that most students used, she had glued hundreds of thin wooden sticks into a graceful arch that curved over the gap like the stone bridges in her travel books. When her turn came, she placed the model on the testing stand and smiled at the judges as they began hanging weights from its center. Two kilograms, then four, then six: the arch held without a sound, and a few students behind her whispered in admiration. At seven kilograms, however, she heard a faint crack. Before she could say anything, one side of the arch twisted sideways, and the whole structure folded onto the table in a pile of broken sticks. The judge wrote down the number and thanked her politely. Leah stared at the pieces with a burning face, realizing that a design could look beautiful and still fail to carry the load it had been built for.

passage: In the sixteenth century, a large deposit of an unusually pure, dark mineral was discovered in the hills of northern England. Local shepherds soon found that it left a clear gray mark, and they began using it to mark their sheep. Because the substance looked and felt like lead, people called it by that name, although it actually contained no lead at all; it was a form of carbon now known as graphite. At first, writers simply wrapped sticks of graphite in string or sheepskin to keep their fingers clean, and later craftsmen began to place the sticks inside hollow pieces of wood. For many years, England controlled the best supply and guarded the mine closely. In the late eighteenth century, war cut France off from this source. A French engineer then found a clever solution: he ground lower-quality graphite into powder, mixed it with clay, and baked the mixture in an oven. By changing the amount of clay, he could make pencils harder or softer, a method that manufacturers around the world still follow today.

passage: When a city decides to build a new park, library, or bus route, officials often hold a public meeting only after the plans are nearly complete. At that stage, residents are shown detailed drawings and asked for their opinions, but everyone in the room knows that major changes are no longer possible. Not surprisingly, such meetings frequently turn into angry debates, and people leave feeling that their voices did not matter. This pattern wastes time and damages trust between citizens and local government. A better approach is to invite residents into the process from the very beginning, when the basic questions are still open. What problems does the neighborhood actually face? Who will use the new space, and at what times of day? Local people often know things that experts cannot find in data, such as which streets feel unsafe at night or where elderly residents usually gather. When planners listen to this knowledge early, they design projects that fit real needs, and residents are far more likely to support the results.

passage: Over the past few decades, many playgrounds have been redesigned to remove almost every possible danger. Tall slides have been lowered, climbing frames shortened, and hard ground covered with soft rubber. These changes were made with good intentions, and they have prevented some serious injuries. Yet researchers who study children's development warn that playgrounds can become too safe. When children climb a little higher than they did last week or balance on a narrow log, they learn to judge their own abilities and to handle the fear that comes with a small risk. These experiences build confidence and the kind of careful judgment that protects them later in life. Children who never face any risk in play may either become overly fearful or, when they finally meet real danger, lack the experience to recognize it. The goal, then, should not be to remove all risk but to separate hidden hazards, such as broken equipment, from challenges that children can see and choose to take on.

passage: Spider silk is one of the most remarkable materials in nature. Weight for weight, some types of spider silk are stronger than steel, yet they can also stretch a great deal before breaking, which allows a web to catch a fast-flying insect without tearing. Scientists have long dreamed of producing this material in large quantities for medical threads, lightweight ropes, or protective clothing. The obvious solution, farming spiders the way we farm silkworms, does not work, because spiders are solitary hunters that attack and eat one another when kept together. Researchers have therefore tried a different route. They have inserted the genes that spiders use to make silk proteins into bacteria, yeast, and even goats, whose milk then contains the proteins. The next challenge is spinning these proteins into fibers, since a spider does not simply squeeze out liquid silk but carefully controls the chemistry and pressure inside its body as the thread forms. Progress has been slow, but several companies now produce small amounts of artificial silk.

passage: Visitors to old European churches are sometimes told a fascinating story. The window panes, the guide explains, are thicker at the bottom than at the top because glass is actually a very slow liquid that has been flowing downward for centuries. The story is memorable, but it does not hold up. Scientists have calculated that at room temperature, glass is so stiff that any flow would be far too slow to notice, even over billions of years. Moreover, glass objects from ancient Rome, which are much older than any church window, show no sign of sagging. The real explanation lies in how windows used to be made. Early glassmakers spun melted glass into a large, flat disk, and the sheets cut from it were never perfectly even. When workers fitted these panes, they usually placed the heavier, thicker edge at the bottom for stability. In some old windows, in fact, the thick edge was installed at the top or the side, which a flowing liquid could never explain.

passage: In a few mountainous regions of the world, people have developed a remarkable way of communicating across deep valleys: they whistle their language. ① These whistles are not a simple code of signals; they copy the melody and rhythm of spoken words, so a skilled listener can follow whole sentences. ② Because a strong whistle can travel several kilometers, much farther than a shout, shepherds and farmers once used it to share news or call for help without walking for hours over rough ground. ③ Many songbirds learn their songs by listening to adults during a short period early in life, and young birds raised alone often sing poorly. ④ Today, however, mobile phones and new roads have made whistling less necessary, and in several villages only a handful of elderly speakers still use it fluently. To keep the tradition alive, some local schools have begun teaching whistled speech to children as part of their regular lessons. They treat it as a valuable piece of cultural heritage.

passage:
For centuries, sailors crossing the open ocean had no landmarks to tell them how far they had traveled, yet knowing the ship's speed was essential for estimating its position and avoiding dangerous waters.

(A) That number told them how fast the ship was moving. This is why, even today, long after the rope and the sandglass have disappeared from ships, the speed of ships and aircraft is still measured in a unit called the knot.

(B) Their solution was surprisingly simple. A flat piece of wood tied to a long rope was thrown into the water from the back of the ship. Since the wood stayed almost still in the water, the rope was pulled out as the ship moved forward.

(C) Knots were tied in this rope at equal distances. While one sailor let the rope run out, another turned over a small sandglass, and when the sand ran out, they counted how many knots had passed through their hands.

passage: Many athletes believe that the best way to master a skill is to repeat exactly the same movement again and again. Coaches often design practice sessions around this idea, asking players to shoot from one spot hundreds of times. ( ① ) Research on motor learning, however, suggests that a certain amount of variety leads to better results. In one study, a group of young basketball players practiced free throws only from the standard line, while another group practiced from several distances, both closer and farther away. Later, both groups were tested from the standard line. ( ② ) Scientists think that varied practice forces the brain to understand the general rules of a movement, such as how force and angle relate to distance, instead of memorizing one fixed pattern. ( ③ ) As a result, the skill becomes more flexible and holds up better under the changing conditions of a real game. ( ④ ) This is why many coaches now mix drills of different distances and speeds into their training.

passage:
Noise-cancelling headphones seem almost magical: you put them on in a noisy airplane, and the roar of the engines suddenly fades into the background while your music remains perfectly clear.

(A) If the high point of one wave meets the low point of another wave of the same size, the two cancel each other out, and the result is silence. Tiny microphones on the headphones take advantage of this by constantly listening to the noise around you.

(B) A small computer chip then creates an opposite wave and plays it through the speakers together with your music. Because this system works best on steady, low sounds, it removes engine noise well but is less effective against sudden sounds like a baby's cry.

(C) The trick behind them depends on the fact that sound is a wave, a pattern of air pressure that rises and falls in a regular rhythm. When two sound waves meet in the same place, they combine with each other.

passage: Many students today spend hours designing the perfect study planner. They choose colored pens for each subject, draw neat boxes for every hour of the day, and watch online videos comparing different note-taking systems. There is nothing wrong with wanting to be organized, and a clear plan can certainly make studying easier. The problem begins when the preparation becomes the main activity. A student may finish an evening feeling productive because the planner looks beautiful, yet realize that not a single math problem has been solved. Organizing gives us a pleasant sense of progress without the discomfort of actually struggling with difficult material, which is exactly why it is so tempting. A telescope is valuable only because of the stars it lets us see, and a planner is valuable only because of the learning it supports. When we forget this, we end up [polishing the lens instead of looking through it]. The simplest system that gets us to the real work quickly is usually the best one.

passage: To a spectator, the rider at the front of a cycling race may appear to be in the strongest position. In reality, leading is often the hardest and least rewarding job on the road. At racing speeds, most of a cyclist's effort goes into pushing air out of the way rather than into overcoming the friction of the tires. A rider who stays close behind another cyclist travels in a pocket of calmer air and may use about a third less energy while moving at exactly the same speed. This is why racers form long lines and why teammates take turns at the front, each one sheltering the others for a while before dropping back to rest. It also explains a common strategy: a team protects its best rider in the middle of the group for most of the race, saving that rider's strength for a final burst in the last few hundred meters. For much of a race, therefore, the smartest place to be is _____.

passage: Beginning painters often feel that every part of the canvas must be filled with color and detail. Experienced artists, however, know that _____ can be just as important as what is shown. In traditional East Asian ink painting, for example, large areas of paper are deliberately left blank. A few strokes suggest a mountain, and the empty space around it becomes mist, sky, or distance in the viewer's imagination. The same principle appears in design and photography, where empty areas around a subject guide the eye and give the image room to breathe. A crowded picture forces the viewer to process everything at once, and nothing stands out. By contrast, an image with carefully chosen empty space invites the viewer to take part in completing it, which makes the experience more personal and memorable. Music follows a similar logic: the short silences between notes shape the rhythm and give meaning to the sounds around them. In each case, restraint allows the essential elements to speak more clearly.

passage: For much of the last century, farmers in many regions removed the hedges and strips of wild plants that once separated their fields. Larger, uninterrupted fields were easier to plow with big machines, and every meter of land could be used for crops. Over time, however, some farmers noticed that pest problems were growing worse, forcing them to spend more money on chemical sprays. Researchers who studied the situation found that the hedges had been home to beetles, spiders, and small birds that feed on crop-eating insects. When the hedges disappeared, these natural predators lost their shelter, and pest populations could grow unchecked. In recent years, several farms have experimented with planting strips of flowers and shrubs along the edges of their fields. Although this reduces the area available for crops slightly, the farms have recorded fewer pest outbreaks and have been able to cut their use of chemicals. In some cases, the overall harvest has even increased, since bees attracted by the flowers also improve pollination.
question:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Removing hedges from farmland seemed (A) _____, but it destroyed the homes of natural pest controllers; restoring such plant strips, though it takes up some land, can (B) _____ farming.

W: Great. Then please deliver them to the school. Here's my card.
question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.

passage:

W: I guess that's true. When I type, I just copy everything the teacher says.
M: Exactly. Writing by hand makes your brain work harder, so you remember the information better.
W: Maybe that's why I forget most of what I type.
M: Give it a try for a few weeks and see if your test scores improve.
W: Okay, I will.

passage: M: Hello, listeners. Welcome back to Healthy Habits. Many of you feel sleepy in the early afternoon, especially after lunch. Some people try to fight this feeling by drinking coffee or energy drinks. But today I'd like to suggest a better solution: a short nap. Research shows that sleeping for just ten to twenty minutes can improve your mood and your ability to focus. The key is to keep it short. If you sleep for more than thirty minutes, you may fall into deep sleep and wake up feeling even more tired. Also, try to nap before three in the afternoon, so it won't disturb your sleep at night. So the next time you feel tired after lunch, put down that coffee and close your eyes for a few minutes.

passage: W: Hello, students. Last time, we talked about how animals hide from their enemies. Today, let's look at the opposite strategy. Some animals use bright colors to warn predators to stay away. Their red bodies with black spots signal that they taste terrible. Bees and wasps also have yellow and black stripes that warn other animals about their painful stings. Interestingly, some harmless animals copy these warning colors. For instance, certain flies look almost exactly like bees, so predators avoid them, too. Now, let's watch a short video that shows these animals in the wild.

why some insects are harmful to humans
ways animals hide from their enemies

passage: M: Good afternoon, everyone. Many people stop exercising as they get older because their knees or backs start to hurt. But giving up exercise completely is not the answer. It improves your balance and makes your body more flexible. Finally, rowing works almost every muscle in your body while keeping your joints safe. Remember, whichever sport you choose, start slowly and increase the intensity step by step.
